# Test plan - Ibex core, opentitan configuration

Deliverable 2 (DV_prompt.txt Section 11): feature -> test-plan items -> tests -> bins. Owner: dv-lead.
Version 2 (after the Critic's advisory pre-review gen_critic_fcov_drafts_prereview_v1.md was folded in: checker direction per gen_bug_log.md, rvfi_trap-on-ebreak-into-debug rule, vacuity fixes, impossible bins pruned, layer-1 weight tables, timing qualifiers), generated 2026-09-03 07:56 UTC from dv/auto_dv/work/dv-lead/parts6/tp_*.md. Companion documents:
dv/auto_dv/docs/gen_feature_list.md (features), gen_fcov_plan.md (bins), gen_bug_log.md (B/D lists),
gen_trace_feature_tp.csv and gen_trace_tp_bin.csv (machine-readable traceability), checked by
dv/auto_dv/tools/gen_trace_check.py.

Build configuration: `opentitan` (ibex_configs.yaml): BaseIsa=RV32IorCHERIoT (CHERIoT mode excluded
by owner ruling), RV32E=0, RV32M=RV32MSingleCycle, RV32B=RV32BOTEarlGrey, RV32ZC=RV32ZcaZcbZcmp,
RegFile=RegFileFF, BranchTargetALU=1, WritebackStage=1, ICache=1, ICacheECC=1, ICacheScramble=1,
BranchPredictor=0, DbgTriggerEn=1, SecureIbex=1, PMPEnable=1, PMPGranularity=0, PMPNumRegions=16,
MHPMCounterNum=10, MHPMCounterWidth=32.

DUT: `gen_dut_top` = `ibex_core` + `ibex_register_file_ff` (DV_prompt.txt Section 2 rulings); `ibex_top`
is not the DUT. Wrapper parameters (owner question Q-002 defaults, pending confirmation): MemECC=1
(39-bit bus data), DummyInstructions=1, ICacheTweakInfection=1, ResetAll=1, RegFileECC=0
(RegFileDataWidth=32), DbgHwBreakNum=1, DmBaseAddr=0x1A110000, DmAddrMask=0xFFF,
DmHaltAddr=0x1A110800, DmExceptionAddr=0x1A110808, CsrMvendorId=CsrMimpId=0, PMP reset values from
ibex_pkg; compiled with +define+RVFI; cheriot_enable_i tied IbexMuBiOff inside the wrapper.

# 0. Conventions

- Item ID `TP-<AREA>-<nnn>`, stable. Fields: Features (F-IDs; ALIAS/FOLDED IDs resolve to their
  canonical feature) / Phase (1 = feature-targeted test, 2 = random-regime item) / Tier (smoke,
  targeted, full) / Preconditions (programmable state the program sets first) / Stimulus / Randomized /
  Knobs (regime knobs, defined in gen_fcov_plan.md Section REG) / Fire-check (the assertion that proves
  the scenario happened; every item has one) / Pass criteria (named checkers) / Expected / Test group /
  Bins (the fcov bins the item must hit; declared per test in the fcov-expectation manifest, an unhit
  declared bin fails the run).
- Expected: `pass`; `pass (doc mismatch Dn)` where the RTL is spec-legal and the Ibex doc is wrong
  (checker follows the RTL, doc defect logged); `expected-fail (Bn)` where the RTL contradicts a
  specification (checker follows the spec; logged in gen_bug_log.md; not excluded from the gate without
  a recorded ruling, owner questions Q-004/Q-005). B6 was reclassified RTL-defined; no item is
  expected-fail for it.
- Stimulus rules (DV_prompt.txt Sections 5-6): every DUT input is driven at the boundary; programmable
  configuration is set by instructions and randomized; three randomization layers (per-transaction
  distributions in Stimulus, regime knobs, regime schedule) are exercised and covered (Section REG of
  the fcov plan); a regime is pinnable from the command line (+gen_knob_<name>=<value>,
  +gen_regime_seed=<seed>); one run seed drives every source of randomness.
- Checker inventory (pass criteria vocabulary; TB Infra implements, each with a disable knob
  +gen_chk_<name>_en=0 for mutation evidence): gen_isa_compare (Spike-based RVFI comparator),
  gen_chk_csr_readback, gen_chk_ibus_proto, gen_chk_dbus_proto, gen_chk_store_intg, gen_chk_bus_intg_rsp,
  gen_chk_pmp, gen_chk_irq, gen_chk_nmi, gen_chk_debug, gen_chk_alerts, gen_chk_icache,
  gen_chk_crash_dump, gen_chk_double_fault, gen_chk_counters, gen_chk_sleep, gen_chk_fetch_en,
  gen_chk_cheriot_quiet, gen_sva_ibus / gen_sva_dbus (bound protocol assertions), and test-level cocotb
  fire-checks (gen_test_<name>). Newly requested checkers are listed in Section 2.
- Test groups: a proposed test hosts a group of closely related items; each item keeps its own
  fire-check (DV_prompt.txt Section 5 step 4). Groups are named gen_<area>_<topic>; the Test Writer
  may split a group but never merges fire-checks.

# 4. Items by area

Each area section ends with its own "Test groups", "New checkers requested" and "Open questions"
subsections (the open questions carry the decision blocked and the recommended default; the DV Lead
resolves them in gen_reading_report.md or escalates through the Orchestrator).

# 4.1 Areas ISA, MUL, CMP, BIT, BTALU: Instruction set: RV32I base, M (RV32MSingleCycle), compressed Zca/Zcb/Zcmp, bitmanip RV32BOTEarlGrey, branch target ALU


Scope: F-ISA-001..052, F-MUL-001..028, F-CMP-001..070, F-BIT-001..041, F-BTALU-001..015 (206
features: 172 ACTIVE, 16 ALIAS, 18 FOLDED after the Critic v1 fixes; source
dv/auto_dv/work/dv-lead/parts/gen_part_isa.md). Companion coverage plan: fcov_isa.md (bin namespace
CG-<AREA>-<nnn>.cp_/cr_<name>.<bin>; `auto` = every auto-cross bin).

Conventions used in every item
- Stimulus is a program fetched over the instruction bus (riscv-dv generated or directed
  assembly emitted by the test), data over the data bus, interrupts/debug over pins. "Handler
  read-back" = the trap handler executes csrr mcause/mtval/mepc and the values retire on RVFI
  (rvfi_rd_wdata) where the TB CSR model checks them (gen_chk_csr_readback). No rvfi_csr_* ports
  exist.
- "Operand mix" = per-transaction distribution over the operand classes named in the item's
  covergroup (zero, all-ones, INT_MIN, INT_MAX, +1/-1, random, sign combinations), plus register
  index distributions (rd = x0 with weight ~1/16, rs1 == rs2 == rd with weight ~1/16, otherwise
  random x1..x31), plus random surrounding instructions (dependency chains, loads/stores, nops)
  so forwarding and stall paths are exercised. Every Phase-1 item additionally randomizes: PC
  alignment (2- and 4-byte), privilege (M or U where the instruction is legal in U), unrelated
  CSR state, and the memory-response regime through the named knobs.
- Fire-checks are test-level cocotb assertions on the RVFI monitor stream unless another
  observable is named; they prove the scenario fired (asserted, not assumed).
- Pass criteria name the checkers from the T-006 inventory; new ones (gen_chk_bitmanip_ref,
  gen_chk_timing_isa, gen_chk_zcmp_seq) are listed under "New checkers requested".
- Doc-mismatch numbering is the canonical list of README_FIX_BRIEF rule 5: D7 = divide latency
  (37 total per RTL; instruction_decode_execute.rst 37, pipeline_details.rst 37 stall); D8 = bfp
  single-cycle (RTL) vs multi-cycle (doc table).
- Feature Status (README_FIX_BRIEF rule 1): items may cite ALIAS or FOLDED F-IDs; traceability
  resolves them to the canonical or parent ID. Every canonical ID of an alias is also cited by an
  item of its own area (checked for F-DBG-017, F-PRV-010, F-DBG-032, F-PRV-016, F-CSR-002/003/005,
  F-EXC-008/016/067, F-CSR-021, F-DIT-002, F-PMC-040 and the in-part canonicals F-BTALU-001,
  F-CMP-038, F-ISA-034).
- Bug candidates in this area (dv/auto_dv/docs/gen_bug_log.md): B4 (cm.mvsa01 r1s' == r2s'
  executes), B8 (dummy mid-Zcmp skips a micro-op, needs repro), B11 (not-taken branches counted as
  taken under data_ind_timing), B13 (rvfi_pc_wdata bit 0 on jalr to odd target). Items for these
  follow the spec/intent and are expected-fail. B14 (RVFI drops the ID-stage trap record when a WB
  error coincides) is downgraded to an RVFI convention note pending its confirmation simulation:
  the priority behaviour (the WB error outranks the ID exception; the killed ID instruction
  re-executes after the handler and produces its own record then) is the pass item TP-ISA-050 and
  the record confirmation is the informational item TP-ISA-051 (excluded from the pass gate).
- Cross-area references (F-DIT-*, F-PMC-041, F-IRQ-*, F-DBG-*, F-PMP-*) are given in the text;
  the Features line lists only this area's F-IDs so the trace CSV stays per area.
- Tier: smoke = per-instruction sanity (short), targeted = corner-heavy Phase-1 (medium), full =
  Phase-2 random regimes (long).
- Timing terms: "delta" and "unstalled" follow fcov_isa.md's conventions: the delta is measured
  from the previous retirement (rvfi_ext_mcycle is captured when the instruction leaves ID,
  rtl/ibex_core.sv:2102) and "unstalled" means gap_clean (fetch_stall == no, cpuctrlsts.
  dummy_instr_en == 0 over the gap, no mcycle/mcycleh/mcountinhibit write in the gap,
  cpuctrlsts.icache_enable == 0) plus wb_busy == no. Items that measure timing or count ibus
  redirects pin icache_enable = 0 (a cache hit issues no bus request) and exclude that bit from
  random cpuctrlsts writes; every other redirect claim is derived from RVFI (rvfi_pc_wdata != pc +
  len and the next rvfi_pc_rdata), never from the absence of an ibus request.
- Bins lines: `CG-X.cr_y.auto` expands (in trace_tp_bin_isa.csv) to every reachable auto bin of
  the cross, named by joining the operand bins with `_`, minus the ignores written in
  fcov_isa.md; when the item also lists explicit bins of one of the cross's coverpoints, the
  expansion is restricted to those bins (the item's own stimulus scope). Probe-gated bins,
  ignore_bins and operand-only standalone bins are never listed.
- Fire-checks are per-seed assertions on an observable (never "every bin hit over the
  regression"); counts such as ">= 50" are per seed.

## Layer-1 weight tables (per-transaction distributions; DV_prompt Section 6 layer 1)

Every Stimulus line that says "operand mix", "class mix", "immediate mix", "index mix", "rd mix" or
names a class set without weights uses the table of its operand class below; an item that states
its own weights overrides the table for that item only. Weights are relative per-transaction
frequencies. Layer 2 (regime knobs) is the item's Knobs line; layer 3 (the regime schedule) is
owned by the xcut part (CG-REG-*).

| Table | Operand class | Distribution |
|---|---|---|
| W1 | 32-bit register operand (rs1/rs2/rs3 of ALU, Zb*, compare and address operands) | zero 1, all_ones 1, int_min 1, int_max 1, one 1, group-specific extremes (p16, two, e0000000, byte_msb, half_msb, single_bit, alt_5/alt_a, bytes_01020304, distinct_lanes) 1 each, pos_rand 4, neg_rand 4 |
| W2 | Immediates (imm12, imm20, imm6, Zc uimm/nzuimm/nzimm) | zero 1, plus1 1, minus1 1, max 1, min 1, pos_rand 4, neg_rand 4 (unsigned fields: zero 1, max 1, rand 6) |
| W3 | Shift / rotate / bit-index amounts and register-form upper bits | amount: 0 1, 1 1, 31 1 (63 1 for funnel shifts), 32/33 1 each where the field allows, the remaining values uniform with total weight 4; rs2[31:5]: zero 4, {32, 33, 0xFFFFFFE0, 0x80000000, 0xFFFFFFFF} 1 each, other_nonzero 2 |
| W4 | Register indices (every instruction) | rd = x0 1/16, rs1 == rs2 == rd 1/16, rs1 == rs2 != rd 1/16, rs1 == rd or rs2 == rd 1/8, otherwise uniform over x1..x31 (x0 as a source 1/16); 3-bit compressed fields uniform over x8..x15; Zcmp rlist uniform over 4..15, spimm uniform over 0..3; ternary rs3 choice eq_rs1/eq_rs2/eq_rd/x0 1 each, distinct 4 |
| W5 | Branch compare-operand pairs | the eight named classes of CG-ISA-007.cp_cmp_class 1 each, rand 6; taken/not-taken balanced per op by construction |
| W6 | Control-transfer offsets and jalr immediates | offset: self 1, max_fwd 1, max_bwd 1, pos_rand 4, neg_rand 4 (the extremes only in items whose memory map provides the targets); jalr imm: zero 1, max_pos 1, min_neg 1, odd 2, pos_rand 3, neg_rand 3; target alignment word/half 1:1 |
| W7 | Multiply / divide operands | rs1/rs2 (dividend/divisor): the named extremes of CG-MUL-001/CG-MUL-003 1 each, pos_rand 4, neg_rand 4; divisor zero 1 (raised to 10 percent of divides in the div-by-zero items); sign pairs balanced |
| W8 | Zc immediates and stack geometry | min 1, max 1, zero 1 (where legal), plus16/minus16 1 each (c.addi16sp), rand 4; sp[1:0]: aligned only, except the misaligned-sp items (aligned 1, mis1/mis2/mis3 1 each); Zcmp frame contents random with a checkable pattern |
| W9 | Zb* control words | grev/gorc control uniform over 0..31 and shfl/unshfl over 0..15 with the canonical values (7, 24, 31; 15) weight 2; bfp len {0, 1, 15} 1 each and 2..14 total 4, off {0, 16, 31} 1 each and the rest total 4, data zero/all_ones 1 each, rand 4; xperm index pattern identity/reverse/all_same/all_oob/mixed_oob 1 each, rand 4 |
| W10 | Memory-response classes inside a regime (ibus/dbus agents) | inside knob value `random`: gnt same_cycle 4, short 3, long 1; rvalid min1 4, short 3, long 1; error injection per knob:*_err_rate (rare = 1 percent, frequent = 10 percent of responses); the pinned values (min1, same_cycle, none) are exact |

Table use by covergroup: W1 + W2 + W4 for CG-ISA-001..005 and CG-BIT-001/002/005/006/007/008;
W3 for CG-ISA-003 and CG-BIT-003/006/008 (amounts, indices); W5 + W6 for CG-ISA-006/007 and
CG-BTALU-001..003; W7 for CG-MUL-001..005; W8 + W4 for CG-CMP-001..010; W9 for CG-BIT-004/005/
008/009; W10 for every item that names an imem/dmem knob.

## AREA ISA

### TP-ISA-001: I-type ALU instructions (addi, slti, sltiu, xori, ori, andi)
- Features: F-ISA-001
- Phase: 1
- Tier: smoke
- Preconditions: M-mode after boot; mtvec set to the test handler.
- Stimulus: >= 2000 I-type ALU instructions in random order with operand mix over rs1 class (7 classes, weights 1:1:1:1:1:4:4) and imm class (7 classes, same weights); rd/rs1 index mix incl. rd = x0 and rs1 == rd; interleaved with random independent instructions.
- Randomized: operand values, immediates, register indices, instruction order, PC alignment, U vs M mode (50/50 after a U-mode entry via mret).
- Knobs: knob:imem_rvalid_delay, knob:imem_gnt_delay
- Fire-check: RVFI shows >= 1 retirement of each of the six opcodes with rvfi_trap = 0 and, per opcode, at least one rs1 class from each of the 7 classes (counted by the test from rvfi_rs1_rdata).
- Pass criteria: gen_isa_compare; detects a wrong rd value, wrong rd index, or a spurious trap.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_isa_alu
- Bins: CG-ISA-001.cp_op.addi, CG-ISA-001.cp_op.slti, CG-ISA-001.cp_op.sltiu, CG-ISA-001.cp_op.xori, CG-ISA-001.cp_op.ori, CG-ISA-001.cp_op.andi, CG-ISA-001.cr_op_rs1.auto, CG-ISA-001.cr_op_imm.auto, CG-ISA-001.cr_op_rd_x0.auto, CG-ISA-001.cp_rs1_eq_rd.yes, CG-ISA-001.cp_rs1_eq_rd.no, CG-ISA-001.cp_result_class.zero, CG-ISA-001.cp_result_class.all_ones, CG-ISA-001.cp_result_class.int_min, CG-ISA-001.cp_result_class.int_max, CG-ISA-001.cp_result_class.one, CG-ISA-001.cp_result_class.other, CG-ISA-001.cp_addi_wrap.none, CG-ISA-001.cp_slt_case.other, CG-ISA-001.cr_slt.slti_other, CG-ISA-001.cr_slt.sltiu_other

### TP-ISA-002: addi overflow wraps to the low 32 bits
- Features: F-ISA-002
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: as TP-ISA-001.
- Stimulus: addi with (rs1, imm) drawn so that 30% of iterations produce a positive wrap (rs1 in [0x7FFFF800:0x7FFFFFFF], imm > INT_MAX - rs1), 30% a negative wrap (rs1 in [0x80000000:0x800007FF], imm < INT_MIN - rs1), 40% random; the pinned pairs (0x7FFFFFFF,+1) and (0x80000000,-1) appear at least once each.
- Randomized: rs1 within the wrap window, imm, rd, surrounding code, PC alignment.
- Knobs: knob:imem_rvalid_delay
- Fire-check: RVFI retirement of an addi whose rs1 and imm have the same sign and rvfi_rd_wdata has the opposite sign, for both signs.
- Pass criteria: gen_isa_compare; detects a 33rd-bit leak or saturation.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_isa_alu
- Bins: CG-ISA-001.cp_addi_wrap.pos_wrap, CG-ISA-001.cp_addi_wrap.neg_wrap, CG-ISA-001.cp_result_class.int_min, CG-ISA-001.cp_result_class.int_max

### TP-ISA-003: slti/sltiu boundary comparisons
- Features: F-ISA-003
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: as TP-ISA-001.
- Stimulus: slti/sltiu with operand pairs from a boundary table (rs1 == sext(imm); slti(INT_MIN, 0); slti(0, INT_MIN-class imm -2048); sltiu rs1, -1; sltiu rs1, 1 with rs1 in {0, 1, random}; sltiu(0xFFFFFFFF, -1)) at weight 50%, random pairs otherwise.
- Randomized: which boundary case, rs1 exact value inside each class, rd, order.
- Knobs: knob:imem_rvalid_delay, knob:imem_gnt_delay
- Fire-check: every cp_slt_case class observed at least once on RVFI with rvfi_trap = 0 (test counts from rs1/imm).
- Pass criteria: gen_isa_compare; detects signed/unsigned confusion of the immediate.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_isa_alu
- Bins: CG-ISA-001.cp_slt_case.eq, CG-ISA-001.cp_slt_case.slti_intmin_0, CG-ISA-001.cp_slt_case.slti_0_neg, CG-ISA-001.cp_slt_case.sltiu_imm_m1, CG-ISA-001.cp_slt_case.sltiu_seqz, CG-ISA-001.cp_slt_case.sltiu_ones_m1, CG-ISA-001.cr_slt.auto

### TP-ISA-004: HINT encodings with rd = x0 execute as no-ops
- Features: F-ISA-004, F-ISA-051
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: M-mode; mcountinhibit = 0 so minstret counts.
- Stimulus: every rd-writing 32-bit class with rd = x0 (I-type, shifts incl. the semihosting markers slli x0,x0,0x1f and srai x0,x0,7, R-type, lui, auipc, canonical nop), each followed within 1-3 instructions by a reader of x0 (rs1 or rs2 = x0) whose result depends on x0 being zero; csrr minstret before/after blocks of 64 such hints.
- Randomized: hint class order, rs1/imm values, distance to the x0 reader, PC alignment, U vs M mode.
- Knobs: knob:imem_rvalid_delay
- Fire-check: >= 1 RVFI retirement per cp_hint_class bin with rvfi_rd_addr = 0, rvfi_rd_wdata = 0, rvfi_trap = 0; the following reader retires with rvfi_rs*_rdata = 0; minstret delta over each 64-hint block == 64 (handler-free straight-line code, dummy_instr_en = 0).
- Pass criteria: gen_isa_compare (x0 stays 0, no trap); gen_chk_counters (minstret counts hints); gen_chk_csr_readback.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_isa_alu
- Bins: CG-ISA-005.cp_hint_class.canonical_nop, CG-ISA-005.cp_hint_class.addi_x0_nzimm, CG-ISA-005.cp_hint_class.andi_x0, CG-ISA-005.cp_hint_class.ori_x0, CG-ISA-005.cp_hint_class.xori_x0, CG-ISA-005.cp_hint_class.slti_x0, CG-ISA-005.cp_hint_class.sltiu_x0, CG-ISA-005.cp_hint_class.lui_x0, CG-ISA-005.cp_hint_class.auipc_x0, CG-ISA-005.cp_hint_class.add_x0, CG-ISA-005.cp_hint_class.sub_x0, CG-ISA-005.cp_hint_class.sll_x0, CG-ISA-005.cp_hint_class.srl_x0, CG-ISA-005.cp_hint_class.sra_x0, CG-ISA-005.cp_hint_class.slt_x0, CG-ISA-005.cp_hint_class.sltu_x0, CG-ISA-005.cp_hint_class.xor_x0, CG-ISA-005.cp_hint_class.or_x0, CG-ISA-005.cp_hint_class.and_x0, CG-ISA-005.cp_hint_class.slli_x0_semihost, CG-ISA-005.cp_hint_class.srai_x0_semihost, CG-ISA-005.cp_hint_class.slli_x0_other, CG-ISA-005.cp_hint_class.srli_x0, CG-ISA-005.cp_hint_class.srai_x0_other, CG-ISA-005.cp_x0_read.rs1_zero, CG-ISA-005.cp_x0_read.rs2_zero, CG-ISA-001.cp_rd_x0.yes, CG-ISA-002.cp_rd_x0.yes, CG-ISA-003.cp_rd_x0.yes, CG-ISA-004.cp_rd_x0.yes

### TP-ISA-006: lui/auipc immediate extremes and PC wrap
- Features: F-ISA-006
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: M-mode; program text placed by the TB memory map in the last page (0xFFFFF000..) for the wrap iterations and in a low page otherwise.
- Stimulus: lui imm 0xFFFFF and 0; auipc with imm chosen so pc + (imm << 12) carries out (program in the high page, imm >= 1) and auipc imm = 0 at both PC alignments; random imm otherwise; lui/auipc also executed from the low page (pc < 0x1000, TB memory map as TP-ISA-016).
- Randomized: exact imm, rd, PC alignment, which page the program runs from.
- Knobs: knob:imem_rvalid_delay, knob:imem_gnt_delay
- Fire-check: RVFI auipc retirement at pc >= 0xFFFFF000 with rvfi_rd_wdata < pc (wrap); lui with rvfi_rd_wdata = 0xFFFFF000 and = 0; auipc imm 0 at pc[1] = 1 with rvfi_rd_wdata = pc.
- Pass criteria: gen_isa_compare; detects a 33rd-bit leak.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_isa_alu
- Bins: CG-ISA-004.cp_imm20.all_ones, CG-ISA-004.cp_imm20.zero, CG-ISA-004.cp_pc_region.high, CG-ISA-004.cr_auipc_pc.auipc_word_wrap, CG-ISA-004.cr_auipc_pc.auipc_half_wrap, CG-ISA-004.cr_auipc_pc.auipc_half_nowrap, CG-ISA-004.cr_auipc_pc.auipc_word_nowrap, CG-ISA-004.cp_pc_region.low

### TP-ISA-011: Shift amount 0 and 31, sign propagation
- Features: F-ISA-011
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: M-mode.
- Stimulus: directed-in-random: shift by 0 of random operands (result must equal rs1); slli 1 by 31; srai by 31 of negative and positive operands; srli 0x80000000 by 31; srai 0x80000000 by 1; same cases through sll/srl/sra with rs2 holding the amount.
- Randomized: which case per iteration, the random operand bits not fixed by the case, register indices, imm vs register form.
- Knobs: knob:imem_rvalid_delay, knob:imem_gnt_delay
- Fire-check: each cr_sra_sign bin's (op, operand class, shamt) tuple observed on RVFI; at least one shift by 0 per op with rvfi_rd_wdata == rvfi_rs1_rdata.
- Pass criteria: gen_isa_compare; detects sign-fill and shift-by-zero errors.

### TP-ISA-012: Reserved shift-immediate encodings: trapping set vs fsri-decoded set
- Features: F-ISA-012
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: M-mode and U-mode iterations; mtvec set; handler reads mcause/mtval/mepc and skips the instruction; x8 pre-loaded with a random value (rs3 of the srai-pattern fsri).
- Stimulus: trapping set - slli (instr[31:27] = 00000) with instr[26:25] in {01, 10, 11} and srli/srai (instr[31:27] = 00000 / 01000) with instr[26:25] = 01; fsri-decoded set - the srli/srai bit patterns with instr[26] = 1 (instr[26:25] in {10, 11}), which execute as fsri rd, rs1, rs3 = instr[31:27] (x0 for the srli pattern, x8 for the srai pattern) with shamt = instr[25:20]; lenient control - sloi (instr[31:27] = 00100) with instr[26:25] != 00 (F-BIT-037); legal instr[26:25] = 00 forms as controls; random rd/rs1/shamt[4:0], embedded in random legal code.
- Randomized: which pattern, rd/rs1/shamt, x8 value, position, privilege.
- Knobs: knob:imem_rvalid_delay
- Fire-check: RVFI retirement with rvfi_trap = 1 for each trapping pattern (slli with 01, 10 and 11; srli and srai with 01) and handler read-back mcause = 2, mtval = the 32-bit word; each instr[26] = 1 pattern retires with rvfi_trap = 0, rvfi_rs3_addr = instr[31:27] and rvfi_rd_wdata = the fsri result; the controls retire with rvfi_trap = 0.
- Pass criteria: gen_isa_compare (trapping set and legal controls agree with Spike; the fsri-decoded and sloi-lenient forms are skipped per OQ-3 c); gen_chk_bitmanip_ref (fsri result for the instr[26] = 1 forms, sloi result for the lenient forms); gen_chk_csr_readback (mcause/mtval/mepc).
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_isa_illegal
- Bins: CG-ISA-011.cp_class.shift_imm_bit25, CG-ISA-011.cp_len.w32, CG-ISA-011.cp_mtval_ok.yes, CG-ISA-011.cp_mepc_ok.yes, CG-ISA-011.cr_class_priv.auto, CG-BIT-008.cp_op.fsri, CG-BIT-008.cp_fsri_hi5.srli_pattern, CG-BIT-008.cp_fsri_hi5.srai_pattern, CG-BIT-003.cp_sloi_bits.b01, CG-BIT-003.cp_sloi_bits.b10, CG-BIT-003.cp_sloi_bits.b11

### TP-ISA-050: Illegal instruction while a load/store is outstanding in WB
- Features: F-ISA-050
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: M-mode; PMP region programmed to fault a chosen data address for the error iterations (or data_err_i injected by the dbus agent); handler as TP-ISA-047 distinguishing mcause 2/5/7.
- Stimulus: a load or store immediately followed by an illegal instruction (random class), with the data response delayed (knob) so the illegal instruction sits in ID while the access is in WB; in 30% of iterations the access faults (PMP or bus error).
- Randomized: load vs store, illegal class, response delay, fault kind, whether the access faults, alignment.
- Knobs: knob:dmem_rvalid_delay, knob:dmem_err_rate, knob:pmp_regime
- Fire-check: no-fault case: the access retires (rvfi_trap = 0, rvfi_mem_* valid) then the illegal instruction retires with rvfi_trap = 1 and mcause 2; fault case: the access retires with rvfi_trap = 1 and mcause 5/7 first, the handler returns to the illegal instruction which then traps with mcause 2 (architectural order); dbus monitor confirms the response arrived after the illegal instruction was fetched.
- Pass criteria: gen_isa_compare (trap order and causes: the WB error outranks the ID exception, the ID instruction is killed and re-executes after the handler, producing its own trap record then); gen_chk_csr_readback; gen_chk_pmp; gen_chk_dbus_proto. The RVFI record-count confirmation of B14 is the informational item TP-ISA-051.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_isa_illegal

### TP-ISA-051: RVFI record confirmation for the ID-stage illegal trap that coincides with a WB error (B14)
- Features: F-ISA-050
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: as TP-ISA-050, fault iterations only. The priority behaviour itself (the WB error outranks the ID exception; the killed ID instruction re-executes after the handler) is the pass item TP-ISA-050; this item only confirms the RVFI record count (gen_bug_log.md B14, downgraded to an RVFI convention note pending this simulation).
- Stimulus: store/load with a slow error response followed immediately by an illegal instruction; the RVFI monitor records every rvfi_trap entry.
- Randomized: as TP-ISA-050.
- Knobs: knob:dmem_rvalid_delay, knob:dmem_err_rate
- Fire-check: per seed >= 1 coincidence in which the dbus response with data_err_i (or the PMP fault) arrives after the illegal instruction was fetched (dbus timestamp versus the RVFI order) and the WB access retires with rvfi_trap = 1; then the RVFI stream shows exactly two trap records for the pair, in order: the access (mcause 5/7) and, after the handler's mret, the re-executed illegal instruction (mcause 2). A single record for the pair re-opens B14 (rtl-arch T-041 fact-check row 48).
- Pass criteria: gen_isa_compare (trap order; the killed ID attempt has no architectural effect, so the ISA model shows the same two traps); the record count is reported by the test, not gated.
- Expected: informational (B14 confirmation; excluded from the pass gate)
- Test group: gen_isa_illegal
- Bins: CG-ISA-011.cr_wb.load_err, CG-ISA-011.cr_wb.store_err

### TP-ISA-052: Writes to x0 are discarded for every instruction class
- Features: F-ISA-051
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: M-mode; data memory mapped.
- Stimulus: x0-destination forms of every class: ALU, load (lw x0), csrr x0, jal x0 (j), jalr x0, mul/mulh/div/rem x0, single- and two-cycle Zb* x0, c.li/c.lui/c.slli/c.mv/c.add x0; each followed by an x0 reader (add rd, x0, x0; sw x0; beq x0, x0).
- Randomized: class order, operand values (nonzero results so a leaked write would be visible), distance to the reader.
- Knobs: knob:dmem_rvalid_delay
- Fire-check: >= 1 RVFI retirement per cp_writer_class with rvfi_rd_addr = 0 and rvfi_rd_wdata = 0, followed by a reader with rvfi_rs*_rdata = 0; the sw x0 stores 0 on the data bus.
- Pass criteria: gen_isa_compare; gen_chk_dbus_proto.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_isa_alu
- Bins: CG-ISA-005.cp_writer_class.alu_imm, CG-ISA-005.cp_writer_class.shift, CG-ISA-005.cp_writer_class.alu_reg, CG-ISA-005.cp_writer_class.lui_auipc, CG-ISA-005.cp_writer_class.load, CG-ISA-005.cp_writer_class.csrr, CG-ISA-005.cp_writer_class.jal, CG-ISA-005.cp_writer_class.jalr, CG-ISA-005.cp_writer_class.mul, CG-ISA-005.cp_writer_class.mulh, CG-ISA-005.cp_writer_class.div_rem, CG-ISA-005.cp_writer_class.bit_1cyc, CG-ISA-005.cp_writer_class.bit_2cyc, CG-ISA-005.cp_writer_class.cmp_hint, CG-ISA-005.cr_writer_read.auto, CG-ISA-005.cp_hint_class.other

### TP-MUL-022: data_ind_timing = 1 forces full-latency divide-by-zero
- Features: F-MUL-022
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted

- Stimulus: div/divu/rem/remu by zero and by non-zero under DIT = 1, bracketed by single-cycle ALU ops; the same sequence under DIT = 0.
- Randomized: op, dividend, DIT schedule, indices.

- Fire-check: under DIT = 1: >= 30 divide-by-zero retirements with delta 37 unstalled and correct results (all-ones / dividend); under DIT = 0 the same ops show delta 2; the cpuctrlsts read-back confirms the DIT value at each measurement.
- Pass criteria: gen_isa_compare; gen_chk_timing_isa (37 for every divide when DIT = 1); gen_chk_csr_readback.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_mul_div
- Bins: CG-MUL-004.cr_dit_div0_delta.dit1_div0_d37, CG-MUL-004.cr_dit_div0_delta.dit1_nodiv0_d37, CG-MUL-004.cr_dit_div0_delta.dit0_div0_d2, CG-MUL-004.cp_dit.on, CG-MUL-004.cr_op_div0.auto

### TP-MUL-023: Interrupt or debug request during a divide is deferred
- Features: F-MUL-023
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: M-mode; mie/mstatus.MIE enabled; debug ROM present; DIT randomized.
- Stimulus: divides (zero and non-zero divisors) while the irq driver asserts an enabled line, irq_nm_i, or debug_req_i at a random cycle inside the divide's 37-cycle window (the driver is synchronized to the RVFI retirement of the instruction before the divide).
- Randomized: event kind, cycle offset within the window, op, operands, DIT.
- Knobs: knob:irq_regime, knob:irq_line_mix, knob:debug_req_regime
- Fire-check: pin assertion timestamp lies inside the divide's window (between the previous retirement and the divide's retirement); the divide retires with rvfi_trap = 0 and the correct result; the next retirement is the handler (rvfi_intr) or the debug ROM; mepc/dpc read-back == the instruction after the divide; measured irq latency <= 37 + entry cycles.
- Pass criteria: gen_isa_compare; gen_chk_irq (entry after the pipeline drains, mepc); gen_chk_debug (dpc); gen_chk_csr_readback.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_mul_timing
- Bins: CG-MUL-004.cr_op_event.auto, CG-MUL-004.cr_event_div0_dit.auto, CG-MUL-004.cp_event_mid.irq, CG-MUL-004.cp_event_mid.debug_req, CG-MUL-004.cp_event_mid.nmi, CG-MUL-004.cp_irq_latency.le37, CG-MUL-004.cp_irq_latency.gt37

### TP-MUL-030: Divider FSM freeze arc: bound SVA cover and assertion under instr_executing-dropping stimuli
- Features: F-MUL-028
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: M-mode; gen_sva_multdiv bound into ibex_multdiv_fast (probe candidate, coverage/assertion only, OQ-9); PMP region and dbus error injection available; mie/mstatus.MIE set; debug ROM present; cpuctrlsts.data_ind_timing randomized per iteration.
- Stimulus: div/divu/rem/remu (zero and non-zero divisors) immediately after a slow load/store (rvalid 2..40 cycles), immediately after a faulting load/store (PMP or data_err_i, handler returns to the access), with an enabled irq line / irq_nm_i / debug_req_i asserted inside the divide window, and with the instruction after the divide fetched from a PMP-denied or instr_err_i word; plain divides as controls.
- Randomized: op, operands, DIT, which disturbance, response delay / cycle offset, fault kind, privilege.
- Knobs: knob:dmem_rvalid_delay, knob:dmem_err_rate, knob:pmp_regime, knob:irq_regime, knob:debug_req_regime, knob:imem_err_rate
- Fire-check: every divide whose first cycle was observed (previous retirement seen, dbus idle or busy as scheduled) retires exactly once on RVFI with the correct rvfi_rd_wdata, also after a fault-kill and re-execution of the same PC; the test records the gen_sva_multdiv cover count (div_en_i == 0 && md_state_q != MD_IDLE), expected 0 per gen_hierarchy_map.md H-D3 - a nonzero count is logged as a reachability finding, not as a failure; the assertion (|=> $stable(md_state_q)) reports no failure over the run.
- Pass criteria: gen_sva_multdiv (bound assertion never fails; new); gen_isa_compare; gen_chk_timing_isa (37 / 2 cycles when unstalled); gen_chk_dbus_proto; gen_chk_pmp.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_mul_timing
- Bins: CG-MUL-005.cp_div_ctx.plain, CG-MUL-005.cp_div_ctx.slow_wb, CG-MUL-005.cp_div_ctx.fault_wb, CG-MUL-005.cp_div_ctx.irq_mid, CG-MUL-005.cp_div_ctx.debug_mid, CG-MUL-005.cp_div_ctx.fetch_err_next (CG-MUL-005 cp_sva_checked yes is probe-gated until the gen_sva_multdiv bind is registered, not in this manifest), CG-MUL-005.cr_ctx_op.auto, CG-MUL-005.cr_ctx_dit.auto

### TP-CMP-060: PMP store fault on the k-th pushed store
- Features: F-CMP-060
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: M-mode with a PMP region (TOR/NA4/NAPOT randomized) denying W over exactly one word of the frame (and mseccfg.MML randomized so M-mode is checked per cross-ref F-PMP-*); handler reads mcause/mtval/mepc and unlocks the word (or re-programs PMP) before mret.
- Stimulus: cm.push with rlist 4..15 where the denied word is the k-th store (k random in 0..N-1).
- Randomized: rlist, spimm, k, region type, x2.
- Knobs: knob:pmp_regime, knob:dmem_rvalid_delay
- Fire-check: store micro-ops 0..k-1 retire with rvfi_trap = 0 and are visible in memory (read back); micro-op k retires with rvfi_trap = 1; mcause 7, mtval = the faulting address, mepc = cm.push PC; no addi sp before the handler; after mret all N stores repeat.

### TP-CMP-072: Zcmp halfword with a fetch error (bus error or PMP execute denial)
- Features: F-CMP-069
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: M/U; trap handler reading mcause/mtval/mepc; for the PMP iterations a region without X covering exactly the word that holds the cm.* halfword (re-enabled by the handler before mret); for the bus-error iterations the ibus agent returns instr_err_i for that word once; stack region mapped and pre-cleared; pushed registers pre-loaded.
- Stimulus: each of cm.push/cm.pop/cm.popret/cm.popretz/cm.mvsa01/cm.mva01s (random rlist/spimm/registers) placed at both halfword alignments, reached sequentially and as a jump target, with the error kind alternating; after the handler clears the error the same PC re-executes (or a different cm.* follows) so the restart from micro-op 0 is observed.
- Randomized: instruction, rlist/spimm, alignment, error kind, privilege, how the halfword is reached, memory-response regime.
- Knobs: knob:imem_err_rate, knob:pmp_regime, knob:imem_rvalid_delay
- Fire-check: exactly one RVFI entry with rvfi_trap = 1 at the cm.* PC; handler read-back mcause = 1 and mtval = mepc = the cm.* PC; on that entry rvfi_ext_expanded_insn_valid = 0 for the bus error and = 1 with rvfi_ext_expanded_insn_last = 0 for the PMP error; dbus monitor shows no data_req_o between the previous retirement and the handler entry; x2 and the rlist registers read back unchanged; the following cm.* retires N+1 / N+2 / N+3 / 2 micro-ops starting with micro-op 0.
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_zcmp_seq (no micro-op executed; restart from micro-op 0); gen_chk_csr_readback (cause 1, mtval, mepc); gen_chk_dbus_proto (no request); gen_chk_pmp; gen_isa_compare (fetch fault at the cm.* PC).
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_cmp_zcmp_faults
- Bins: CG-CMP-010.cp_err_kind.bus, CG-CMP-010.cp_err_kind.pmp, CG-CMP-010.cr_insn_err.auto, CG-CMP-010.cp_expanded_tag.bus_not_expanded, CG-CMP-010.cp_expanded_tag.pmp_expanded, CG-CMP-010.cp_no_dreq.yes, CG-CMP-010.cp_next_uop0.yes, CG-CMP-010.cp_mtval_ok.yes, CG-CMP-010.cr_err_align.auto, CG-CMP-010.cr_err_reach.auto

- Bins: CG-BIT-010.cr_class_event.auto, CG-BIT-010.cr_class_wb.auto, CG-BIT-010.cr_class_prev.auto, CG-BIT-010.cr_class_next.auto, CG-BIT-009.cp_delta.d2plus, CG-BIT-010.cp_fetch_stall.yes

### TP-BIT-043: Two-cycle bitmanip op held in its second cycle by a busy writeback stage
- Features: F-BIT-041
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: M-mode; cpuctrlsts.icache_enable = 0 pinned for the whole test (the ibus monitor then sees every fetch; excluded from random cpuctrlsts writes) with knob:imem_rvalid_delay pinned to min1 and knob:imem_gnt_delay to same_cycle for the measurement blocks (+gen_regime_pin).
- Stimulus: load or store with rvalid delayed 3..24 cycles immediately followed by rol/ror/rori/cmov/cmix/fsl/fsr/fsri/crc32* whose operands do not depend on the load (so the hold is WB-busy, not a load-use stall), then a consumer of the result; controls with response delay 1.
- Randomized: access type, delay, op, operands, rs3 choice, whether a consumer follows.
- Knobs: knob:dmem_rvalid_delay, knob:dmem_gnt_delay
- Fire-check: dbus monitor timestamps data_rvalid_i of the preceding access after the op entered ID (previous retirement seen before the response); the op retires exactly once with retire delta = 2 + hold cycles and correct rvfi_rd_wdata (rvfi_rs3_* populated for the ternary forms); the consumer's rvfi_rs*_rdata equals it.
- Pass criteria: gen_isa_compare / gen_chk_bitmanip_ref (result); gen_chk_dbus_proto; gen_chk_timing_isa (delta >= 2 with wb_busy; exactly 2 + hold in the directed cases).
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_bit_multicycle
- Bins: CG-BIT-010.cr_class_wb.auto, CG-BIT-010.cp_wb_busy.yes, CG-BIT-010.cp_hold_cycles.h1, CG-BIT-010.cp_hold_cycles.h2_4, CG-BIT-010.cp_hold_cycles.h5plus, CG-BIT-010.cr_class_hold.auto, CG-BIT-010.cp_wb_kind.load, CG-BIT-010.cp_wb_kind.store

## AREA BTALU

### TP-BTALU-001: Branch target computed in parallel with the condition (single ID cycle)
- Features: F-BTALU-001
- Phase: 1
- Tier: smoke
- Preconditions: M-mode; cpuctrlsts.data_ind_timing = 0; cpuctrlsts.icache_enable = 0 pinned for the whole test (the ibus monitor then sees every fetch; excluded from random cpuctrlsts writes) with knob:imem_rvalid_delay pinned to min1 and knob:imem_gnt_delay to same_cycle for the measurement blocks (+gen_regime_pin).
- Stimulus: taken and not-taken branches of all six ops in straight-line code bracketed by single-cycle ALU ops, forward/backward, targets at both alignments, distances from short to maximum.
- Randomized: op, operands, direction, distance, alignment, surrounding ALU ops.
- Knobs: knob:imem_rvalid_delay
- Fire-check: >= 100 taken branches with retire delta 2 and >= 100 not-taken with delta 1 while the ibus monitor reports no fetch stall; ibus shows the target request issued immediately after the branch fetch (one redirect per taken branch).
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_timing_isa (taken 2 / not-taken 1 unstalled); gen_isa_compare; gen_chk_ibus_proto.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_btalu_basic

### TP-BTALU-005: Not-taken branch does not redirect (data_ind_timing = 0)

### TP-BTALU-006: data_ind_timing = 1 makes every branch two cycles and redirects not-taken branches
- Features: F-BTALU-006
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: M-mode; cpuctrlsts.data_ind_timing set/cleared by csrw at random points (cross-ref F-DIT-*), read back; cpuctrlsts.icache_enable = 0 pinned for the whole test (the ibus monitor then sees every fetch; excluded from random cpuctrlsts writes) with knob:imem_rvalid_delay pinned to min1 and knob:imem_gnt_delay to same_cycle for the measurement blocks (+gen_regime_pin).

- Pass criteria: gen_chk_timing_isa (constant 2 under DIT); gen_chk_ibus_proto (redirect on every branch under DIT); gen_isa_compare; gen_chk_csr_readback.

### TP-BTALU-008: rvfi_pc_wdata keeps bit 0 for jalr to an odd target
- Features: F-BTALU-008
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: M-mode.
- Stimulus: jalr/c.jr/c.jalr with odd rs1 + imm sums; the RVFI monitor records rvfi_pc_wdata[0] and the next rvfi_pc_rdata.

### TP-BTALU-009: BTALU carry-out discarded (address wrap)
- Features: F-BTALU-009
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: M-mode; TB memory map with code near 0xFFFFFFF0 and near 0.
- Stimulus: jal at 0xFFFFFFFC with +8; branches near the top with positive offsets and near 0 with negative offsets; jalr with rs1 + imm carrying out.

### TP-BTALU-010: Fetch error at the branch/jump target is reported on the target
- Features: F-BTALU-010
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: M/U; a PMP region without X covering the target page (cross-ref F-PMP-*), or the ibus agent returning instr_err_i for the target word; handler reads mcause/mtval/mepc and redirects.

- Fire-check: the transfer retires with rvfi_trap = 0; the next RVFI entry has rvfi_trap = 1 with rvfi_pc_rdata = target; read-back mcause 1, mtval = target, mepc = target; not-taken variants produce no trap.
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_pmp (fetch denied: no ibus request when PMP denies); gen_chk_ibus_proto; gen_chk_csr_readback; gen_isa_compare.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_btalu_hazard
- Bins: CG-BTALU-003.cr_cti_fault.auto, CG-BTALU-003.cp_target_fault.pmp_exec, CG-BTALU-003.cp_target_fault.bus_err, CG-BTALU-003.cp_mtval_target_ok.yes

### TP-BTALU-011: branch_set/jump_set issued once while the instruction waits for an outstanding WB access
- Features: F-BTALU-011
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: M-mode; for the error iterations a PMP-denied or data_err_i store/load address; handler as TP-ISA-050; cpuctrlsts.icache_enable = 0 pinned and data_ind_timing = 0 (the redirect count is bus-derived).
- Stimulus: a load or store with a slow response immediately followed by a taken branch, jal or jalr (operands independent of the access); 30% of iterations make the access fault.
- Randomized: access kind, delay, CTI kind, fault.
- Knobs: knob:dmem_rvalid_delay, knob:dmem_gnt_delay, knob:dmem_err_rate, knob:pmp_regime
- Fire-check: no-fault: exactly one ibus redirect for the CTI and the CTI retires after the access; fault: the access retires with rvfi_trap = 1, the CTI never retires (next RVFI entry is the handler), and the redirected fetch is discarded (no retirement from the target before the handler).
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_ibus_proto (single redirect); gen_isa_compare (CTI absent from the architectural stream on fault); gen_chk_csr_readback; gen_chk_pmp.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_btalu_hazard
- Bins: CG-BTALU-003.cr_cti_wb.auto, CG-BTALU-003.cr_cti_redirects.auto, CG-BTALU-003.cp_redirect_count.one, CG-BTALU-003.cp_redirect_count.zero

### TP-BTALU-012: fence.i uses the BTALU for pc + 4
- Features: F-BTALU-012
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted

- Pass criteria: gen_chk_ibus_proto; gen_chk_timing_isa; gen_isa_compare.

### TP-BTALU-015: Branch/jump performance counter events
- Features: F-BTALU-015
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: M-mode; the event counters are hardwired: mhpmcounter7 = NumJumps, mhpmcounter8 = NumBranches, mhpmcounter9 = NumBranchesTaken (rtl/ibex_cs_registers.sv:1585-1597; the mhpmevent selectors are read-only, :1600-1617, so no mhpmevent write selects them; one csrw mhpmevent7..9 with random data is issued as a control and its read-back must be unchanged); mcountinhibit = 0; data_ind_timing = 0.
- Stimulus: blocks of N random branches (taken/not-taken mix known to the test), M jumps (jal/jalr/fence.i), read the three counters before and after each block.
- Randomized: N, M, mix, block contents.
- Knobs: knob:imem_rvalid_delay
- Fire-check: counter deltas over each block (csrr mhpmcounter7/8/9 pairs): branch = N, taken = number of taken branches in the block (test-known), jump = M (fence.i counted); rvfi_ext_mhpmcounters[7 - 3], [8 - 3], [9 - 3] agree per instruction (rtl/ibex_core.sv:2108-2126).
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_counters; gen_chk_csr_readback.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_btalu_dit
- Bins: CG-BTALU-001.cr_perf.t_dit0_inc1, CG-BTALU-001.cr_perf.nt_dit0_inc0, CG-BTALU-001.cp_branch_inc.inc1

## New checkers requested

- gen_chk_bitmanip_ref: RTL-independent reference model for the draft-0.93 Zbp/Zbt/Zbf/Zbr
  instructions Spike does not implement (slo/sro/sloi/sroi, grev/grevi/gorc/gorci with controls
  other than 7 and 24, shfl/unshfl/shfli/unshfli with controls other than 15, xperm.h, packu,
  bfp, cmix/cmov/fsl/fsr/fsri, crc32.b/h/w, crc32c.b/h/w), written from
  tools/specs/riscv-bitmanip/texsrc/bext.tex (sections "Pack two words in one register", "Shift
  Ones", "Generalized Reverse", "Generalized Shuffle", "Crossbar Permutation Instructions",
  "Generalized OR-Combine", "Bit-Field Place", "CRC Instructions", "Ternary Bit-Manipulation
  Instructions") with the rendered reference code in bitmanip-draft.pdf, and cross-checked against
  the rtl/ibex_alu.sv comment blocks (never against the RTL nets). Consumes the RVFI transaction
  (insn, rs1/rs2/rs3 rdata) and predicts rd_wdata; also applied to pack/packh/xperm.n/xperm.b/
  zext.h/rev8/orc.b/zip/unzip as a cross-check of gen_isa_compare. Must carry the legalization
  note that gen_isa_compare skips these encodings (Spike traps on them) and that the lenient
  reserved-bit forms (F-BIT-037) are modelled as don't-care bits (open question OQ-4). Fails via
  uvm_error; plusarg +gen_chk_bitmanip_ref_en=0.
- gen_chk_timing_isa: retire-to-retire cycle-delta checker at the RVFI boundary. Inputs: RVFI
  stream (rvfi_ext_mcycle per retirement), ibus monitor fetch_stall flag, dbus monitor wb_busy
  flag, TB CSR model (data_ind_timing). Rules: single-cycle ALU/mul/bfp -> delta 1; mulh-class,
  rol/ror/rori, cmov/cmix/fsl/fsr/fsri, crc32* -> delta 2; div/rem non-zero divisor -> 37;
  div/rem by zero -> 2 (DIT = 0) or 37 (DIT = 1); taken branch/jal/jalr/fence.i -> 2, not-taken
  branch -> 1 (DIT = 0) or 2 (DIT = 1); the delta is measured from the previous retirement
  (rvfi_ext_mcycle is captured when the instruction leaves ID) and equality is checked only when
  gap_clean (fetch_stall == 0, dummy_instr_en == 0 over the gap, no mcycle/mcycleh/mcountinhibit
  write in the gap, icache_enable == 0) and wb_busy == 0, otherwise delta >= expected. Expected
  constants derive from the RTL FSM (37;
  doc mismatch D7) and are named once in gen_tb_pkg. Fails via uvm_error; plusarg
  +gen_chk_timing_isa_en=0.
- gen_chk_zcmp_seq: Zcmp micro-op sequence checker. From the first rvfi_ext_expanded_insn_valid
  of a PC it predicts the full micro-op list (store/load register order highest-first, addresses
  sp-4k / sp+stack_adj-4k with stack_adj from rlist/spimm per zcmp.adoc, the addi sp, li a0, ret,
  the two moves) and checks each retired micro-op (rvfi_insn synthesized word, rvfi_rs2_addr /
  rvfi_rd_addr, rvfi_mem_addr, tags: expanded_valid on all, _last only on the final one,
  intermediate pc_wdata == pc_rdata), the COMMIT rule (no rvfi_intr/debug entry between a COMMIT
  micro-op and the LAST one), the abandon rule (after an interrupt or fault mid-sequence sp is
  unchanged, and the next execution of that PC restarts from micro-op 0), and the micro-op count.
  Needed because the ISA model folds micro-ops into one step (feature-list question 8) and the
  memory order is RTL-defined. Fails via uvm_error; plusarg +gen_chk_zcmp_seq_en=0.

- gen_sva_multdiv: SVA module bound into ibex_multdiv_fast (probe candidate, coverage/assertion only;
  no checker depends on it): assert (div_en_i == 0 && md_state_q != MD_IDLE) |=> $stable(md_state_q)
  and cover the antecedent. The cover is expected to stay unhit (gen_hierarchy_map.md H-D3, believed
  unreachable) and a hit is reported as a reachability finding, not counted as coverage. Needed by
  TP-MUL-030 (F-MUL-028). Fails via uvm_error on the assertion; plusarg +gen_sva_multdiv_en=0.

## Open questions

- OQ-1 (D numbering) - RESOLVED: README_FIX_BRIEF rule 5 makes D7 (divide latency, 37 total per
  RTL) and D8 (bfp single-cycle) canonical; the labels of TP-MUL-012 and TP-BIT-030 stand.
- OQ-2 (riscv-dv adoption) - policy applied per the Critic pre-review S-9: this subagent did not
  read vendor/google_riscv-dv/**; every partition was derived from the ISA text and every CSV row
  has adopted = 0. The six partitions the Critic found identical to riscv_instr_cover_group.sv
  coverpoints (cp_sign_pair in CG-ISA-002/CG-MUL-001/CG-MUL-003 = cp_sign_cross; cp_taken in
  CG-ISA-007 = cp_branch_hit; CG-BIT-001.cp_eq_operands for min/max = cp_rs1_eq_rs2;
  CG-CMP-001.cp_reg3 = the compressed gpr[] bins; CG-BIT-004.cp_grev_ctrl/cp_shfl_ctrl =
  reverse_mode/shuffle_mode) carry "Adopted (riscv-dv): partition identical to ..., independently
  derived from the ISA text" in fcov_isa.md. Open for the DV Lead: record the policy (identical
  partitions independently derived count as spec-derived) in the folded plan; the riscv-dv
  partitions this plan does NOT have (rotate/bit-location/bfp 0..31 value ranges, cp_logical
  similarity, instr_trans sequences) are candidates for CG-ADOPT-* in the xcut part.
- OQ-3 (gen_isa_compare fold rule and skip list). The ISA comparator must (a) fold Zcmp micro-ops
  into one architectural step keyed on rvfi_ext_expanded_insn_last while comparing each memory
  access individually, (b) mask rvfi_pc_wdata bit 0 for jalr-family (except in TP-BTALU-008 where
  the unmasked rule is the point), (c) skip the draft Zb* encodings, the lenient reserved-bit
  forms and the srli/srai bit patterns with instr[26] = 1 that decode as fsri (F-ISA-012,
  TP-ISA-012), handing them to gen_chk_bitmanip_ref. Blocks: TP-CMP-039..069, TP-ISA-019, TP-BIT-011/
  016/022..033/037. Recommended default: implement (a)-(c) as named legalization rules in the shim
  with a per-rule plusarg so each can be disabled for mutation evidence.
- OQ-4 (F-BIT-037 leniency). Are non-canonical instr[26:25]/[25] bits for sloi/sroi/grevi/gorci/
  shfli/unshfli accepted don't-cares or illegal-decode gaps? Blocks: the Expected of TP-BIT-037
  (currently pass, RTL-defined) and whether Phase-2 generation may emit them. Recommended default:
  cover them as "executes" (TP-BIT-037), generate only canonical encodings for positive tests,
  and log the leniency as a design note; if the owner rules them illegal, TP-BIT-037 becomes
  expected-fail with a new bug id.
- OQ-5 (B14) - RESOLVED by gen_bug_log.md B14 / gen_tb_architecture.md 8.1 item 5: B14 is an
  RVFI convention note pending its confirmation simulation. TP-ISA-050 (pass) owns the priority
  behaviour (WB error outranks the ID exception; the killed ID instruction re-executes and produces
  its own record later) and TP-ISA-051 is `informational (B14 confirmation; excluded from the pass
  gate)` with the two-trap-records-in-order fire-check; one record for the pair re-opens B14.
- OQ-6 (probe P1 for B8). The CG-CMP-008 dummy_inserted / dummy_ls / dummy_commit bins are
  probe-gated (P1), not in any manifest, until the probe register carries P1 (gen_tb_architecture.md
  8.3 item 5). TP-CMP-065's fire-check is boundary-derived meanwhile (insertion count = minstret
  delta minus RVFI retirements, which relies on dummies being counted in minstret, bug candidate
  B7; if B7 is fixed first the count moves to P1) and its manifest bins are the boundary-derived
  CG-CMP-006.cp_dummy_en.on / cr_insn_dummy. Blocks: nothing for the plan; the probe decision
  turns the three probe-gated bins into must-hit bins. Recommended default: accept P1 as a
  wrapper-internal observation (tb-infra section 9 notes it is an ibex_core port), register it, and
  keep dummy_instr_en = 0 in every other Zcmp item until B8 is ruled.
- OQ-7 (divide latency constant). gen_chk_timing_isa expects 37 cycles (RTL FSM) against
  pipeline_details.rst's 38. Blocks: the constant in gen_tb_pkg. Recommended default: 37, confirmed
  on the first TP-MUL-012 run; log D7.
- OQ-8 (Spike misa/zicntr string for Zb*). The Spike ISA string must be rv32imc_zicsr_zifencei_
  zba_zbb_zbc_zbs_zbkb_zbkx(+zcb+zcmp) so pack/packh/brev8/zip/unzip/xperm4/xperm8 compare in
  Spike; if the pinned Spike lacks Zbkb/Zbkx those rows move to gen_chk_bitmanip_ref. Blocks:
  Pass criteria of TP-BIT-011/024/025/026 and TP-BIT-001. Recommended default: probe the pinned
  Spike once at shim build; route any missing extension to gen_chk_bitmanip_ref and record it.
- OQ-9 (gen_sva_multdiv bind). TP-MUL-030 needs a bind into ibex_multdiv_fast (md_state_q,
  div_en_i) - a probe-register entry, coverage/assertion only. Blocks: whether TP-MUL-030 can run
  in the first regression with its SVA fire-check. Recommended default: register the bind as a
  probe candidate next to P1; if rejected, TP-MUL-030 keeps its RVFI fire-check and drops
  CG-MUL-005.cp_sva_checked (ignore_bins, reason "probe rejected").


# 4.2 Areas CSR, PRV: Control and status registers; privilege modes M/U and mstatus semantics


T-006 subagent output for the DV Lead. Areas: CSR (F-CSR-001..103) and PRV (F-PRV-001..035).
Feature source: dv/auto_dv/work/dv-lead/parts/gen_part_csr.md (Implemented CSR map and features).
Companion coverage file: fcov_csr.md. Traceability: trace_feat_tp_csr.csv, trace_tp_bin_csr.csv.

Conventions used in every item
- Programs enter through the fetch bus (gen instruction-memory agent), data through the data bus,
  interrupts / debug / hart_id_i / boot_addr_i / mcounteren_writable_i through pins. All
  programmable state (privilege, CSR fields, PMP, counters, dcsr) is set by CSR instructions in
  the test program and randomized; U-mode is entered by mret with MPP=U, left by ecall or another
  trap.
- "Read-back" = rvfi_rd_wdata of the csrr that follows the write (ibex_core has no rvfi_csr_*
  ports). gen_chk_csr_readback predicts the value after WARL legalisation; gen_isa_compare checks
  pc/insn/trap/rd/mem/mode per retirement and the trap contract (mcause 2, mtval = encoding).
- "Trap seen" = rvfi_trap = 1 on the offending instruction plus the handler's csrr of mcause /
  mtval / mepc; the handler is part of the generated program and writes the values to a data-bus
  signature area the cocotb test reads back.
- Per-transaction distributions are stated in Stimulus; regime knobs by name; the regime schedule
  is owned by the cross-cutting subagent.
- Doc-mismatch items follow the RTL and are `pass (doc mismatch D<n>)` with the canonical D-numbers
  of dv/auto_dv/docs/gen_bug_log.md (D1 mip reads raw pins, D2 illegal MPP -> U, D3 mcause
  software-writable, D4 tdata1 reset 0x2800_1048, D12 trigger CSRs readable in M-mode); bug
  candidates follow the specification and are `expected-fail (B<n>)` (B1, B2, B3, B15). Rulings
  applied (gen_bug_log.md; gen_tb_architecture.md 8.1 item 5): B6 (exception in debug mode forces
  priv M) is RTL-defined, Sdext.adoc:51 leaves it UNSPECIFIED, the touching items expect `pass
  (RTL-defined, spec UNSPECIFIED)`; B12 (mret clears sync_exc_seen) is documented behaviour
  (cs_registers.rst:556, exception_interrupts.rst:191), TP-CSR-094 expects pass and carries a
  design-weakness note for the security owner; B5 (dcsr.nmip) has ONE owner item, TP-DBG-021, and
  every dcsr compare here excludes bit 3; B15 (dcsr.ebreaks): the checker predicts bit 13 = 0
  (core_registers.xml:163-172), the dcsr writable mask is DCSR_W_MASK = 0x9007 (ebreakm, ebreaku,
  step, prv), items that write bit 13 = 1 are expected-fail (B15) and pass items never set bit 13;
  B3: the checker follows Sdtrig (reads of tdata3/mcontext/scontext/mscontext trap), only
  TP-CSR-083 exercises them (expected-fail). Feature IDs cited below may be ALIAS or FOLDED in
  gen_part_csr.md; traceability resolves them to the canonical ID.
- S-2 (rtl/ibex_core.sv:1885-1886): rvfi_trap is 0 on an ebreak that enters debug mode. The debug
  path is identified by is_ebreak(rvfi_insn) && !rvfi_trap && next fetch (instr_addr_o / next
  rvfi_pc_rdata) == DmHaltAddr; the exception path by rvfi_trap = 1. An ebreak executed inside
  debug mode is not an exception: it re-enters the debug ROM at DmHaltAddr without any CSR save
  (rtl/ibex_controller.sv:874-882). An ebreak-into-debug record is not counted in minstret.
- core_busy_o is ibex_mubi_t, not a bit: sleep is observed as core_busy_o == IbexMuBiOff, which in
  WAIT_SLEEP holds only while no instruction-bus beat is outstanding, no icache invalidation is
  active and the LSU is idle (gen_tb_architecture.md 8.2 item 1); fire-checks that need the dip
  run the wfi with the fetch agent idle (no outstanding beat) and no invalidation pending.
- Fire-checks are per-seed assertions on an observable; regression-wide bin closure is the
  coverage plan's job (fcov_csr.md), never a fire-check.
- Parameter-derived constants (ibex_pkg / wrapper parameters; the literals in parentheses are this
  build's values): HPM_IDX = 3..2+MHPMCounterNum (3..12); HPM_UNIMPL_IDX = 3+MHPMCounterNum..31
  (13..31); CTR_MASK = ((1 << (3 + MHPMCounterNum)) - 1) & ~(1 << 1) (0x1FFD, mcounteren and
  mcountinhibit implemented bits); MIE_MASK = (((1 << $bits(irq_fast_i)) - 1) << 16) | 0x888
  (0x7FFF_0888); NUM_IRQ_LINES = 3 + $bits(irq_fast_i) (18); fast ids 0..$bits(irq_fast_i)-1
  (0..14); DCSR_W_MASK = 0x9007 (above); PMP CSRs pmpcfg0..PMPNumRegions/4-1 and
  pmpaddr0..PMPNumRegions-1.

## Layer-1 weight tables (per-transaction distributions)

Every Stimulus line that lists operand classes without explicit weights draws them from these
tables (DV_prompt Section 6, layer 1); an inline weight in an item overrides the table for that
item only. Classes that do not apply to the addressed CSR are dropped and the rest renormalised.

| Table | Operand class | Weights (percent) |
|---|---|---|
| W-OP | CSR op {csrrw, csrrs, csrrc, csrrwi, csrrsi, csrrci} | 25 / 20 / 20 / 15 / 10 / 10 |
| W-FORM | op form {write form, demoted read (rs1 = x0 or uimm = 0)} | 70 / 30 (read-centred items 30 / 70) |
| W-PAT | write pattern {rand, legal_only, illegal_only, all1, all0, msb_only, near_wrap, small, walking-one} | 30 / 15 / 15 / 10 / 10 / 5 / 5 / 5 / 5 |
| W-REG | rd {x0, x1..x15, x16..x31} 10 / 45 / 45; rs1 register (write forms) {x1..x15, x16..x31} 50 / 50; rs1 value {0, all-ones, single bit, uniform} | 10 / 10 / 20 / 60 |
| W-UIMM | uimm {0, 1, 2..30, 31} | 15 / 15 / 55 / 15 |
| W-ADDR | random CSR address class {rw_m, wi_m, trig, pmp, dbg_only, info_ro, alias_impl, alias_unimpl, time, s_lvl, cheriot, hole_lo, hole_m, hole_ro} | 30 / 8 / 5 / 12 / 4 / 6 / 8 / 3 / 2 / 2 / 3 / 6 / 8 / 3 |
| W-PRIV | privilege of the accessing code {M, U} | 60 / 40 (U-mode items 20 / 80) |
| W-IRQ | irq line {software, timer, external, fast} | 15 / 15 / 20 / 50, the fast share uniform over the $bits(irq_fast_i) lines |
| W-DBGC | debug entry cause {haltreq, ebreakm/ebreaku, step, trigger} | 40 / 30 / 15 / 15 |
| W-GAP | distance between a write and its dependent instruction {0, 1, 2..4, 5..16} | 40 / 30 / 20 / 10 |
| W-EXC | synchronous exception kind {ecall, ebreak (ebreakm/u = 0), illegal opcode, illegal CSR, load/store bus fault, load/store PMP fault, fetch fault} | 20 / 10 / 15 / 20 / 15 / 10 / 10 |
| W-FILL | filler between the instructions of a sequence {none, 1 ALU, 2..4 ALU/branch, load/store} | 40 / 25 / 25 / 10 |

- CSR op set = {csrrw, csrrs, csrrc, csrrwi, csrrsi, csrrci}; "write forms" exclude the demoted
  csrrs/csrrc x0 and csrrsi/csrrci uimm=0 reads; "rd=x0 form" = csrrw/csrrwi with rd = x0.

### TP-CSR-001: CSR operation classes and single-cycle read-modify-write on RW CSRs
- Features: F-CSR-001, F-CSR-100
- Phase: 1
- Tier: smoke
- Preconditions: M-mode; target CSR pre-loaded by csrrw with a random value.
- Stimulus: for each of mscratch, mtval, mepc, mie, mcountinhibit, mcounteren (gate On), pmpaddr[k], dscratch0/1 (in debug mode) run sequences <op> rd, csr, src ; csrr rd2, csr with op uniformly over the 6 ops, src register uniform over x1..x31 with random 32-bit content, uimm uniform 0..31 (nonzero for set/clear), rd uniform over x1..x31; 200 sequences per seed. Weights: per the Layer-1 weight tables unless stated.
- Randomized: op, operand value, rd/rs1 registers, CSR choice, interleaved unrelated ALU/branch instructions (0..4) between the two CSR instructions, knob-driven memory latency.
- Knobs: knob:instr_mix, knob:imem_gnt_delay, knob:imem_rvalid_delay
- Fire-check: every op class appears at least once on RVFI (rvfi_insn funct3 in {1,2,3,5,6,7}) with rvfi_trap = 0, and rvfi_rd_wdata of the op equals the CSR value before the op (pre-write value).
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_csr_readback (read-back == predicted rdata OP operand after legalisation); gen_isa_compare (rd write of the pre-write value)
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_csr_access

### TP-CSR-006: CSR write causes a pipeline flush; the next instruction observes the new state
- Features: F-CSR-006
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: M-mode; irq pin (random one of sw/timer/ext/fast) driven high with mie bit set and mstatus.MIE = 0 for the MIE case; PMP region prepared for the PMP case; icache enabled/disabled for the cpuctrlsts case.
- Stimulus: write-then-dependent pairs: (a) csrrsi mstatus, 8 followed by an ALU op (interrupt must be taken first); (b) csrrw mie then wfi; (c) csrrw mcountinhibit then csrr mcycle; (d) csrrw mtvec then ecall; (e) csrrw pmpcfg then a load into the newly denied region; (f) csrrw cpuctrlsts (icache_enable toggle) then a jump; each 20 times per seed with random operands in the legal class. Weights: per the Layer-1 weight tables unless stated.
- Randomized: which pair, operand values, irq line, distance to the next instruction (0 = adjacent), memory latencies.
- Knobs: knob:irq_regime, knob:imem_rvalid_delay, knob:dmem_gnt_delay
- Fire-check: retirement gap after the write >= 2 cycles (FLUSH); for (a) rvfi_intr on the next retirement with no instruction between; for (e) rvfi_trap on the load; for (c) the mcycle read-back equals the frozen value.
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_csr_flush (bubble present for flushing CSRs); gen_chk_irq (interrupt taken before the next instruction); gen_chk_pmp; gen_chk_counters; gen_chk_icache
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_csr_ordering
- Bins: CG-CSR-012.cr_fam_next.other_alu, CG-CSR-012.cr_fam_next.other_irq_taken, CG-CSR-012.cr_fam_next.other_wfi, CG-CSR-012.cr_fam_next.other_csr_rd_other, CG-CSR-012.cr_fam_next.other_load_store, CG-CSR-012.cr_fam_next.other_branch_jump, CG-CSR-012.cr_fam_next.other_ecall, CG-CSR-012.cr_fam_gap.other_g2_3, CG-CSR-012.cr_enable_next.enables_irq_taken

### TP-CSR-007: mscratch and mepc writes do not flush; back-to-back write/read is coherent

### TP-CSR-008: CSR write in ID is cancelled when the instruction in WB raises a load/store error
- Features: F-CSR-008
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: M-mode; data agent armed to return data_err_i on a chosen load/store address (50%) or a PMP region denying that address (50%); CSR pre-loaded with a known value; handler returns to the CSR instruction (mepc + 4 skip of the faulting access is NOT done: handler re-executes from mepc after fixing the PMP / disarming the error, or skips the access with mepc += 4 for the bus-error variant).
- Stimulus: lw/sw to the faulting address immediately followed by a CSR write op (uniform over 6 ops) to a random RW CSR (mscratch, mie, mtval, mcountinhibit, mepc excluded); 40 per seed. Weights: per the Layer-1 weight tables unless stated.
- Randomized: load vs store, error source (bus vs PMP), CSR, op, operand, alignment of the access (aligned / misaligned).

- Fire-check: rvfi_trap on the load/store with mepc read in the handler == its PC; the CSR instruction has no RVFI retirement before the handler entry and retires after mret (rvfi_order increasing); the handler's csrr of the CSR returns the pre-load value.
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_csr_readback (CSR unchanged inside the handler, updated after re-execution); gen_isa_compare (trap on the memory instruction, mepc = pc_wb); gen_chk_dbus_proto
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_csr_ordering
- Bins: CG-CSR-015.cr_cause_fam.lsu_err_flush, CG-CSR-015.cr_cause_fam.lsu_pmp_flush, CG-CSR-015.cr_cause_fam.lsu_err_mscratch, CG-CSR-015.cr_cause_reexec.lsu_err_yes, CG-CSR-015.cr_cause_reexec.lsu_err_no, CG-CSR-015.cr_cause_reexec.lsu_pmp_yes, CG-CSR-015.cr_cause_op.lsu_err_csrrw, CG-CSR-015.cr_cause_op.lsu_err_csrrs, CG-CSR-015.cr_cause_op.lsu_err_csrrc, CG-CSR-015.cr_cause_op.lsu_err_csrrwi, CG-CSR-015.cp_op.csrrsi

### TP-CSR-017: Debug-only CSRs trap outside debug mode and are RW inside it
- Features: F-CSR-017
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: M-mode program; debug_req_i asserted by the TB at a random point; debug ROM code at DmHaltAddr performs the in-debug accesses.
- Stimulus: outside debug: read and write forms to dcsr, dpc, dscratch0, dscratch1 (uniform over 6 ops), 40 per seed, each trapping; inside debug (after debug_req_i): csrrw/csrrs/csrrc/csrrwi/csrrsi/csrrci with random values to the same four CSRs followed by csrr; dret; repeat 3 entries per seed; control: demoted reads and write forms of tselect, tdata1, tdata2 (0x7A0..0x7A2) outside debug mode, which must NOT trap (doc defect D12: debug.rst:54-55 claims they do; the write-ignored behaviour is checked in TP-CSR-080/081/082/084). Weights: per the Layer-1 weight tables unless stated.
- Randomized: op, values, which CSR, debug entry point, order of the four.
- Knobs: knob:debug_req_regime
- Fire-check: rvfi_trap = 1 with rvfi_ext_debug_mode = 0 for the outside accesses (mcause 2, mtval = encoding); rvfi_trap = 0 with rvfi_ext_debug_mode = 1 for the inside accesses and read-back equals the legalised prediction; the tselect/tdata1/tdata2 controls retire outside debug mode with rvfi_trap = 0.
- Pass criteria: gen_isa_compare (outside traps for 0x7B0..0x7B3 only; no trap for 0x7A0..0x7A2); gen_chk_csr_readback (dcsr/dpc/dscratch WARL inside debug); gen_chk_debug (entry/exit)
- Expected: pass (doc mismatch D12)

### TP-CSR-031: mie write is visible to irq_pending_o and to WFI wake on the next cycle
- Features: F-CSR-031
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: M-mode, MIE = 0 (wake without trap) in half the seeds, MIE = 1 in the other half; one random irq pin held high by the TB.
- Stimulus: (a) csrrs mie, <bit of the high pin> ; csrr mie ; then an ALU marker: irq_pending_o must rise the cycle after the write commits; (b) wfi with the pin high but mie bit clear, then the TB observes sleep, then raises debug_req_i / another enabled pin to end it (wake by disabled pin must not happen); (c) csrrc mie, <bit> in the cycle window where the pin rises (TB raises the pin 0..3 cycles around the write retirement): no interrupt taken when the bit is cleared first, and every (c) write is followed by csrr mie (the read-back the fire-check compares); 40 rounds per seed. Weights: per the Layer-1 weight tables unless stated.
- Randomized: pin, MIE, timing offset of the pin edge, op form.
- Knobs: knob:irq_hold, knob:irq_line_mix
- Fire-check: (a) irq_pending_o edge within 2 cycles after the mie write retirement; (b) core_busy_o == IbexMuBiOff for >= 8 cycles with the disabled pin high, then wake by the enabled source; (c) rvfi_intr present iff the read-back of mie still has the bit set.
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_irq (irq_pending_o == |(pins & mie) every cycle); gen_chk_sleep (no wake by a disabled pin); gen_isa_compare
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_csr_trap_setup
- Bins: CG-CSR-012.cr_fam_next.other_wfi, CG-CSR-012.cr_enable_next.none_alu, CG-PRV-005.cr_dis_irq.dis_then_irq_en, CG-PRV-005.cr_dis_irq.dis_then_dbg, CG-PRV-005.cr_len_wake.long_irq_en, CG-PRV-005.cr_len_wake.short_irq_en, CG-CSR-002.cr_mie_w_op.std_csrrs, CG-CSR-002.cr_mie_w_op.std_csrrc

### TP-CSR-074: dcsr: debug-only RW register with WARL fields; random write and read-back in debug mode
- Features: F-CSR-074
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: debug mode via debug_req_i; debug ROM program at DmHaltAddr does the accesses; TB reads results from the signature area.
- Stimulus: 6 ops with rand/legal_only (DCSR_W_MASK bits 15, 12, 2, 1:0)/illegal_only (read-only bits other than 13)/all0 operands to dcsr, every operand with bit 13 forced 0 (bit 13 = 1 and the all-ones pattern belong to TP-CSR-075/076, expected-fail B15), each followed by csrr dcsr; step and ebreak bits are restored to 0 before dret so the program flow stays deterministic; 120 pairs per seed over 4 debug entries. Weights: per the Layer-1 weight tables unless stated.

- Knobs: knob:debug_req_regime
- Fire-check: pairs in debug mode (rvfi_ext_debug_mode = 1) for every op and pattern; read-back == 0x4000_0000 | (w & DCSR_W_MASK & ~0x3) | (prv legalised) | (cause preserved), with bit 13 == 0 and bit 3 (nmip) excluded from the compare.
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_csr_readback (dcsr WARL with the spec-side prediction: bit 13 predicted 0 (B15) and never written 1 here, so the item passes on current RTL; bit 3 nmip excluded from the compare, owner TP-DBG-021 (B5)); gen_chk_debug
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_csr_debug_csr

### TP-CSR-075: dcsr write of all-ones must read back 0x4000_9007 | (cause << 6) (bit 13 forced 0); current RTL returns 0x4000_B007 (B15)
- Features: F-CSR-075
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: debug mode; the entry cause (haltreq 3, ebreak 1, step 4, trigger 2) is known to the TB from the entry stimulus.
- Stimulus: csrrw dcsr, -1 ; csrr ; csrrs dcsr, -1 ; csrr ; then restore dcsr to the legal pre-entry value; 4 entries per seed with different causes. Weights: per the Layer-1 weight tables unless stated.
- Randomized: cause of entry, order, rd.
- Knobs: knob:debug_req_regime
- Fire-check: the all-ones write and set pairs retire in debug mode (rvfi_ext_debug_mode = 1, rvfi_trap = 0) with the read-back pairs closed and cause matching the entry stimulus; prv == 11 (M) after all-ones; bit 3 (nmip) excluded from the compare (B5, owner TP-DBG-021).
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_csr_readback predicting 0x4000_9007 | (cause << 6) (bit 13 = 0 per core_registers.xml:163-172) - fails on current RTL, which returns 0x4000_B007 | (cause << 6) (rtl/ibex_cs_registers.sv:810-836); the all-ones legalisation of every other field is guarded by TP-CSR-074 (patterns with bit 13 cleared), so this expected-fail masks no other regression; gen_chk_debug (cause) - passes
- Expected: expected-fail (B15)
- Test group: gen_csr_debug_csr
- Bins: CG-CSR-007.cr_csr_wpat_dbg.dcsr_all1, CG-CSR-007.cr_dcsr_bits.all1, CG-CSR-007.cr_prv_w_op.prv_m_csrrw, CG-PRV-007.cp_cause.haltreq, CG-PRV-007.cp_cause.ebreak, CG-PRV-007.cp_cause.step, CG-PRV-007.cp_cause.trigger

### TP-CSR-076: dcsr.ebreaks (bit 13) must read 0 without S-mode; current RTL stores it (B15)
- Features: F-CSR-076
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: debug mode.
- Stimulus: csrrs dcsr, 0x2000 ; csrr ; csrrc dcsr, 0x2000 ; csrr ; csrrw with bit 13 alone; 20 rounds per seed; then dret and an ebreak in M/U to show no functional effect (ebreak behaviour per ebreakm/ebreaku only). Weights: per the Layer-1 weight tables unless stated.
- Randomized: op, other bits, round order.
- Knobs: knob:debug_req_regime
- Fire-check: RVFI shows the bit-13 set/clear/write pairs retiring in debug mode (rvfi_ext_debug_mode = 1, rvfi_trap = 0) with the read-back pairs closed; the following ebreak outside debug traps (rvfi_trap = 1, mcause 3) or enters debug (rvfi_trap = 0, next fetch == DmHaltAddr, S-2) according to ebreakm/ebreaku only.
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_csr_readback with the B15 spec expectation (tools/specs/riscv-debug-spec/xml/core_registers.xml:163-172: ebreaks is hardwired to 0 when the hart has no S-mode, so read-back bit 13 == 0 after every write) - fails on current RTL, which stores the bit (rtl/ibex_cs_registers.sv:811-835); gen_chk_debug (ebreak behaviour independent of bit 13; functional impact nil, rtl/ibex_controller.sv:481-483) - passes
- Expected: expected-fail (B15)
- Test group: gen_csr_debug_csr
- Bins: CG-CSR-007.cr_dcsr_bits.ebreaks_only, CG-CSR-007.cp_dcsr_ebreaks_w.b1, CG-CSR-007.cp_dcsr_ebreaks_w.b0, CG-CSR-007.cr_csr_op_dbg.dcsr_csrrs, CG-CSR-007.cr_csr_op_dbg.dcsr_csrrc

### TP-CSR-083: tdata3, mcontext, mscontext, scontext read 0 and ignore writes in M; U-mode access traps

- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: M-mode, debug mode and U-mode rounds.
- Stimulus: read and write forms (6 ops, all1/rand operands) to 0x7A3, 0x7A8, 0x7AA, 0x5A8 in M-mode and debug mode, followed by csrr; the same in U-mode (all trap); 80 accesses per seed. Weights: per the Layer-1 weight tables unless stated.

### TP-CSR-089: cpuctrlsts.sync_exc_seen set by hardware on a synchronous exception, cleared by mret; double_fault_seen set on a second one
- Features: F-CSR-089

- Knobs: knob:irq_regime, knob:priv_regime, knob:dmem_err_rate
- Fire-check: bit 6 read 1 in every first-level handler and 0 after mret; bit 7 read 1 in every nested handler; double_fault_seen_o pulses exactly once per nested exception and never for the interrupt/NMI rounds.
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_double_fault (pulse vs model); gen_chk_csr_readback (bits 7:6)
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_csr_cpuctrl
- Bins: CG-CSR-009.cr_dbl_detect.sync_s0_set, CG-CSR-009.cr_dbl_detect.sync_s1_pulse, CG-CSR-009.cr_dbl_detect.s1_irq_nopulse, CG-CSR-009.cr_dbl_detect.s1_nmi_nopulse, CG-CSR-009.cr_dbl_detect.mret_clr_s1, CG-CSR-009.cr_dbl_detect.mret_clr_s0, CG-CSR-009.cp_sync_state.s1, CG-CSR-009.cp_dbl_state.d1

### TP-CSR-094: mret from an interrupt handler clears cpuctrlsts.sync_exc_seen (B12: documented behaviour, design-weakness note)
- Features: F-CSR-089, F-PRV-006
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: M-mode with MIE = 1 and one mie bit set; a first-level synchronous exception handler that re-enables MIE (nested interrupts allowed) and spins on a mailbox.
- Stimulus: ecall (bit 6 <- 1); inside the handler csrrsi mstatus, 8; the TB raises the irq; the interrupt handler reads cpuctrlsts, executes mret back into the exception handler; the exception handler reads cpuctrlsts again, then a second ecall (nested) before its own mret; 20 rounds per seed. Weights: per the Layer-1 weight tables unless stated.
- Randomized: irq line, delay before the irq, exception kind.
- Knobs: knob:irq_line_mix, knob:irq_hold
- Fire-check: the interrupt handler reads bit 6 == 1; after the interrupt's mret the exception handler reads bit 6 == 0; the second ecall then produces no double_fault_seen_o pulse and its handler reads bit 7 == 0.
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_double_fault following the documented behaviour (cs_registers.rst:556 and exception_interrupts.rst:191: sync_exc_seen is cleared by any mret, including an interrupt handler's; no RISC-V specification covers double-fault detection) - passes; gen_chk_csr_readback (bit 6 == 0 after the interrupt's mret). Design-weakness note for the security owner (gen_bug_log.md B12, Q-DL-3): an interrupt handler's mret disarms double-fault detection for the enclosing synchronous handler; recorded here, not a pass-gate failure.
- Expected: pass (B12 documented behaviour; design-weakness note for the security owner)
- Test group: gen_csr_cpuctrl
- Bins: CG-CSR-009.cr_dbl_detect.mret_clr_s1, CG-CSR-009.cr_dbl_detect.s1_irq_nopulse, CG-PRV-002.cr_entry.m_mie1_irq, CG-PRV-002.cr_mret.m_1_0

### TP-CSR-102: A trapping CSR instruction never writes; exception entry and software CSR write never coincide

### TP-CSR-110: U-mode access sweep over every implemented M-level CSR and the trigger/debug/custom CSRs
- Features: F-CSR-014, F-CSR-015, F-CSR-017, F-CSR-083, F-CSR-097
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: U-mode entered via mret; handler returns to U after each trap; mcounteren random.
- Stimulus: for every implemented address with csr[9:8] != 00 (every row of the CSR map incl. pmpcfg/pmpaddr, mseccfg, tselect/tdata*, mcontext/mscontext/scontext, dcsr/dpc/dscratch, cpuctrlsts/secureseed, all counters, all machine-info CSRs, mshwm/mshwmb/cdbg_ctrl) one demoted read and one write form; the sweep is split across seeds by a random stride. ### TP-PRV-004: Exceptions taken while in debug mode do not update mstatus/mepc/mcause/mtval or the double-fault flags
- Features: F-PRV-005
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: mstatus/mepc/mcause/mtval/cpuctrlsts loaded with random values, read before debug entry; debug entry via debug_req_i; the debug ROM executes an illegal instruction, an ecall, an illegal CSR access and a faulting load (PMP or bus error) at DmExceptionAddr-safe points, plus an ebreak as a separate case (inside debug mode ebreak is not an exception: it re-enters the debug ROM at DmHaltAddr with no CSR save, rtl/ibex_controller.sv:874-882).
- Stimulus: one debug-mode exception per entry, 5 entries per seed; after dret the program re-reads the five CSRs. Weights: per the Layer-1 weight tables unless stated.
- Randomized: exception kind, pre-loaded values, entry point.
- Knobs: knob:debug_req_regime, knob:dmem_err_rate
- Fire-check: the debug-mode exception retires with rvfi_trap = 1, rvfi_ext_debug_mode = 1 and rvfi_pc_wdata == DmExceptionAddr; the ebreak case retires with rvfi_ext_debug_mode = 1 and next fetch == DmHaltAddr (identified by the fetch address, not by rvfi_trap, whose mask covers ebreak_into_debug only, rtl/ibex_core.sv:1885-1886; S-2); rvfi_mode == 3 for every debug-mode retirement (B6: RTL-defined); post-dret reads equal the pre-entry values; double_fault_seen_o never pulses.
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_debug (DmExceptionAddr, no M-CSR update); gen_chk_csr_readback; gen_chk_double_fault
- Expected: pass (RTL-defined, spec UNSPECIFIED; B6 ruling C-20 for the M privilege of the debug-mode exception)
- Test group: gen_prv_debug
- Bins: CG-PRV-007.cr_exc_dbg.illegal, CG-PRV-007.cr_exc_dbg.ecall, CG-PRV-007.cr_exc_dbg.ebreak, CG-PRV-007.cr_exc_dbg.ls_fault, CG-PRV-007.cr_exc_dbg.csr_illegal, CG-PRV-007.cr_exc_dbg.fetch_fault, CG-PRV-001.cr_trans.dbg_dbg_exc, CG-PRV-008.cr_cause_target.dbg_exc_dm, CG-PRV-007.cp_event.exc_in_dbg, CG-PRV-001.cp_mode_change.same
