## New checkers requested

- gen_chk_csr_flush: observes every retired CSR write op (not demoted, not trapped) and the next
  retirement; asserts a retirement gap >= 2 cycles (FLUSH) for every CSR except mscratch/mepc and
  a gap of exactly 1 cycle for mscratch/mepc when the fetch agent is at min latency and no other
  stall source is active (memory latency, WB drain); also asserts no bubble after a demoted read.
  Used by TP-CSR-002/003/006/007/021/033/093/101/115. Mutation class: csr_pipe_flush condition
  (rtl/ibex_id_stage.sv:593-597).
- gen_sva_csr_excl (probe assertion, DV Lead decision): never (cs_registers_i.csr_we_int &&
  cs_registers_i.csr_save_cause_i). Internal-signal assertion; used only by TP-CSR-102 as a
  witness; no boundary alternative exists because both events are internal to the same cycle.
- gen_chk_csr_readback extension request: the checker must carry the per-CSR WARL model listed in
  fcov_csr.md conventions (mstatus MPP->U rule, mtvec mask, mcause 3-field storage, mcounteren gate
  on the mcounteren_writable_i pin, dcsr writable mask DCSR_W_MASK = 0x9007 (bit 13 predicted 0 per B15; bit 3 nmip excluded from the compare per B5, owner TP-DBG-021) + prv rule + cause preservation, tdata1 bit 2
  only in debug mode, tselect clamp to DbgHwBreakNum-1, cpuctrlsts 0xFF + bit 8 mirror, secureseed
  reads 0, mseccfg sticky rules, pmpcfg/pmpaddr lock rules shared with gen_chk_pmp, counters via
  gen_chk_counters) and the B1/B2/B3/B15 spec-side expectations (B15: dcsr bit 13 always predicted
  0; TP-CSR-074 never writes it, TP-CSR-075/076 write it and are expected-fail; B12 is documented
  behaviour, no switch).
- gen_chk_counters extension request: "write wins over increment in the write cycle" for every
  counter, the minstret/hpm10 speculative-read rule, and the minstret exclusion list (ecall,
  ebreak, the ebreak-into-debug record with rvfi_trap = 0 (S-2), trapping instructions, minstret(h)
  write ops, Zcmp once, dummies per SEC ruling).

## Open questions

- OQ-CSR-1 (B3 ownership): F-CSR-083 covers the same behaviour as F-TRG-008 / B3 (tdata3,
  mcontext, mscontext, scontext read 0 instead of trapping). TP-CSR-083 is marked expected-fail
  (B3) so the checker follows Sdtrig; the TRG area owns the ruling. Blocked: the pass/fail
  expectation of one item. Recommended default: keep expected-fail (B3) in both areas until the
  controller rules; if ruled "RTL-defined, doc-consistent", both flip to pass in one commit.
- OQ-CSR-2 (mcounteren_writable_i regime): the pin is a DUT input with no knob in the list.
  Blocked: how TP-CSR-050/051/052 and the U-mode alias items pick the pin value. Recommended
  default: a per-test TB parameter gen_mcen_gate in {on 70%, off 20%, invalid 10%} printed in the
  config banner; ask the cross-cutting subagent to add knob:mcounteren_writable {on, off, invalid}.
- OQ-CSR-3 (hart_id_i mid-test change): TP-CSR-020 has a directed variant that changes hart_id_i
  while the core runs (RTL reads the pin live). Blocked: whether the TB may change a "static"
  input mid-test. Recommended default: allowed in that one directed test only, changed while the
  core spins on a mailbox; constant within every other test.
- OQ-CSR-4 (secureseed pulse probe): the only observation of the reseed is
  cs_registers_i.dummy_instr_seed_en_o / dummy_instr_seed_o (fcov Probe candidates). Blocked:
  fire-checks of TP-CSR-092/093 and CG-CSR-010.cp_pulse. Recommended default: admit the probe to
  the probe register for fire-check and coverage only; pass criteria stay at the boundary
  (read-back 0, no trap, no flush for demoted forms).
- OQ-CSR-5 (Spike divergences): mie fast bits, mtvec mask, misa constant, mcause storage,
  mcounteren gate, dcsr, custom CSRs and trigger CSRs diverge from upstream Spike (tb-infra c.3).
  Blocked: whether gen_isa_compare masks CSR-derived state or the shim legalises. Recommended
  default: gen_chk_csr_readback is the primary CSR-value checker for every item here;
  gen_isa_compare checks trap/no-trap, rd of reads through the shim legalisation per rtl-arch's
  answers, and masks nothing silently (every mask is listed in the shim's divergence file).
- OQ-CSR-6 (B12 intent): RESOLVED by gen_bug_log.md v1a / Critic pre-review S-1: B12 is documented
  behaviour (cs_registers.rst:556, exception_interrupts.rst:191); TP-CSR-094 expects pass and carries
  the design-weakness note for the security owner (Q-DL-3). No item is blocked.
- OQ-PRV-1 (B2 item placement): TP-PRV-035 duplicates the DBG/PMP-owned B2 reproducer from the
  MPRV side. Blocked: which area's item is the gate item. Recommended default: DBG owns the gate
  item; TP-PRV-035 stays as the MPRV-cross witness and inherits the DBG ruling.
- OQ-PRV-2 (mret-after-reset at PC 0): TP-PRV-008 needs executable memory at address 0. Blocked:
  the TB memory map (gen_tb_pkg constants). Recommended default: reserve a 256-byte U-mode stub at
  address 0 in the memory model for this test only; if address 0 is unmappable, the test writes
  mepc explicitly and the reset-value part is checked by read-back alone.


# 4.3 Areas EXC, IRQ: Synchronous exceptions; interrupts, NMI, WFI, vectoring


Area group EXC + IRQ: F-EXC-001..069, F-IRQ-001..066 (dv/auto_dv/work/dv-lead/parts/
gen_part_exc_irq.md; F-IRQ-066 added in the fix pass after Critic verdict v1). Supporting facts: gen_behaviour_summaries.md CTRL-05..19, CTRL-23,
CTRL-39..44; gen_reading_report.md Section 5 (B5, B6, B12, B14 touch this area) and 6/6a (Q-DL-1,
Q-DL-7, Q-DL-8 defaults). Companion coverage file: fcov_exc_irq.md.

Conventions used in every item
- DUT boundary only: programs enter through the instruction bus (imem agent serving the ELF),
  data through the data bus (dmem agent), interrupts/debug through irq_*_i / irq_nm_i /
  debug_req_i, integrity errors through the *_intg_i bits. CSR state (mtvec, mie, mstatus, PMP,
  dcsr, cpuctrlsts, tselect/tdata*) is programmed by instructions in the test program and is
  randomized per seed; dcsr fields are programmed inside a debug-mode prologue (debug_req_i) when
  a non-reset value is needed.
- "Handler read-back" = the trap handler executes csrr mepc/mcause/mtval/mstatus (and others as
  named) whose results appear on rvfi_rd_wdata; gen_chk_csr_readback compares them with its
  prediction (ibex_core has no rvfi_csr_* ports).
- Exception-side terms: "trap record" = rvfi_valid && rvfi_trap; "vector fetch" = instr_req_o
  with instr_addr_o == {mtvec[31:8], 8'h00} (exceptions) or mtvec base + 4*id (interrupts),
  seen by the ibus monitor. "Interrupt entry" = rvfi_intr on the first handler instruction (or
  an rvfi_ext_irq_valid pulse) with the handler pc.
- Three randomization layers: per-transaction distributions are in Stimulus/Randomized; regime
  knobs are named in Knobs (bins owned by the cross-cutting subagent); the regime schedule is
  owned by the cross-cutting subagent and only referenced.
- Doc-mismatch numbering used in Expected: the canonical D-numbers of the fix brief
  (dv/auto_dv/work/dv-lead/parts/README_FIX_BRIEF.md). Used here: D1 mip reads raw pins
  (cs_registers.rst:246); D2 illegal mstatus.MPP legalises to U (doc says M, :138); D3 mcause
  software-writable (doc marks R, :213); D10 mtval carries the fetch address on an instruction
  access fault (cs_registers.rst:235 says 0); D12 trigger CSRs tselect/tdata* are accessible from
  M-mode (debug.rst:54-55 says Debug Mode only). D5 (dcsr.ebreaks) is RETIRED in favour of bug
  candidate B15 (DBG/CSR areas).
- Bug candidates touching this area (status per dv/auto_dv/docs/gen_bug_log.md): B5 (dcsr.nmip
  hardwired 0; core_registers.xml:292-298) has ONE owner item, TP-DBG-021 (dbg area); TP-IRQ-041
  excludes dcsr bit 3 from its compare and expects pass. B12 (mret from an interrupt handler clears
  sync_exc_seen) is documented behaviour (exception_interrupts.rst:191, cs_registers.rst:556): TP-EXC-056
  expects pass and carries the design-weakness note for the security owner. B14 (RVFI drops the ID trap
  record when a WB error coincides, rtl/ibex_core.sv:1851-1853) is downgraded to an RVFI convention note
  pending its confirmation simulation: TP-EXC-035 carries the priority behaviour (pass) and TP-EXC-065 the
  record confirmation (informational, excluded from the pass gate). B6 (exception in debug mode forces priv
  M) is RTL-defined (Sdext.adoc:32/:51, Critic C-20): TP-EXC-046 expects pass. No item in this file is
  expected-fail.
- S-2: an ebreak that enters debug mode retires with rvfi_trap == 0 (rtl/ibex_core.sv:1885-1886). The
  debug path is is_ebreak(rvfi_insn) && !rvfi_trap && next fetch == DmHaltAddr; the exception path is
  rvfi_trap == 1. Fire-checks here use that rule (TP-EXC-018, TP-EXC-019, TP-EXC-064).
- S-4 timing: with the instruction cache enabled a word can reach ID without an instruction-bus
  transaction, so every fire-check that infers "in ID" or "delivered" from the ibus monitor pins
  cpuctrlsts.icache_enable = 0 in its Preconditions and excludes icache_enable from the random cpuctrlsts
  field set (TP-EXC-015, 034, 035, 040, 062, TP-IRQ-021, 026, 064); redirects are otherwise derived from
  RVFI (rvfi_pc_wdata != pc + len). RVFI-anchored events are back-dated by one cycle (rvfi_valid is one
  flop after WB exit, rtl/ibex_core.sv:1868); commit-to-record offsets are 2 (CSR writes) and 1
  (trap/mret/dret). The interrupt decision cycle N and IRQ_TAKEN N + 1 are defined in fcov_exc_irq.md
  Conventions (CTRL-09: the live pins at N + 1 decide; a one-cycle pulse is never taken).
- core_busy_o port rule (gen_tb_architecture.md 8.2 item 1): in WAIT_SLEEP/SLEEP core_busy_o == Off iff
  no instruction-bus beat is outstanding, no icache invalidation is active and the LSU is idle; otherwise
  the ctrl_busy dip is invisible. WFI items treat "Off not seen" as legal when a fetch beat was outstanding.

## Layer-1 weight tables (per-transaction distributions; items reference them by name)

Phase 2 items draw every per-transaction value from these tables; Phase 1 items name the table when
their Stimulus line does not spell the distribution out. Weights are relative.

| table | operand | distribution |
|---|---|---|
| W-IRQ-LINE | which line rises per event | fast 45 (uniform over $bits(irqs_t.irq_fast) ids), external 20, software 15, timer 15, irq_nm_i 5 (only with knob:irq_line_mix with_nmi) |
| W-IRQ-SET | lines per event | single 70, pair 20, 3..NUM_IRQ_LINES 10 (all-lines set 1 in 50 multi events) |
| W-IRQ-HOLD | hold per event (within knob:irq_hold) | until_taken 60, through_handler 25, pulse 15; pulse width 1 cycle 40, 2 cycles 30, 3..8 cycles 30 |
| W-IRQ-GAP | cycles between events | 0..3 20, 4..31 40, 32..255 30, 256..2047 10 |
| W-MEM-LAT | gnt / rvalid delay per transaction (within the knob class) | 0 or min 40, 1..3 35, 4..15 20, 16..63 5 |
| W-MEM-ERR | error kind per injected error (within knob:*_err_rate) | data_err_i 60, integrity-bit corruption 30 (1 bit 60, 2 bits 25, 3..7 bits 15), instr_err_i 10 |
| W-PRG-EXC | injected exception source per event | illegal encoding 35 (decoder 50, CSR check 30, SYSTEM rs1/rd != 0 10, Zcmp reserved rlist 10), ecall 20, ebreak 15, faulting load/store 20, faulting fetch 10 |
| W-PRG-CSR | trap-related CSR programming per segment | mtvec class boot_init 20 / sw_aligned 50 / sw_legalised 30; mstatus.MIE 0 40 / 1 60; mie all 30 / single 40 / random mask 30; privilege M 60 / U 40; mstatus.TW 0 80 / 1 20 |
| W-PRG-ZCMP | Zcmp form / rlist per sequence | cm.push 35, cm.pop 25, cm.popret 25, cm.popretz 15; rlist 4 15, 5..7 30, 8..11 30, 12..15 25; spimm uniform |
| W-DBG-REQ | debug_req_i events (within knob:debug_req_regime) | pulse 1 cycle 30, held until DmHaltAddr fetch 60, held through the session 10; position uniform over the program |
| W-WFI | WFI placement and sleep length | wfi every 20..200 instructions; wake after 0..2 cycles 15, 3..10 25, 11..100 40, 101..2000 20 |

## Items: EXC

### TP-EXC-001: Instruction access fault from an instruction-bus error response
- Features: F-EXC-003, F-EXC-001, F-EXC-002
- Phase: 1
- Tier: smoke
- Preconditions: privilege M or U (U entered by mret with MPP=U); mtvec left at boot init or written by the program to a random 256-byte-aligned base inside the TB program window (both classes); mstatus.MIE random; PMP off for the program region.
- Stimulus: random legal instruction stream (knob:instr_mix); the test names one instruction address X (random position, word- or half-aligned, 16- or 32-bit instruction); the imem agent returns instr_err_i=1 on the response for the fetch word containing X and normal data otherwise; X is reached sequentially, by a taken branch, by a jump, or as the target of an mret / dret (random). The handler reads mepc/mcause/mtval/mstatus and returns to X+len.
- Randomized: X and its alignment/length, privilege, mtvec class, MIE, control-flow path to X, imem response latency, the instruction bits returned with the error.
- Knobs: knob:imem_rvalid_delay, knob:imem_gnt_delay
- Fire-check: the ibus monitor records an instr_err_i=1 response for the word containing X, RVFI shows a trap record with rvfi_pc_rdata == X, and the next retirement has rvfi_pc_rdata == mtvec base with rvfi_intr == 0 (observable at the instruction bus and RVFI).
- Pass criteria: gen_isa_compare (trap taken iff predicted, next pc == mtvec base, no rvfi_intr); gen_chk_csr_readback (mcause 1, mepc X, mtval X, MPIE<-MIE, MIE<-0, MPP<-priv); gen_chk_ibus_proto

### TP-EXC-002: Instruction access fault from a PMP fetch violation
- Features: F-EXC-004
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: M-mode code programs pmpcfg/pmpaddr so that one program page is executable except for a denied window (U-mode: region without X; M-mode: mseccfg.MML/MMWP with a non-executable region); privilege chosen consistent with the rule; mtvec random class.
- Stimulus: the program enters the denied window by fall-through, taken branch or jump; the imem agent answers every fetch normally (no bus error).

- Pass criteria: gen_isa_compare; gen_chk_pmp (denied fetch => cause 1, mtval = pc); gen_chk_csr_readback
- Expected: pass (doc mismatch D10)

### TP-EXC-034: WB load/store fault kills the younger instruction in ID, which re-executes after mret
- Features: F-EXC-035
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: privilege random; mtvec random class; mscratch initialised; cpuctrlsts.icache_enable = 0 (pinned; excluded from the random cpuctrlsts field set, S-4).
- Stimulus: a faulting load or store (dmem error, response delayed 1..8 cycles) immediately followed by a younger instruction from {ALU op writing a register, csrw mscratch, csrrs mstatus, mret (inside a handler)}; the handler returns to mepc without adjusting it so the pair re-executes with the fault removed.

- Pass criteria: gen_isa_compare (younger not retired, single architectural effect); gen_chk_exc_flush (no data_req_o and no CSR side effect from the killed instruction); gen_chk_csr_readback
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_exc_lsu_fault

### TP-EXC-056: mret from an interrupt handler nested in an exception handler must not disarm detection
- Features: F-EXC-056
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: exception handler with sync_exc_seen == 1 (read back); an enabled interrupt line pending.
- Stimulus: the exception handler sets MIE = 1; the interrupt is taken; its handler reads cpuctrlsts (sync_exc_seen == 1) and executes mret back into the exception handler, which then raises a second synchronous exception.
- Randomized: causes, line, gaps, privilege.
- Knobs: knob:irq_regime
- Fire-check: RVFI sequence trap(sync) -> interrupt entry -> mret -> trap(sync) with no other mret in between, and the cpuctrlsts read-back inside the interrupt handler shows sync_exc_seen == 1 before its mret (observable at RVFI).
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_double_fault following the RTL and the Ibex documentation (exception_interrupts.rst:191, cs_registers.rst:556: sync_exc_seen is cleared by ANY mret, so the nested interrupt's mret disarms detection; no double_fault_seen_o pulse and cpuctrlsts.double_fault_seen == 0 on the second synchronous exception); gen_chk_csr_readback. Design-weakness note for the security owner (B12, documented behaviour, not a bug candidate): an interrupt taken inside a synchronous-exception handler disarms double-fault detection for the rest of that handler.
- Expected: pass (design note B12)
- Test group: gen_exc_double_fault
- Bins: CG-EXC-010.cp_event.mret_irq_in_exc

### TP-EXC-070: WB fault while the core waits to take an interrupt with the fetch stalled (three conditions in one cycle)
- Features: F-EXC-069
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: mstatus.MIE = 1 (or U-mode), one or more mie bits set; mtvec random class.
- Stimulus: a load or store is issued and the imem agent stalls the fetch of the following instruction (gnt delayed or rvalid delayed by 4..16 cycles) so ID empties while WB waits; during the wait the irq driver raises an enabled line (or irq_nm_i, or debug_req_i in the debug variant); the dmem agent then returns the response with data_err_i=1 (latency 1..12) while the line is still high and the fetch is still stalled.
- Randomized: load vs store, which line (single/multi/NMI), imem stall kind and length, dmem latency, privilege, mtvec class.
- Knobs: knob:dmem_rvalid_delay, knob:imem_rvalid_delay, knob:imem_gnt_delay, knob:irq_regime, knob:irq_line_mix, knob:irq_hold
- Fire-check: in the dbus error response cycle the TB asserts all three at once: (1) data_rvalid_i && data_err_i, (2) irq_pending_o == 1 with MIE or U-mode (or irq_nm_i), (3) the ibus monitor has an outstanding fetch without rvalid (or without gnt); then RVFI shows a trap record with mcause 5/7 before any interrupt entry, irq_pending_o stays 1 through the handler, and the interrupt entry (or the debug entry at the handler for the debug variant) follows the handler's mret (observable at both buses, irq_pending_o and RVFI).
- Pass criteria: gen_isa_compare (exception first, then interrupt); gen_chk_irq (irq_pending_o model; entry bound after the mret); gen_chk_csr_readback; gen_chk_debug (debug variant: dpc == mtvec base)
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_exc_priority
- Bins: CG-EXC-013.cr_wb_irq_ibus.wb_ls_fault_wins_irq_enabled_rvalid_pending, CG-EXC-013.cr_wb_irq_ibus.wb_ls_fault_wins_irq_enabled_gnt_pending, CG-EXC-013.cr_wb_irq_ibus.wb_ls_fault_wins_irq_enabled_idle, CG-EXC-013.cr_wb_irq_ibus.wb_ls_fault_wins_nmi_rvalid_pending, CG-EXC-013.cr_wb_irq_ibus.wb_ls_fault_wins_none_rvalid_pending, CG-EXC-013.cr_stage_irq.wb_cause_irq_enabled, CG-EXC-013.cr_stage_irq.wb_cause_nmi, CG-EXC-013.cp_ibus_at_commit.rvalid_pending, CG-EXC-013.cp_ibus_at_commit.gnt_pending, CG-EXC-013.cp_irq_at_commit.irq_enabled, CG-EXC-013.cp_irq_at_commit.nmi, CG-EXC-006.cp_resp_latency.one, CG-EXC-006.cp_resp_latency.short, CG-EXC-006.cp_resp_latency.long

### TP-IRQ-030: Interrupt request withdrawn before it is taken: no spurious trap
- Features: F-IRQ-025
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: MIE = 1 or U-mode; enabled line; mepc/mcause read before and after the window.
- Stimulus: the irq driver produces 1- and 2-cycle pulses swept against the retirement of the last instruction (RVFI back-dated by one cycle, S-4) so that the pulse's LAST high cycle is the decision cycle N: a one-cycle pulse landing on N, or a two-cycle pulse whose first cycle passed with an instruction still in ID and whose second cycle is N; both are low in IRQ_TAKEN N + 1 and are withdrawn (CTRL-09). A two-cycle pulse whose FIRST cycle is N is high at N + 1 and IS taken: those iterations are the control (CG-IRQ-004.cr_pulse_change_outcome.two_stable_taken, TP-IRQ-021). Also pulses during a load wait and during a divide.
- Randomized: pulse width, offset, line, pipeline context, privilege.
- Knobs: knob:irq_hold, knob:dmem_rvalid_delay
- Fire-check: the pin monitor shows a pulse of width 1 or 2 whose last high cycle is a decision cycle (irq_pending_o == 1 with MIE or U-mode, ID empty and WB done per the RVFI/dbus monitors: the rvfi_ext_irq_valid pulse appears at N + 1) and which is low at N + 1; no rvfi_intr within the next 8 cycles, the mepc/mcause read-backs are unchanged, and the ibus monitor shows a fetch bubble of at most one cycle (observable at the irq pins, irq_pending_o, instruction bus and RVFI).
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_irq (entry iff a takeable line is present in the IRQ_TAKEN cycle N + 1; a two-cycle pulse starting at N is taken); gen_isa_compare (no unpredicted entry); gen_chk_csr_readback
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_irq_timing
- Bins: CG-IRQ-004.cp_outcome.withdrawn, CG-IRQ-004.cr_ctx_outcome.id_empty_withdrawn, CG-IRQ-004.cr_ctx_outcome.id_load_wait_withdrawn, CG-IRQ-004.cr_ctx_outcome.id_div_withdrawn, CG-IRQ-004.cr_pulse_change_outcome.one_dropped_all_withdrawn, CG-IRQ-004.cr_pulse_change_outcome.two_dropped_all_withdrawn, CG-IRQ-004.cr_pulse_change_outcome.two_stable_taken, CG-IRQ-004.cp_pulse_width.one, CG-IRQ-004.cp_pulse_width.two, CG-IRQ-004.cp_change_before_taken.dropped_all

### TP-IRQ-078: Debug entry and dret inside the NMI handler keep NMI mode: pending interrupts and a re-asserted NMI stay masked until mret
- Features: F-IRQ-066, F-IRQ-030
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: NMI handler installed at mtvec base + 0x7C; the handler sets mstatus.MIE = 1 and >= 1 mie bit early, then runs a marker loop of random length before its mret; a debug program that reads dcsr/dpc (and writes dcsr.step in variant b) and drets.
- Stimulus: irq_nm_i pulse (NMI taken, handler entered). Inside the handler: (a) debug_req_i asserted, debug program runs, dret; afterwards >= 1 irq_*_i line with its mie bit set is high (already high or rising) and, in half of the iterations, irq_nm_i is re-asserted, all before the handler's mret; (b) as (a) with dcsr.step = 1 written in the debug program so the first handler instruction after dret is single-stepped (second debug entry, second dret); (c) control: the same line set without a debug session (masking by nmi_mode alone, TP-IRQ-037).
- Randomized: position of debug_req_i within the handler, line set (fast/external/software/timer mix), irq_nm_i re-assertion, hold policy, dcsr.prv, debug-program and handler length, imem latency.
- Knobs: knob:debug_req_regime, knob:irq_line_mix, knob:irq_hold
- Fire-check: the debug program's dcsr read-back shows cause == 3 (haltreq) with dpc inside the NMI handler, rvfi_ext_debug_mode falls at the dret, and the pin monitor shows irq_pending_o == 1 (plus irq_nm_i high in the re-assert variant) for >= 1 retired handler instruction after the dret and before the mret; the ibus monitor shows no vector fetch and RVFI no rvfi_intr in that window; the first rvfi_intr follows the mret with mcause 0x8000001F (re-asserted NMI) or the regular cause (observable at the irq pins, irq_pending_o, instruction bus and RVFI).
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_irq (no entry while nmi_mode is set, including after the dret); gen_chk_nmi (nmi_mode held across debug entry and dret; mstack restored by the handler's mret; re-asserted NMI taken only after the mret); gen_chk_debug (entry cause 3 / step, dpc, dret); gen_isa_compare

### TP-IRQ-079: NMI arriving between IRQ_TAKEN and the handler's first retirement pre-empts the interrupt handler (mepc = the interrupt vector)
- Features: F-IRQ-034, F-IRQ-032, F-IRQ-016
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: MIE = 1 or U-mode; mie enables the line; cpuctrlsts.icache_enable = 0 (pinned, S-4); NMI handler that reads mepc/mcause and returns by mret; the interrupt handler reads mcause and acknowledges; imem latency of the vector fetch long enough to open the window (knob:imem_rvalid_delay long, or the vector word held by the agent).
- Stimulus: a regular line rises and is taken (decision N, IRQ_TAKEN N + 1); the irq driver raises irq_nm_i k cycles after the vector instr_req_o with k swept from 0 to the vector's rvalid delay + 1, so the NMI lands (a) while the vector request is outstanding or (b) after the vector word returned but before it enters ID; variant (c): the interrupted code's last store carries a corrupted integrity response draining in WB so the internal NMI is the pre-empting source; control: irq_nm_i raised after the handler's first retirement (ordinary nesting, TP-IRQ-036).
- Randomized: line per W-IRQ-LINE, k, window class, NMI source, privilege, mtvec class, vector-fetch latency.
- Knobs: knob:irq_line_mix, knob:imem_rvalid_delay, knob:imem_gnt_delay, knob:dmem_err_rate
- Fire-check: the ibus monitor shows the vector fetch (base + 4*id) issued and the pin monitor shows irq_nm_i rising after that request and before any retirement at the vector; the next retirement is at base + 0x7C with rvfi_ext_nmi (or rvfi_ext_nmi_int) == 1 and the NMI handler's mepc read-back == base + 4*id (the interrupt vector), mcause read-back in the NMI handler == the NMI cause; after the NMI handler's mret the next retirement is the interrupt vector with rvfi_intr == 0 and the interrupt handler's mcause read-back == the regular cause (restored from mstack) (observable at the instruction bus, irq pins and RVFI).
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_nmi (entry from the vector pc; mstack holds the interrupt's mepc/mcause/mstatus and is restored by the mret); gen_chk_irq (the regular interrupt is not re-taken: MIE == 0 after its entry; the handler runs after the NMI); gen_isa_compare; gen_chk_csr_readback
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_irq_nmi
- Bins: CG-IRQ-013.cp_preempt.nmi_ext, CG-IRQ-013.cp_preempt.nmi_int, CG-IRQ-013.cp_window_pos.vector_req_outstanding, CG-IRQ-013.cp_window_pos.vector_word_in_if, CG-IRQ-013.cr_preempt_pos.nmi_ext_vector_req_outstanding, CG-IRQ-013.cr_preempt_pos.nmi_ext_vector_word_in_if, CG-IRQ-013.cr_preempt_pos.nmi_int_vector_req_outstanding, CG-IRQ-013.cr_preempt_line.nmi_ext_software, CG-IRQ-013.cr_preempt_line.nmi_ext_timer, CG-IRQ-013.cr_preempt_line.nmi_ext_external, CG-IRQ-013.cr_preempt_line.nmi_ext_fast, CG-IRQ-013.cr_preempt_resume.nmi_ext_irq_handler_runs, CG-IRQ-013.cr_preempt_resume.nmi_ext_irq_lost_to_second_entry, CG-IRQ-013.cp_resume.irq_handler_runs, CG-IRQ-013.cp_resume.irq_lost_to_second_entry

### TP-IRQ-080: debug_req_i arriving between IRQ_TAKEN and the handler's first retirement enters debug with dpc = the interrupt vector
- Features: F-IRQ-024, F-IRQ-039, F-IRQ-016

- Tier: targeted

- Stimulus: a regular line is taken; the debug driver asserts debug_req_i k cycles after the vector instr_req_o (k swept over the vector-fetch latency + 1) so the request lands while the vector request is outstanding or while the vector word waits in IF; the line is held or released inside the debug session (random).

- Pass criteria: gen_chk_debug (cause 3, dpc == vector, prv M); gen_chk_irq (no second entry: MIE == 0 in the handler; no entry inside the session); gen_chk_csr_readback; gen_isa_compare
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_irq_debug

## New checkers requested

- gen_chk_trap_timing: cycle bounds for trap commit. ID-stage cause: the vector fetch (instr_req_o
  to mtvec base / DmExceptionAddr) appears exactly one cycle after the trigger when WB is empty,
  else one cycle after the last data_rvalid_i of the outstanding access; WB cause: one cycle after
  the error response; exactly one vector fetch per trap record (exception request flops cleared in
  FLUSH); interrupt wake-to-vector latency after a WFI wake is a constant. Used by TP-EXC-015,
  TP-EXC-062, TP-EXC-071, TP-IRQ-066. gen_chk_irq only bounds interrupt entry; nothing bounds
  exception commit today.
- gen_chk_exc_flush: quietness of killed instructions. Between a WB fault response (or any trap
  commit) and the handler's first data access no data_req_o is issued that is not attributable to
  a retired instruction, and no CSR side effect of the killed ID instruction is visible in the
  read-backs (mscratch/mstatus canaries). Used by TP-EXC-034, TP-EXC-037, TP-EXC-038, TP-EXC-060.
  gen_isa_compare sees RF/memory effects through RVFI but not a spurious bus request.
- Required extensions to inventoried checkers (not new names): gen_chk_irq must (a) sample the
  lines in the IRQ_TAKEN cycle (decision + 1) so a withdrawn request predicts no trap and a late
  higher-priority line predicts the new cause (CTRL-09), (b) model irq_enabled = MIE | (priv == U),
  (c) wait for the WB drain and block during Zcmp INSTR_EXPANDED_COMMIT micro-ops (CTRL-39), (d)
  compare irq_pending_o cycle-exactly (combinational, mie_q updates at the write commit edge).
  gen_chk_nmi must model the single-entry mstack exactly as the RTL (pushed on every trap,
  restored only by mret in nmi_mode; overwritten by a nested trap, F-IRQ-036) and the internal-NMI
  pending flag (set on any corrupted load or store response, cleared only on an entry with
  irq_nm_i low). gen_chk_sleep must accept the nop-path core_busy_o Off pulse (CTRL-42) and the
  >= 4-cycle WFI bubble, and use the wake predicate |(mip & mie) | irq_nm | debug_req | debug_mode
  | step. gen_chk_bus_intg_rsp must treat store-response integrity errors as NMI sources (CTRL-12).

## Open questions

1. Doc-mismatch numbering. RESOLVED by the fix brief's canonical list: D1, D2, D3 and D10 as used
   here are canonical; D12 (trigger CSRs accessible from M-mode) is used by TP-EXC-008; D5 is
   retired in favour of B15 (not in this area). No renumbering is needed when folding the parts.
2. F-IRQ-036 (synchronous exception inside the NMI handler). TP-IRQ-040 is written `pass` with
   gen_chk_nmi modelling the RTL (single-entry mstack, nmi_mode cleared by the first mret), per the
   area's owner-question default. Blocks: whether the item flips to expected-fail (design weakness).
   Recommended default: pass with the RTL model; record as a design note for the security owner.
3. B14: RESOLVED by gen_tb_architecture.md 8.1 item 5 / gen_bug_log.md (downgraded to an RVFI
   convention note pending the confirmation simulation). TP-EXC-035 carries the priority behaviour
   (pass); TP-EXC-065 is the record confirmation (informational, excluded from the pass gate; two
   trap records in order; one record re-opens B14).
4. Q-DL-7 and Q-DL-8 defaults are applied as `pass` with RTL-defined models (TP-EXC-032 second-half
   access after a first-half PMP fault; TP-IRQ-060 trap state advancing while fetch_enable_i is
   Off). Blocks: whether either becomes expected-fail after an owner ruling. Recommended default:
   as recorded (pass, design notes).
5. B5 (dcsr.nmip hardwired 0): RESOLVED per the fix brief S-1: the single owner item is TP-DBG-021
   (dbg area, expected-fail B5); TP-IRQ-041 masks dcsr bit 3 in its compare and expects pass.
6. Edge alignment capability of the irq/debug drivers. TP-IRQ-023, 026, 027, 031, 039, 064,
   TP-EXC-048 and TP-EXC-040 need a pin edge placed in a cycle defined by another agent (scheduled
   data_rvalid_i / error response, ibus delivery of a given word, the trap-decision cycle). Blocks:
   tb-infra driver design (b.5/b.6). Recommended default: the memory agents publish their scheduled
   response cycle one cycle ahead through the bridge and the drivers accept an "align to event +
   offset" transaction; if not available in Phase 1, the drivers sweep random offsets and the
   fire-check bins (same-cycle classes) prove coincidence.
7. Mid-run stimulus changes by the memory agents (TP-EXC-059 storm recovery: the imem agent stops
   erroring the vector word after N re-entries; TP-EXC-039: the dmem agent commits write data even
   when it returns an error). Blocks: agent API. Recommended default: both are boundary stimulus
   choices of the TB equipment and are allowed; no RTL or memory backdoor is involved.
8. Zcmp micro-op position (first/middle/last) and the COMMIT vs EXPANDED phase are derived from the
   cm.* encoding (rlist) plus rvfi_ext_expanded_insn_* and the dbus request count, not from a probe.
   Blocks: nothing if tb-infra confirms rvfi_ext_expanded_insn_valid/last are traced per micro-op
   (a.4). Recommended default: derive from the boundary; fall back to the P4 controller probe
   (coverage-only) only if the DV Lead approves.
9. IRQ_TAKEN-window pre-emption (TP-IRQ-079/080, CG-IRQ-013) needs the vector fetch to be slow enough
   to open the window: the imem agent must be able to delay one specific word (the vector) per
   iteration. Blocks: agent API (same class as Open question 7). Recommended default: allowed as a
   boundary stimulus choice; with the icache enabled the vector may hit, so these items also pin
   cpuctrlsts.icache_enable = 0 through the interrupt handler table's first use.


# 4.4 Areas PMP: Physical memory protection and Smepmp (16 regions, G=0)


Area group PMP; source features dv/auto_dv/work/dv-lead/parts/gen_part_pmp.md; supporting facts gen_behaviour_summaries.md MEM-13 and CTRL-34. DUT: gen_dut_top (ibex_core, opentitan configuration: PMPEnable=1, PMPGranularity=0, PMPNumRegions=16, PMPNumChan=3 (PMP_I on pc_if, PMP_I2 on pc_if+2, PMP_D on data_addr_o), DmBaseAddr=0x1A110000, DmAddrMask=0xFFF, PMP reset values from ibex_pkg).

Conventions used below:
- 'model' = the gen_chk_pmp Smepmp reference model (PMPNumRegions regions, granule 2^(PMPGranularity+2) bytes, TOR/NA4/NAPOT, MML/MMWP/RLB, lock rules, debug-mode DM-window bypass, per-word checking of split accesses) fed from the CSR values tracked by gen_chk_csr_readback; its verdict per access is compared to rvfi_trap (cause 1/5/7 via a csrr mcause in the handler) and to bus activity (data_req_o per word; instr_req_o never gated).
- 'ibus monitor' / 'dbus monitor' = the TB monitors on instr_req_o/instr_addr_o/instr_gnt_i and data_req_o/data_addr_o/data_we_o/data_be_o/data_gnt_i/data_rvalid_i.
- CSR contents are observed with a following csrr whose result appears on rvfi_rd_wdata (ibex_core has no rvfi_csr ports).
- Every item randomizes at three layers: per-transaction distributions (Stimulus), regime knobs (Knobs), and the regime schedule owned by the cross-cutting subagent (referenced by knob name only).
- Feature IDs with Status ALIAS or FOLDED in gen_part_pmp.md (Critic v1 fix) resolve to the canonical / parent ID; items that cite an ALIAS PMP ID also cite the canonical ID (F-EXC-005/006/035, F-PRV-005/007/015, F-DBG-055, F-CSR-024). TP-PMP-073/074 keep expected-fail (B1/B2) against the canonical F-PRV-015 / F-DBG-055.
- Spike (gen_isa_compare) must be configured with pmpregions=PMPNumRegions and granularity 2^(PMPGranularity+2), PMP CSRs zeroed at reset to match ibex_pkg, and the Ibex WARL legalisations (RW=01 -> W=0 under MML=0, pmpcfg bits 6:5 zero, full 32-bit pmpaddr storage, mseccfgh zero) applied in the shim (owner question Q1 default).
- Fix-2 conventions (Critic pre-review T-034): every fire-check is a per-seed assertion on an RVFI/bus observable (never "every bin hit over the regression"); items that infer a prefetch from an ibus grant pin cpuctrlsts.icache_enable = 0 and exclude it from random cpuctrlsts writes (S-4); every debug-mode item that is not a B2 carrier pins mstatus.MPRV = 0 for the debug episode (B1/B2 isolation); the expected-fail items TP-PMP-073/074 own only bins that encode the observed RTL outcome; literals for the region count, top index and granule are written as PMPNumRegions, PMPNumRegions-1/-2 and 2^(PMPGranularity+2); Bins patterns are expanded against the post-ignore bin set of fcov_pmp.md to produce trace_tp_bin_pmp.csv.
- Verified RTL facts the items rely on are listed in fcov_pmp.md Appendix C (CSR flush retains the fetch FIFO; privilege changes always redirect; rvfi_trap = 1 for debug-mode PMP faults; DmHaltAddr/DmExceptionAddr inside the bypassed DM window; NAPOT whole-space encodings have base 0).

### TP-PMP-001: pmpcfg0..pmpcfg(PMPNumRegions/4-1) per-entry packing: write and read back every entry byte
- Features: F-PMP-001
- Phase: 1
- Tier: smoke
- Preconditions: M-mode; mseccfg = 0 (reset); all entries unlocked (L never written 1 in this item).
- Stimulus: Program writes each pmpcfgN (N in 0..PMPNumRegions/4-1) with csrrw of a 32-bit value whose four entry bytes are drawn independently: A uniform over {OFF,TOR,NA4,NAPOT}, RWX uniform over the 8 values, L = 0, bits 6:5 random; each write is followed by csrr pmpcfgN; 8..32 writes per CSR interleaved with random ALU filler and random pmpaddr writes so that entry i is exercised in every byte lane.
- Randomized: values per entry byte, CSR order, write count, filler instructions, seed of the pmpaddr values.
- Knobs: knob:instr_mix csr_heavy, knob:pmp_regime off
- Fire-check: RVFI: csrrw to pmpcfgN retires with rvfi_trap = 0, the following csrr pmpcfgN retires and its rvfi_rd_wdata is compared; every N in 0..PMPNumRegions/4-1 written and every byte lane 0..3 carries a non-zero A at least once (checked by the test-level assertion over the retire trace).
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_csr_readback (predicted WARL-legalised value vs csrr readback on rvfi_rd_wdata); gen_isa_compare (rd value and trap agreement); detects byte-lane swaps, cross-entry write leakage, missing per-entry write enables
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_pmp_csr_warl
- Bins: CG-PMP-001.cp_entry.*, CG-PMP-001.cp_op.csrrw, CG-PMP-001.cp_wr_mode.*, CG-PMP-001.cp_wr_lrwx.*, CG-PMP-001.cp_res_bits.zero, CG-PMP-001.cp_prelock.unlocked, CG-PMP-001.cp_rlb.rlb0, CG-PMP-001.cp_outcome.written, CG-PMP-001.cr_mode_lrwx.*, CG-PMP-004.cr_op_class.csrrw_pmpcfg, CG-PMP-004.cp_class.pmpcfg, CG-PMP-004.cp_op.csrrw, CG-PMP-004.cp_priv.m, CG-PMP-004.cp_dbg.d0, CG-PMP-004.cp_rw.write, CG-PMP-004.cp_trap.none, CG-PMP-004.cr_priv_trap.m_none

### TP-PMP-006: A field: OFF/TOR/NA4/NAPOT all selectable at G=0 and behave as their mode

### TP-PMP-037: NA4/NAPOT entries whose base lies above 4 GiB never match
- Features: F-PMP-039, F-PMP-014
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: Entry with pmpaddr bit 30 and/or 31 set and a mask that does not cover those bits (NA4, or NAPOT with few trailing ones); a second, higher-index region gives a distinguishable default verdict.
- Stimulus: Accesses at the 32-bit alias of the base (pmpaddr[29:0] << 2, the alias range of the NA4 word or of the NAPOT region truncated to 32 bits): first byte, last byte and interior of the alias range, plus the bytes around it; loads/stores/fetches in M and U; the fallback rule is a higher-index matching entry in half the seeds and the default (no match) in the other half.

- Knobs: knob:priv_regime alternating
- Fire-check: RVFI: per seed, every access into the alias range retires with the verdict of the fallback rule (next matching entry or default), never with the hi-base entry's permissions (the hi-base entry is given the opposite permission); csrr pmpaddr confirms bits 31:30 stored.
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_pmp (model verdict == rvfi_trap with cause 1/5/7; denied data word => no data_req_o; denied fetch still on ibus, traps in ID); gen_isa_compare (trap/no-trap agreement); gen_chk_csr_readback
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_pmp_match_napot

### TP-PMP-042: TOR bounds above 4 GiB: upper bound hi matches all addresses above start; lower bound hi is empty

- Expected: pass

### TP-PMP-091: PMP CSR write while a fetch is in flight: the prefetched word is checked with the new state
- Features: F-PMP-092, F-PMP-066
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: cpuctrlsts.icache_enable = 0 (pinned for the whole test and excluded from random cpuctrlsts writes) so the prefetch of the word after the csrw is visible as an ibus grant (S-4); imem timing tuned so the prefetch buffer has already been granted that word before the csrw retires (same-cycle grant, min rvalid); a table where the csrw changes that word's verdict. RTL basis (fcov Appendix C): the CSR flush asserts halt_if/flush_id only and sets no PC, so the granted word stays in the fetch FIFO and is PMP-checked on pc_if at the IF/ID handoff with the post-write state.
- Stimulus: csrw pmpcfg/pmpaddr/mseccfg that makes the next word denied (variant A) or allowed (variant B, the word was denied when fetched).
- Randomized: CSR, direction, filler, outstanding cap, privilege.
- Knobs: knob:imem_gnt_delay same_cycle, knob:imem_rvalid_delay min1, knob:imem_outstanding_cap 2, knob:instr_mix csr_heavy
- Fire-check: RVFI/ibus, per seed: the next word's grant precedes the csrw retire and the word is not granted again before its instruction retires (it survived the flush); variant A -> that instruction retires with rvfi_trap = 1 (cause 1); variant B -> it retires with rvfi_trap = 0 although it was denied when fetched.
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_pmp (model verdict == rvfi_trap with cause 1/5/7; denied data word => no data_req_o; denied fetch still on ibus, traps in ID); gen_isa_compare (trap/no-trap agreement); gen_chk_ibus_proto
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_pmp_recfg
- Bins: CG-PMP-011.cr_src_fetch.bus_prefetched_now_denied, CG-PMP-011.cr_src_fetch.bus_prefetched_now_allowed, CG-PMP-011.cr_src_fetch.fresh_now_denied, CG-PMP-011.cr_src_fetch.fresh_now_allowed, CG-PMP-011.cp_next_src.bus_prefetched, CG-PMP-011.cp_next_src.fresh, CG-PMP-010.cr_outcome_priv.retired_ok_recfg_m, CG-PMP-010.cr_outcome_priv.retired_ok_recfg_u, CG-PMP-010.cp_outcome.retired_ok_recfg

### TP-PMP-092: PMP-denied lines are cached by the icache; a later hit is re-checked at IF/ID
- Features: F-PMP-093

- Pass criteria: gen_chk_pmp (model verdict == rvfi_trap with cause 1/5/7; denied data word => no data_req_o; denied fetch still on ibus, traps in ID); gen_isa_compare (trap/no-trap agreement); gen_chk_icache (fills are legal; F-IC-036 cross-reference)
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_pmp_icache_dummy
- Bins: CG-PMP-009.cr_src.*, CG-PMP-009.cp_src.cache_hit, CG-PMP-010.cr_hit_outcome.*, CG-PMP-010.cr_hit_cause.*, CG-PMP-010.cp_later_outcome.hit_fault, CG-PMP-010.cp_later_outcome.hit_ok, CG-PMP-010.cp_later_cause.*, CG-PMP-011.cr_src_fetch.cache_hit_now_denied, CG-PMP-011.cr_src_fetch.cache_hit_now_allowed, CG-PMP-011.cp_next_src.cache_hit

- Features: F-PMP-027, F-PMP-028, F-PMP-007, F-PMP-008, F-PMP-009
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: M-mode; mseccfg.RLB = 1; 1..PMPNumRegions entries locked (L=1, random A including OFF, one of them a TOR entry i+1 with an unlocked entry i below it) under RLB=1; MML random with survivable rules; the table state is recovered by a wrapper reset between iterations.
- Stimulus: csrw/csrrc mseccfg clearing RLB (locked entries exist, so the clear is permanent) followed at gap 0 (adjacent rvfi_order) by one of: csrw pmpcfg of a locked entry (variant A), csrw pmpaddr of a locked entry (variant B), csrw pmpaddr(i) below the locked TOR entry (variant C); csrr readbacks; then a csrrs mseccfg RLB attempt (blocked); repeated with 1..3 filler instructions between the two writes.
- Randomized: locked subset and modes, variant, values, op class of both writes, gap, MML.
- Knobs: knob:instr_mix csr_heavy, knob:imem_gnt_delay random, knob:imem_rvalid_delay random
- Fire-check: RVFI, per seed: the mseccfg write retires and csrr shows bit CSR_MSECCFG_RLB_BIT = 0; the adjacent locked write retires trap = 0 with adjacent rvfi_order and its readback equals the pre-write value; the later RLB set attempt reads back 0 while locked entries exist.
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_csr_readback (predicted WARL-legalised value vs csrr readback on rvfi_rd_wdata); gen_isa_compare (rd value and trap agreement)
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_pmp_lock
- Bins: CG-PMP-011.cp_bb.rlbclr_then_cfg, CG-PMP-011.cp_bb.rlbclr_then_addr, CG-PMP-003.cr_rlb_trans.rlb_1_w0_clear, CG-PMP-003.cr_rlb_trans.rlb_0_w1_locked_blocked, CG-PMP-003.cr_state_trans.s001_to_s000, CG-PMP-003.cr_state_trans.s011_to_s010, CG-PMP-003.cr_state_trans.s101_to_s100, CG-PMP-003.cr_state_trans.s111_to_s110, CG-PMP-001.cr_lock_outcome.locked_rlb0_ignored, CG-PMP-002.cr_self_lock.locked_rlb0_ignored, CG-PMP-002.cr_tor_lock.nl_tor_rlb0_ignored

## New checkers requested

- No new checker name is requested. Two extensions of inventory checkers are required and are named in the pass criteria:
  - gen_chk_pmp must check PER WORD of a split misaligned access (MEM-13): a denied word produces no data_req_o while the other word is still issued; the trap cause/mtval follow F-PMP-087/088/089 (mtval = original EA for a first-half or both-half fault, word-aligned second address for a second-half-only fault). It must also carry the debug-mode DM-window exemption keyed on rvfi_ext_debug_mode and, per the brief's bug-candidate rule, the Sdext MPRV rules (cleared on dret to a lower privilege; ignored in debug mode) so that TP-PMP-073/074 are expected-fail.
  - gen_chk_dbus_proto must accept (and require) the second-half request after a first-half PMP fault and a single request for a second-half-only fault; the scoreboard/shim memory image must apply the partially performed store (Q-DL-7 default).
  - gen_isa_compare: the Spike shim is configured with pmpregions = 16, granularity 4, PMP CSRs zeroed at reset, and mirrors the Ibex WARL legalisations (Q1 default). Spike checks a misaligned access as one operation, so for split accesses whose two words get different verdicts the trap/no-trap comparison is delegated to gen_chk_pmp and the Spike comparison for that instruction is limited to pc/order (documented tolerance, not a waiver of the RTL check).
  - gen_chk_pmp model attribution (fix-2): the model must expose, per checked word, the deciding region index, the per-entry match set, the alias range of degenerate entries (CG-PMP-015) and a per-entry liveness record (CG-PMP-016), plus the U-vs-M verdict pair used by CG-PMP-012.cp_uvm; these are model outputs consumed by the covergroups, not new checks.

## Open questions

- OQ-PMP-1 (Q-DL-7 / F-PMP-087): the second word of a misaligned store whose first word is PMP-denied is written to memory. Decision blocked: whether gen_chk_pmp asserts suppression (expected-fail) or models the partial write. Recommended default: model the RTL (spec permits non-atomic decomposition), keep TP-PMP-085 as pass, record a security/integration note.
- OQ-PMP-2 (B1/B2, F-PMP-075/076): TP-PMP-073 and TP-PMP-074 are expected-fail with the checker following Sdext. Decision blocked: whether the debug-area items sharing these bug candidates use the same model so the two areas do not disagree. Recommended default: one shared MPRV rule in gen_chk_pmp, owned by this area, referenced by the DBG items.
- OQ-PMP-3 (D numbering): gen_reading_report.md Section 5.3 lists doc mismatches without D-numbers; TP-PMP-075 cites the illegal-MPP entry as D2 by list position. Decision blocked: the canonical D-number. Recommended default: DV Lead assigns numbers in Section 5.3 order and this file is renumbered mechanically.
- OQ-PMP-4 (memory map): TP-PMP-036/039/068 need TB memory at address 0, the top word 0xFFFFFFFC and arbitrary NAPOT bases. Decision blocked: whether the memory agents are sparse (any address backed). Recommended default: sparse memory model with a default fill; the boot region and DM window are fixed, everything else is backed on demand.
- OQ-PMP-5 (F-PMP-084 latency bin): the two-cycle fake-response latency is not observable at the boundary. Decision blocked: accept the probe listed under Probe candidates or drop the bin. Recommended default: keep the probe (read-only, define-gated), because it is the only witness that a denied access never waits for the bus agent.
- OQ-PMP-6 (Q2 of the feature list): directed per-row Smepmp tests vs the 96-bin covergroup. Recommended default kept here: TP-PMP-054 (random, all 96 bins mandatory) plus the directed sanity items TP-PMP-055..062, one per truth-table row group.
- OQ-PMP-7 (TP-PMP-078 exc_entry variant): a trap vector inside a PMP-denied region produces a fetch fault on trap entry and then a double fault. Decision blocked: whether the item may exercise this (it ends the program) or only records the first fault and resets. Recommended default: run it as the last scenario of a seed and end the test on the double-fault (cross-check with gen_chk_double_fault).
- OQ-PMP-8 (Critic pre-review pmp section vs RTL, TP-PMP-091 / CG-PMP-010 / CG-PMP-011): the Critic states that every PMP CSR write flushes the pipeline so the pre-fetched word is discarded. The RTL reading in this revision (fcov_pmp.md Appendix C): csr_pipe_flush (rtl/ibex_id_stage.sv:595-597) drives a FLUSH state that asserts halt_if/flush_id and sets no PC (rtl/ibex_controller.sv:816-819, 953-963); the fetch FIFO is cleared only by branch_i (rtl/ibex_prefetch_buffer.sv:78), so the granted word is retained and PMP-checked on pc_if at the IF/ID handoff with the post-write state. Decision blocked: which reading the DV Lead / Critic accept. Recommended default: keep TP-PMP-091 and the bus_prefetched / retired_ok_recfg bins as written (icache_enable pinned to 0 so the grant is visible, S-4); one directed simulation settles it and, if the Critic is right, the bins become ignore_bins and TP-PMP-091 is rewritten to the discard behaviour.
- OQ-PMP-9 (CG-PMP-007.cr_napot_k_bclass k30/k31/k32_inside_low, TP-PMP-036): the Critic's M-03 row range (488-492, 513-517) also covered k30/k31_inside_low; those bins are kept because the NAPOT decode gives base 0 for these encodings (rtl/ibex_pmp.sv:160-209), so an access at address 0 is inside_low (needs the sparse memory of OQ-PMP-4). Only the inside_high bins (region last byte above 2^32) are ignored. Decision blocked: confirm the reading; default as stated.


# 4.5 Areas DBG, TRG, PMC: External debug (Sdext), triggers (Sdtrig), performance counters


Area group DBG/TRG/PMC, T-006 subagent output. Configuration and DUT as in
fcov_dbg_trg_pmc.md. Conventions:
- Every item is driven at the DUT boundary: programs through the ibus (TB instruction memory,
  incl. the debug ROM aliased at DmHaltAddr/DmExceptionAddr per tb-infra b.6), data through the
  dbus, debug_req_i / irq_*_i / irq_nm_i / mcounteren_writable_i through pins. CSR, PMP, counter,
  trigger and privilege state is set by instructions in the test program and randomized.
- "debug program" = the code at DmHaltAddr: prologue `csrr dcsr; csrr dpc; sw both to the TB
  mailbox`, a randomized body (from the item), an epilogue that optionally rewrites dcsr/dpc,
  then dret. DmExceptionAddr holds `csrr mcause/mepc/mtval -> mailbox; j <resume>`.
- "held" debug_req_i = level driven until the ibus monitor reports the DmHaltAddr fetch (tb-infra
  b.6), then released after a randomized 0..8 cycles unless the item says otherwise.
- Three randomization layers: per-transaction distributions are in Stimulus; regime knobs are
  named in Knobs (bins owned by the cross-cutting subagent); the regime schedule is the
  cross-cutting subagent's, referenced as "schedule" where relevant.
- Expected values: `expected-fail (B<n>)` means the checker follows the specification and the RTL is
  known to differ (bug candidate B<n>, canonical numbering of the fix brief: B1 dret/MPRV, B2 MPRV
  in debug mode, B3 tdata3/context CSRs read 0, B5 dcsr.nmip, B7 dummies in minstret, B9 dcsr.cause
  0 window, B10 trigger cause on ebreak entry, B11 NumBranchesTaken under DIT, B15 dcsr.ebreaks
  writable; B6 is reclassified RTL-defined and has no expected-fail item). `pass (doc mismatch
  D<n>)` uses the canonical doc-defect numbers: D4 tdata1 reset 0x2800_1048, D6 misaligned counted
  once, D12 debug.rst trigger CSRs "Debug Mode only", D16 performance_counters.rst parameter text,
  D18 cs_registers.rst DbgHwNumLen / scontext 0x7AA (D5 is RETIRED in favour of B15).
- Feature citations may name ALIAS/FOLDED IDs of gen_part_dbg_trg_pmc.md; traceability resolves
  them to the canonical or parent ID.
- Q-005 default (Section 6, Q-DL-4): exact-count counter items run with
  cpuctrlsts.dummy_instr_en=0; only the B7 item enables dummies (TP-TRG-026 runs them with the
  counter checker in bound mode).
- Ebreak-into-debug rule (S-2; fcov_dbg_trg_pmc.md Conventions): the RVFI record of an ebreak that
  enters debug mode has rvfi_trap = 0 (rtl/ibex_core.sv:1885-1886); fire-checks identify the debug
  path as `is_ebreak(rvfi_insn) && !rvfi_trap` followed by the DmHaltAddr fetch and the exception
  path as `rvfi_trap = 1` followed by the mtvec fetch; inside debug mode an ebreak re-enters with
  rvfi_trap = !ebreakX (rtl/ibex_controller.sv:874-876). The counter model does not count the
  ebreak-into-debug record in minstret (rtl/ibex_id_stage.sv:1218); TP-PMC-009 carries that check.
- Window definitions W-DEC(X) / W-FLUSH(X) / W-IRQTAKEN / W-DBGTAKEN / W-WAITSLEEP(wfi) are the
  boundary forms defined in fcov_dbg_trg_pmc.md (Conventions); items name them instead of
  controller states. Items whose driver keys on a redirect-target or instruction fetch pin
  cpuctrlsts.icache_enable=0 (S-4). Entry bound: 17 RVFI records (gen_tb_architecture.md 8.2
  item 5); cycle bounds derive from the agent knobs (DBG_ENTRY_BOUND_CYCLES).
- core_busy_o port rule (gen_tb_architecture.md 8.2 item 1): the one-cycle WAIT_SLEEP dip is a
  ctrl_busy fact; it is visible on core_busy_o only when no ibus beat is outstanding, no icache
  invalidation sweep is active and the LSU is idle in that cycle; gen_chk_sleep applies the rule
  and the dip bins carry a `hidden` class.
- minstret checks need a minstret read: only items whose program reads minstret carry minstret
  bins and gen_chk_counters minstret claims; DBG items cite the PMC item that checks the counter
  effect of their scenario. mhpmcounter and mcycle effects are visible per retirement on
  rvfi_ext_mhpmcounters / rvfi_ext_mcycle and need no read.
- Parameter shorthands (S-8): HPM_LAST = MHPMCOUNTER_BASE + MHPMCounterNum - 1; HPM_CTRL_MASK =
  ((32'd1 << (MHPMCOUNTER_BASE + MHPMCounterNum)) - 1) & ~32'h2 (writable mcountinhibit /
  mcounteren bits; 32'h1FFD for MHPMCounterNum = 10); implemented counter CSRs are
  CSR_MHPMCOUNTER3 + k, CSR_MHPMCOUNTER3H + k, CSR_MHPMEVENT3 + k and the aliases CSR_HPMCOUNTER3 + k,
  CSR_HPMCOUNTER3H + k for k in [0 : MHPMCounterNum-1]; the unimplemented range is k in
  [MHPMCounterNum : 28]; post_op = the value the CSR op produces (csrrw: wdata; csrrs: old | wdata;
  csrrc: old & ~wdata) before WARL legalisation. DIV_STALL_FULL = 36, DIV_STALL_ZERO = 1 (fcov
  Conventions).
- Layer-1 weight tables (S-6). Every class list in a Stimulus or Randomized line that carries no
  explicit percentage draws from the table of its operand class below; an item-local percentage
  overrides the table. Items name the tables they use as `weights: W<n>` at the end of their
  Randomized line.
  - W1 CSR op form: csrrw 25, csrrs 20, csrrc 20, csrrwi 15, csrrsi 10, csrrci 10 (percent).
  - W2 CSR write data / pattern: zeros 15, all-ones 15, walking-one 25, random 45.
  - W3 privilege of the scenario: M 50, U 50 (an item that pins a privilege says so).
  - W4 interrupt line: software 15, timer 15, external 30, fast[k] 30 (k uniform over
    $bits(irq_fast_i)), NMI 10; multi-line episodes 20.
  - W5 bus latency per transaction (both agents): gnt/rvalid delay 0: 20, 1: 20, 2-7: 30, 8-40: 30;
    error injection per the knob:*_err_rate regime.
  - W6 program instruction class: ALU 40, load/store 20, branch 15, jump 5, CSR 10, compressed 10
    (compressed_heavy: compressed 50, the rest scaled).
  - W7 data access width / alignment: byte 25, half 25, word 50; misaligned 20 of half/word.
  - W8 Zcmp: opcode uniform over {cm.push, cm.pop, cm.popret, cm.popretz, cm.mvsa01, cm.mva01s};
    rlist uniform 4..15; spimm uniform.
  - W9 multiply / divide operands: random 60, divide-by-zero 15, signed overflow 10, small (< 16) 15.
  - W10 counter window length / event count: 0: 10, 1: 15, 2-15: 35, >= 16: 40.
  - W11 PMP deny mechanism: plain region deny 34, MMWP no-match 33, MML locked without permission
    33; region mode TOR 50, NAPOT 50.
  - W12 trapping instruction class: illegal 25, ecall 25, ebreak (exception path) 20, fetch fault
    15, load/store fault 15.
  - W13 position / offset / timing / address: uniform over the legal range the item states.
  - W14 debug_req_i shape per transaction: level held 60, short pulse 1-3 cycles 20, released 0-8
    cycles after the DmHaltAddr fetch 20 (the regime knob sets the density).

  and then DmHaltAddr with no retirement between (gen_test_dbg_haltreq).
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_debug (dpc == mtvec target, cause 3, prv M); gen_isa_compare (mepc,
  mcause 5/7, mtval == address as the ISA model predicts); gen_chk_pmp for the PMP variant.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_dbg_haltreq
- Bins: CG-DBG-001.cr_cause_ctx.haltreq_flush_exc, CG-DBG-001.cr_cause_dpc.haltreq_mtvec, CG-DBG-002.cr_coincident_outcome.exc_entered

### TP-DBG-006: Halt request coincident with a synchronous exception from ID (illegal, ecall, ebreak with ebreakm=0, fetch error)
- Features: F-DBG-004

- Features: F-DBG-001, F-DBG-068

### TP-DBG-011: debug_req_i deasserted exactly in W-FLUSH(ecall), the cycle before W-DBGTAKEN, records dcsr.cause = 0
- Features: F-DBG-006

  target); the driver sweeps the fall offset over [0:3] cycles so the exact window is hit in a
  fraction of iterations.

- Knobs: knob:debug_req_regime

- Pass criteria: gen_chk_debug follows Sdext: every debug entry records a defined cause (1..4);
  cause==0 is a failure. gen_isa_compare unaffected.
- Expected: expected-fail (B9)
- Test group: gen_dbg_req_shape
- Bins: CG-DBG-001.cp_cause.none, CG-DBG-002.cr_shape_outcome.flush_entered, CG-DBG-002.cp_shape.pulse_flush

### TP-DBG-018: dcsr WARL: all-ones, all-zeros, walking-one and random writes read back with only ebreakm/ebreaku/step/prv changed; bit 13 (ebreaks) must read 0 (B15)
- Features: F-DBG-012, F-DBG-015, F-DBG-016
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: debug mode (any cause); irq_nm_i low throughout (the nmip compare with an NMI
  pending belongs to TP-DBG-021, the single B5 owner).
- Stimulus: debug program performs 8..32 dcsr writes (csrrw/csrrs/csrrc/csrrwi/csrrsi/csrrci) with
  data drawn from {all-ones 20%, zeros 20%, walking one 30%, random 30%}, each followed by csrr
  dcsr; the epilogue restores step=0 and a valid prv.
- Randomized: pattern sequence, op, immediate values.
- Knobs: none
- Fire-check: every written pattern class appears in the mailbox log paired with its readback
  (gen_test_dbg_csr asserts >= 1 of each class).
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_csr_readback predicts readback = (post_op & 32'h0000_9007 with prv WARL) |
  32'h4000_0000 | cause<<6, i.e. bits 15, 12, 2, 1:0 writable, everything else as before; bit 13
  (ebreaks) is expected to read 0 per tools/specs/riscv-debug-spec/xml/core_registers.xml:163-172
  ("hardwired to 0 if the hart does not support S-mode"); the RTL stores it
  (rtl/ibex_cs_registers.sv:810-834 forces every other field), so the item fails on bit 13.
  Functional impact nil (rtl/ibex_controller.sv:481-483 never reads it). The bit-13 sub-check is
  separately disable-able after an owner ruling.
- Expected: expected-fail (B15)
- Test group: gen_dbg_csr
- Bins: CG-DBG-007.cr_bit_rb.ebreakm_w, CG-DBG-007.cr_bit_rb.ebreaku_w, CG-DBG-007.cr_bit_rb.step_w, CG-DBG-007.cr_bit_rb.ebreaks_w, CG-DBG-007.cr_bit_rb.prv_w, CG-DBG-007.cr_bit_rb.stepie_0, CG-DBG-007.cr_bit_rb.stopcount_0, CG-DBG-007.cr_bit_rb.stoptime_0, CG-DBG-007.cr_bit_rb.mprven_0, CG-DBG-007.cr_bit_rb.nmip_0, CG-DBG-007.cr_bit_rb.z27_0, CG-DBG-007.cr_bit_rb.z14_0, CG-DBG-007.cr_bit_rb.z5_0, CG-DBG-007.cr_bit_rb.xdv_c, CG-DBG-007.cr_pattern_op.zeros_rw, CG-DBG-007.cr_pattern_op.zeros_rc, CG-DBG-007.cr_pattern_op.ones_rw, CG-DBG-007.cr_pattern_op.ones_rs, CG-DBG-007.cr_pattern_op.ones_rc, CG-DBG-007.cr_pattern_op.walk_rw, CG-DBG-007.cr_pattern_op.walk_rs, CG-DBG-007.cr_pattern_op.walk_rc, CG-DBG-007.cr_pattern_op.rand_rw, CG-DBG-007.cr_pattern_op.rand_rs, CG-DBG-007.cr_pattern_op.rand_rc, CG-DBG-008.cr_csr_op.dcsr_wr, CG-DBG-008.cr_csr_op.dcsr_set, CG-DBG-008.cr_csr_op.dcsr_clr

### TP-DBG-034: Exception in debug mode while the privilege inside debug is U (after mret-in-debug) forces privilege back to M (RTL-defined; B6 reclassified)
- Features: F-DBG-026, F-DBG-060, F-DBG-064
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: debug mode; mstatus.MPP=U, mepc = an address in the debug body; PMP permits U
  fetch of the debug window (DM bypass covers it) and a U-permitted data region.
- Stimulus: debug body executes mret (privilege becomes U while debug_mode stays 1), then one of:
  ecall, csrr dcsr (illegal from U), a load to an M-only region (PMP fault), a jump to an M-only
  code page (fetch fault); the DmExceptionAddr handler reads dcsr (works only in M).
- Randomized: exception kind; PMP layout; weights: W11, W12.
- Knobs: knob:pmp_regime
- Fire-check: RVFI shows rvfi_mode==U with rvfi_ext_debug_mode==1 for the retirement before the
  trap and the trap item itself, then the DmExceptionAddr fetch (gen_test_dbg_exc).
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_debug follows the RTL, which is spec-legal: Sdext.adoc:32 runs debug mode
  at M privilege and :51 leaves privilege changes in debug mode UNSPECIFIED, so the exception path
  (rtl/ibex_cs_registers.sv:908) setting priv_lvl := M with dcsr.prv untouched (:918 guard) is
  RTL-defined (Critic C-20). Checks: rvfi_mode == M for the DmExceptionAddr handler retirements,
  dcsr.prv unchanged on csrr read-back, mepc/mcause/mtval unchanged. gen_isa_compare for the trap
  classification (shim models the RTL per Q-005).
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_dbg_exc_in_debug
- Bins: CG-DBG-004.cr_kind_priv.ecall_u, CG-DBG-004.cr_kind_priv.illegalcsr_u, CG-DBG-004.cr_kind_priv.loadpmp_u, CG-DBG-004.cr_kind_priv.fetchpmp_u, CG-DBG-011.cr_mret_mpp.mret_u, CG-DBG-011.cr_class_mode.alu_u

### TP-DBG-049: Step over WFI: WFI acts as a nop, dpc = wfi pc + 4, core_busy_o dips for exactly one cycle when the port rule allows it
- Features: F-DBG-044
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: step armed; mstatus.TW=0; no interrupt pending (irq_pending_o==0); >= 256 cycles
  after reset release / key valid (invalidation sweep finished).
- Stimulus: stepped instruction is wfi in M or U mode; the imem regime alternates between minimum
  latency (no fetch beat outstanding at W-WAITSLEEP(wfi): the dip is visible) and slow (a prefetch
  beat outstanding: the dip is hidden by if_busy).
- Randomized: privilege, mstatus.MIE, instructions around the wfi, imem latency; weights: W3, W5.
- Knobs: knob:irq_regime, knob:imem_rvalid_delay
- Fire-check: the stepped RVFI item is wfi (rvfi_insn==0x10500073) and the DmHaltAddr fetch follows
  within DBG_ENTRY_BOUND_CYCLES; per seed >= 1 iteration with core_busy_o Off for exactly 1 cycle
  (no ibus beat outstanding, no dbus access outstanding in W-WAITSLEEP(wfi)) and >= 1 iteration
  with the dip hidden (an ibus beat outstanding, logged by the ibus monitor) (gen_test_dbg_step).
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_debug (dpc == wfi pc + 4, cause 4); gen_chk_sleep applies the core_busy_o
  port rule (gen_tb_architecture.md 8.2 item 1): exactly one Off cycle when no masking source is
  active (WAIT_SLEEP clears ctrl_busy_o, SLEEP stays busy because debug_single_step_i is set,
  rtl/ibex_controller.sv:598-621; no wake source needed), otherwise no Off cycle; wfi counted in
  minstret is checked by TP-PMC-050.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_dbg_step
- Bins: CG-DBG-006.cr_stepped_prv.wfi_m, CG-DBG-006.cr_stepped_prv.wfi_u, CG-DBG-006.cr_stepped_retired.wfi_ok, CG-DBG-001.cr_cause_dpc.step_wfi, CG-DBG-001.cr_cause_ctx.step_sleep, CG-DBG-001.cr_ctx_busy.sleep_one, CG-DBG-001.cr_ctx_busy.sleep_hidden

- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: PMP programmed (before the halt, in M-mode) to deny the DM window: a region
  covering it with no permissions (MML=0), or MMWP=1 with no matching region, or an MML locked
  region without X/R/W; debug ROM inside the window with a data scratch area also inside.
- Stimulus: haltreq; debug body fetches (its own code), loads and stores to random addresses

  bits, entry privilege.

### TP-DBG-058: DM-window bypass boundaries: DmBaseAddr and the last word are bypassed; one word below/above and a straddling fetch are checked
- Features: F-DBG-053
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: as TP-DBG-057 with the PMP deny extended to cover the neighbourhood of the window;
  debug ROM placed so that a 32-bit instruction can be positioned at (DmBaseAddr|DmAddrMask)-1
  (the aliasing in tb-infra b.6 maps the whole window; a jump into the last halfword is used).

  fetch traps although its first halfword is inside (gen_test_dbg_pmp).
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_pmp (exact mask compare of the DM window on the instruction address and,
  for a 32-bit instruction with address[1]==1, on address+2 (the upper halfword's word, requested
  on instr_addr_o as the next word), and on data_addr_o for loads/stores); gen_chk_debug.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_dbg_pmp_dm
- Bins: CG-DBG-010.cr_bypass.f_base_deny_ok, CG-DBG-010.cr_bypass.f_top_deny_ok, CG-DBG-010.cr_bypass.l_base_deny_ok, CG-DBG-010.cr_bypass.l_top_deny_ok, CG-DBG-010.cr_bypass.s_base_deny_ok, CG-DBG-010.cr_bypass.s_top_deny_ok, CG-DBG-010.cr_bypass.f_straddle_fault, CG-DBG-010.cr_bypass.f_below_fault, CG-DBG-010.cr_bypass.f_above_fault, CG-DBG-010.cr_bypass.l_below_fault, CG-DBG-010.cr_bypass.l_above_fault, CG-DBG-010.cr_bypass.s_below_fault, CG-DBG-010.cr_bypass.s_above_fault

### TP-DBG-063: WFI executed in debug mode acts as a nop (one-cycle core_busy_o dip when the port rule allows it), independent of interrupt inputs
- Features: F-DBG-059
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: debug mode; interrupt lines random (pending in 50%, none in 50%); >= 256 cycles
  after reset release / key valid.
- Stimulus: debug body contains 1..4 wfi instructions with random neighbours; the imem regime
  alternates between minimum latency (dip visible) and slow (a prefetch beat outstanding at
  W-WAITSLEEP(wfi): dip hidden).
- Randomized: pending lines, positions, body, imem latency; weights: W4, W5, W6, W13.
- Knobs: knob:irq_regime, knob:irq_line_mix, knob:imem_rvalid_delay
- Fire-check: RVFI retirement of wfi with rvfi_ext_debug_mode==1 followed by the retirement of
  wfi pc + 4 as the next record, no record in between, with a gap of at most 3 cycles plus the fetch
  latency of wfi + 4 (the WFI path adds 3 cycles and no record, gen_tb_architecture.md 8.2 item 5);
  per seed >= 1 wfi with core_busy_o Off for exactly 1 cycle and >= 1 with the dip hidden by an
  outstanding ibus beat (gen_test_dbg_misc).
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_sleep applies the core_busy_o port rule: exactly one Off cycle when no
  masking source is active (WAIT_SLEEP; SLEEP stays busy because debug_mode_q is set,
  rtl/ibex_controller.sv:598-621; no wake dependency, no bus request during the dip), none
  otherwise; gen_chk_debug (rvfi_ext_debug_mode stays 1); gen_chk_irq (no interrupt taken).
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_dbg_mode_misc
- Bins: CG-DBG-011.cr_wfi.wfi_irq, CG-DBG-011.cr_wfi.wfi_none, CG-DBG-011.cp_insn_class.wfi, CG-DBG-011.cr_wfi_busy.irq_one, CG-DBG-011.cr_wfi_busy.none_one, CG-DBG-011.cr_wfi_busy.irq_hidden, CG-DBG-011.cr_wfi_busy.none_hidden

  cache contents retained across the window unless invalidated); gen_chk_ibus_proto; gen_chk_debug.

- Bins: CG-DBG-011.cr_fetch_icache.repeat_on, CG-DBG-011.cr_fetch_icache.first_on, CG-DBG-011.cr_fetch_icache.repeat_off

### TP-DBG-071: Halt request swept cycle by cycle around W-DEC of a wfi / mret / CSR-flush / dret: entry arc and core_busy_o profile per offset
- Features: F-DBG-068, F-DBG-001, F-DBG-007, F-DBG-009
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: M-mode (U-mode with mstatus.TW=0 for the wfi); no interrupt pending
  (irq_pending_o==0) so the wfi would really sleep; for dret the core is in a debug window with a
  held debug_req_i re-asserted at the offset; icache_enable=0 (the ibus fetch of the instruction
  anchors the driver); >= 256 cycles after reset release / key valid.
- Stimulus: one special instruction (wfi 40%, mret 20%, flushing csrw 20%, dret 20%) at a random
  position; debug_req_i rises at offset k relative to the first W-DEC cycle of the instruction
  (back-dated from its record), k drawn uniformly from {-2, -1, 0, +1, +2, +3, +8}, and is held.
- Randomized: instruction kind, offset k, mret MPP/MPIE/mepc, CSR target, neighbours.
- Knobs: knob:debug_req_regime, knob:instr_mix, knob:imem_gnt_delay
- Fire-check: gen_test_dbg_haltreq classifies each iteration from the boundary trace: (a) k <= 0 and
  wfi/mret/csrw: the special instruction retires with rvfi_ext_debug_req==1 and the DmHaltAddr fetch
  follows with core_busy_o never Off (W-FLUSH -> W-DBGTAKEN); (b) k >= +1 and wfi: W-WAITSLEEP(wfi)
  is reached and, with no masking source active (port rule), core_busy_o is Off for exactly one
  cycle when debug_req_i is already high in the first SLEEP cycle, otherwise for one cycle plus one
  per un-woken SLEEP cycle, then the DmHaltAddr fetch (SLEEP wake, F-DBG-009); with a masking
  source active (an ibus beat outstanding, logged) the dip is hidden and the iteration is classed
  (b)-hidden; (c) dret at any k: zero non-debug retirements between the two windows (W-DEC(dret) ->
  W-DBGTAKEN re-halt, F-DBG-007). Each of (a), (b) with a one-cycle dip, (b) with a dip >= 2,
  (b)-hidden and (c) must occur at least once per seed.
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_debug (cause 3; dpc == wfi pc + 4 / mepc / csrw pc + 4 / dret target;
  dcsr.prv == old MPP for mret); gen_chk_sleep (core_busy_o profile per class: none / exactly one /
  k cycles; no bus request while Off); gen_isa_compare (mret and CSR side effects committed;
  stream continuous).
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_dbg_haltreq
- Bins: CG-DBG-001.cr_cause_ctx.haltreq_flush_wfi, CG-DBG-001.cr_cause_ctx.haltreq_flush_mret, CG-DBG-001.cr_cause_ctx.haltreq_flush_csr, CG-DBG-001.cr_cause_ctx.haltreq_sleep, CG-DBG-001.cr_cause_ctx.haltreq_after_dret, CG-DBG-001.cr_ctx_busy.flush_wfi_none, CG-DBG-001.cr_ctx_busy.sleep_one, CG-DBG-001.cr_ctx_busy.sleep_many, CG-DBG-001.cr_cause_dpc.haltreq_wfi, CG-DBG-001.cr_cause_dpc.haltreq_mret, CG-DBG-001.cr_cause_dpc.haltreq_dret, CG-DBG-002.cr_coincident_outcome.wfi_entered, CG-DBG-002.cr_coincident_outcome.mret_entered, CG-DBG-002.cr_coincident_outcome.csr_entered, CG-DBG-002.cr_shape_outcome.dret_rehalt, CG-DBG-001.cr_ctx_busy.sleep_hidden

### TP-DBG-072: Step disarmed (dcsr.step 1 -> 0) in the last step window: the next dret free-runs with no re-entry
- Features: F-DBG-037, F-DBG-065
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: a first haltreq window drets with step = 0 (plain resume); then a step sequence of
  2..8 steps (TP-DBG-042 path); the last step window clears dcsr.step (csrrc / csrrw with bit 2
  clear: post-op value 0) and leaves dpc; debug_req_i low afterwards.
- Stimulus: dret; the resumed program runs >= 64 instructions of random ALU/branch/load code with
  no ebreak, trigger or debug request; a control iteration keeps step = 1 (one more step).
- Randomized: number of steps before the disarm, the op used to clear step, program after the
  resume, privilege; weights: W1, W6, W3.
- Knobs: knob:priv_regime, knob:instr_mix
- Fire-check: after the disarming dret >= 64 consecutive RVFI items with rvfi_ext_debug_mode==0 and
  no DmHaltAddr fetch; the control iteration re-enters after exactly one retirement with cause 4;
  the first plain dret of the seed is followed by >= 8 free-run retirements (gen_test_dbg_step).
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_debug (step_armed follows the post-op dcsr.step, not the write data: no
  entry after the disarm, one-instruction entry in the control); gen_chk_csr_readback (dcsr.step
  readback 0 before the disarming dret); gen_isa_compare.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_dbg_step
- Bins: CG-DBG-005.cr_step_next.offafteron_run, CG-DBG-005.cr_step_next.on_step, CG-DBG-005.cr_step_next.offfirst_run

### TP-DBG-073: dcsr.ebreakm / ebreaku toggled across debug windows: the ebreak outcome follows the latest post-op enable value
- Features: F-DBG-017, F-DBG-018, F-DBG-019, F-DBG-020, F-DBG-021
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: mtvec handler skips ebreaks; debug ROM epilogue writes dcsr.ebreakm/ebreaku with
  csrrs/csrrc/csrrw (post-op value tracked by the CSR model); PMP permits the U section.
- Stimulus: per privilege a sequence of 4..8 windows: ebreak with the enable 0 (exception,
  handler), a haltreq window that sets the enable (0 -> 1), ebreak (debug entry) whose window
  clears the enable (1 -> 0), ebreak (exception), and so on; both privileges interleaved via mret /
  dret.
- Randomized: toggle order and op, number of toggles, privilege schedule, ebreak form (32-bit /
  c.ebreak); weights: W1, W3.
- Knobs: knob:priv_regime, knob:debug_req_regime
- Fire-check: per seed >= 1 ebreak whose outcome changed from exception to debug entry after a
  0 -> 1 write and >= 1 that changed from debug entry to exception after a 1 -> 0 write, in each
  privilege; outcome decoded from the next fetch (DmHaltAddr vs mtvec) and rvfi_trap (0 on the
  debug path, S-2 rule) (gen_test_dbg_ebreak).
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_debug (entry iff the post-op enable bit of the current privilege is 1 at
  the ebreak); gen_isa_compare (exception path otherwise); gen_chk_csr_readback (enable readback
  after each toggle).
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_dbg_ebreak
- Bins: CG-DBG-003.cr_edge_outcome.mset_dbg, CG-DBG-003.cr_edge_outcome.mclr_exc, CG-DBG-003.cr_edge_outcome.uset_dbg, CG-DBG-003.cr_edge_outcome.uclr_exc, CG-DBG-007.cr_bit_rb.ebreakm_w, CG-DBG-007.cr_bit_rb.ebreaku_w

### TP-PMC-005: A CSR write to mcycle/mcycleh wins over the increment in the write cycle; the read part of csrrw returns the pre-write value
- Features: F-PMC-004

- Tier: targeted

  (N in [0:8]) by csrr mcycle(h); the TB measures the cycles between the two retirements.

  captured (gen_test_pmc_mcycle).

### TP-PMC-009: minstret excludes trapping instructions (ecall, ebreak exception, illegal, fetch fault, load/store fault) and includes wfi, mret, dret, fence.i
- Features: F-PMC-007
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: dummy_instr_en=0; mtvec handler returns past the trapping instruction; PMP/bus
  error configured for the fault variants; ebreakm=0 except in the ebreak-into-debug variant
  (ebreakm=1 set in a first debug window; the debug program reads minstret in its prologue,
  advances dpc by the ebreak size and drets).
- Stimulus: windows each containing one class of excluded instruction (1..5 occurrences) plus
  included ones (wfi with a pending interrupt so it returns, mret, fence.i), bounded by minstret
  reads; the ebreak-into-debug variant places 1..3 ebreaks with ebreakm=1 in the window and reads
  minstret before the first ebreak and after the last dret.
- Randomized: class per window, counts, positions, privilege for ecall, ebreak form in the
  into-debug variant; weights: W1, W3, W6, W10.
- Knobs: knob:dmem_err_rate, knob:imem_err_rate, knob:pmp_regime, knob:irq_regime
- Fire-check: each window's RVFI stream contains >= 1 rvfi_trap item of the intended class (or the
  included instruction) between its two reads; the into-debug variant shows >= 1 ebreak record with
  rvfi_trap == 0 followed by the DmHaltAddr fetch (gen_test_pmc_minstret).
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_counters (delta excludes rvfi_trap items and every ebreak record, includes
  wfi/mret/fence.i/dret items); counter-model rule (S-2, rtl/ibex_id_stage.sv:1218): the
  ebreak-into-debug record has rvfi_trap = 0 and is NOT counted, so the window delta equals the
  counted records plus the debug-program retirements (incl. dret); gen_isa_compare.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_pmc_minstret
- Bins: CG-PMC-002.cr_window_delta.ecall_eq, CG-PMC-002.cr_window_delta.ebreakexc_eq, CG-PMC-002.cr_window_delta.illegal_eq, CG-PMC-002.cr_window_delta.fetchfault_eq, CG-PMC-002.cr_window_delta.lsfault_eq, CG-PMC-002.cr_window_delta.wfi_eq, CG-PMC-002.cr_window_delta.mret_eq, CG-PMC-002.cr_window_delta.fencei_eq, CG-PMC-002.cr_window_delta.ebreakdbg_eq

### TP-PMC-046: mhpmcounter12 (NumCyclesDivWait) counts iterative divider stall cycles incl. divide-by-zero and overflow
- Features: F-PMC-044
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: mcountinhibit[12]=0; dummy_instr_en=0.
- Stimulus: windows with div/divu/rem/remu with random operands, divide-by-zero with
  cpuctrlsts.data_ind_timing=0 (early-out: DIV_STALL_ZERO = 1 stall cycle,
  rtl/ibex_multdiv_fast.sv:434,445) and =1 (full latency), and the signed overflow case, bounded by
  mhpmcounter12 reads; each divide is preceded by a single-cycle ALU instruction; the TB measures
  each divide's stall count as its RVFI gap from the previous retirement minus 1 (S-4: deltas from
  the previous retirement only) under the qualifiers: icache_enable=0 pinned and the divide's fetch
  already delivered (no fetch stall), the previous record a single-cycle non-memory instruction
  retired without a WB stall, dummy_instr_en=0 (no dummy in the gap), no mcycle/mcountinhibit write
  in between; a window in which a qualifier fails is checked as a bound.
- Randomized: opcode, operands, data_ind_timing, counts (0, 1 early-out, 2..15 early-outs, 1 full,
  >= 2 full, mixed); weights: W9, W10, W13.
- Knobs: knob:instr_mix
- Fire-check: RVFI divide count and measured gaps per window; per seed >= 1 window of each shape
  (early-outs only, exactly one full divide, several full divides) with all qualifiers holding
  (gen_test_pmc_hpm_event).
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_counters exact_gap class: delta == sum(gap - 1) over the divides of a
  qualified window (DIV_STALL_FULL = 36 per full divide, DIV_STALL_ZERO = 1 per early-out); bound
  class (0 <= delta <= cycles elapsed) otherwise.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_pmc_hpm_event
- Bins: CG-PMC-003.cr_idx_events.div_0, CG-PMC-003.cr_idx_events.div_1, CG-PMC-003.cr_idx_events.div_few, CG-PMC-003.cr_idx_events.div_many, CG-PMC-003.cr_variant_rel.div_eq, CG-PMC-003.cr_variant_rel.divu_eq, CG-PMC-003.cr_variant_rel.rem_eq, CG-PMC-003.cr_variant_rel.remu_eq, CG-PMC-003.cr_variant_rel.divzero_eq, CG-PMC-003.cr_variant_rel.divovf_eq, CG-PMC-003.cr_idx_inhibit.div_eq, CG-PMC-003.cr_div_shape.div_early, CG-PMC-003.cr_div_shape.div_full1, CG-PMC-003.cr_div_shape.div_fullmany, CG-PMC-003.cr_div_shape.div_mixed, CG-PMC-003.cr_div_shape.div_none

### TP-PMC-047: Event counter written in the cycle its event fires: the write wins and that event is lost
- Features: F-PMC-045
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: mcountinhibit[N]=0; dummy_instr_en=0; slow dmem for the LSU-wait variant.
- Stimulus: csrw mhpmcounterN placed so that N's event fires in the write cycle: N=3 with a load
  waiting in WB; N=5/6 with a load/store issued in the same cycle (the csrw follows the load
  directly); N=7/8 with a jump/branch adjacent to the csrw (the event fires in DECODE, so the TB
  sweeps the relative position 0..2 and the coincidence occurs in a fraction of iterations); N=4
  with an IF starvation cycle; then a read. The bounding window read pair is placed around the
  write so the window model sees delta < events for the lost event.
- Randomized: N, position sweep, value; weights: W2, W10, W13.
- Knobs: knob:dmem_rvalid_delay, knob:imem_rvalid_delay, knob:instr_mix
- Fire-check: the boundary model logs the event in the write cycle for >= 1 iteration per N class
  (gen_test_pmc_hpm_csr).
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_counters (readback == written + events after the write cycle only).
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_pmc_hpm_csr
- Bins: CG-PMC-003.cp_delta_rel.lt, CG-PMC-007.cr_target_coinc.hpm_lsu, CG-PMC-007.cr_target_coinc.hpm_if, CG-PMC-007.cr_target_coinc.hpm_load, CG-PMC-007.cr_target_coinc.hpm_store, CG-PMC-007.cr_target_coinc.hpm_jump, CG-PMC-007.cr_target_coinc.hpm_branch, CG-PMC-007.cr_target_coinc.hpmh_load, CG-PMC-007.cr_target_coinc.hpm_none, CG-PMC-004.cr_idx_reg_op.fi_lo_wr, CG-PMC-004.cr_idx_reg_op.li_lo_wr
