### TP-PMC-056: mcountinhibit bit set (and cleared) in the middle of an event window: events before the write count, events after do not, counting resumes after the clear
- Features: F-PMC-021, F-PMC-001
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: dummy_instr_en=0; mcountinhibit=0 at the window start.
- Stimulus: window bounded by reads of mcycle and of mhpmcounterN (N in {loads, stores, branches,
  ret_c}): E1 events of N's class, csrs mcountinhibit with bit N (and CY in a variant) set, E2
  events, optionally csrc clearing the bit, E3 events, then the closing reads; the boundary model
  counts E1/E2/E3 from RVFI / dbus and the cycles of each segment.
- Randomized: N, E1/E2/E3, whether the bit is cleared again (60%), CY variant (30%), op used for
  the write; weights: W10, W1.
- Knobs: knob:instr_mix, knob:dmem_rvalid_delay
- Fire-check: per seed >= 1 window with E1 >= 2, E2 >= 2 and the inhibit write retired between them
  (RVFI order), and >= 1 window with the clear-and-resume shape (E3 >= 2) (gen_test_pmc_ctrl).
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_counters (delta == E1 (+ E3 after the clear); the inhibit takes effect from
  the cycle after the csrs (F-PMC-021) and counting resumes the cycle after the clear; mcycle delta
  == cycles outside the inhibited segment in the CY variant); gen_chk_csr_readback.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_pmc_ctrl
- Bins: CG-PMC-003.cr_idx_inhibit.ld_setmid, CG-PMC-003.cr_idx_inhibit.st_setmid, CG-PMC-003.cr_idx_inhibit.br_clrmid, CG-PMC-003.cr_idx_inhibit.rc_setmid, CG-PMC-001.cr_ctx_delta.inhmid_partial

### TP-PMC-057: mcounteren_writable_i transitions (On -> Off, Off -> On, On -> invalid, invalid -> On) between two mcounteren writes: the pin value in the write cycle decides
- Features: F-PMC-026, F-PMC-025
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: mcounteren preset while the pin is On; the pin driver changes the pin between
  consecutive mcounteren writes (spacing 1..20 instructions) and holds each value across the write.
- Stimulus: sequence of 4..10 mcounteren writes (random data, all ops) with the pin driven through
  the transition classes On -> Off -> On -> invalid -> On in random order; csrr after each write; a
  U-mode alias read after each transition whose legality depends on the (applied or unchanged)
  value.
- Randomized: transition order, spacing, data and op, invalid encoding; weights: W1, W2, W13.
- Knobs: none
- Fire-check: the pin monitor logs each transition class at least once between two retired
  mcounteren writes per seed, and the readbacks are captured (gen_test_pmc_ctrl).
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_csr_readback (a write with the pin != On in W-DEC of the write is dropped,
  with the pin On applied, whatever the previous pin value; no trap); gen_isa_compare (alias
  legality follows the applied value).
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_pmc_ctrl
- Bins: CG-PMC-005.cr_pin_tr_effect.en_ontooff_drop, CG-PMC-005.cr_pin_tr_effect.en_offtoon_app, CG-PMC-005.cr_pin_tr_effect.en_ontoinv_drop, CG-PMC-005.cr_pin_tr_effect.en_invtoon_app

# 4.6 Areas IMEM, DMEM, FE, IC: Instruction and data memory protocol, LSU, fetch stage, instruction cache


T-006 subagent output for the area group IMEM, DMEM, FE, IC (156 feature IDs after the Critic v1
fixes: 129 ACTIVE incl. 7 new, 11 ALIAS, 16 FOLDED; items may cite ALIAS/FOLDED IDs, traceability
resolves them to the canonical ID). Companion of
fcov_mem_fetch_icache.md (bin definitions), trace_feat_tp_mem_fetch_icache.csv and
trace_tp_bin_mem_fetch_icache.csv. Fixed context: `opentitan` configuration, gen_dut_top =
ibex_core + ibex_register_file_ff with MemECC=1 (39-bit buses), ICacheTweakInfection=1,
DummyInstructions=1, ResetAll=1, ICache=1 (prefetch buffer absent, F-FE-001), +define+RVFI.
CHERIoT is out of scope (cheriot_enable_i Off).

Common stimulus base for every item unless stated: a randomized program image loaded into the
imem/dmem agent memory (mix per knob:instr_mix), boot_addr_i random 256-byte aligned, M-mode at
reset, cpuctrlsts.icache_enable set by the program as stated in Preconditions, fetch_enable_i On,
ic_scr_key_valid_i per knob:scr_key_delay, all agents protocol-clean (gnt only with req, rvalid
>= 1 cycle after gnt, exactly one per grant, in order, valid inverted 39/32 SECDED on every
response; Q-DL-9 default). "Agent record" = the per-transaction record of gen_imem_agent /
gen_dmem_agent / gen_icache_ram_model / gen_scr_key_agent. Bus-side fire-checks are taken from
those records; program-side fire-checks from RVFI (rvfi_valid/pc/insn/trap/rd/mem fields and
handler CSR reads visible as rvfi_rd_wdata).

Doc-mismatch and bug-candidate references (canonical numbers of the fix brief): D9 = icache.rst
instr_pmp_err_i / branch_spec_i ports do not exist and the data RAM is 2x39 bits, not 72; D13 =
cs_registers.rst:544-545 "fence.i guaranteed to fetch a new key" vs icache.rst:113-116 and the RTL
(ignored while a key request is pending); D14 = security.rst:85-87 implies an internal NMI for any
bus-integrity mismatch, the I-side gives alert + fetch fault and no NMI; D17 = load_store_unit.rst /
instruction_fetch.rst list separate 7-bit intg ports, at ibex_core they are bits [38:32]; B14 = RVFI
drops the ID-stage trap record when a WB load/store error coincides (rtl/ibex_core.sv:1851-1853),
downgraded to an RVFI convention note pending its confirmation simulation (gen_bug_log.md B14,
gen_tb_architecture.md 8.1 item 5): the priority behaviour is a pass item (TP-DMEM-034) and the
two-record confirmation an informational item (TP-DMEM-063).
Q-DL-7/8/9 defaults from the reading report are applied as stated; the two Q-DL-9 informational
unsolicited-rvalid demonstrations are TP-IMEM-040 (I side) and TP-DMEM-062 (D side), both
`Expected: informational (excluded from the pass gate)` and listed in their test groups. Fill-buffer bound (Critic C-05):
linear prefetch holds at most 3 non-stale fill buffers (FB_THRESHOLD = NUM_FB-2 counting the line
being output); the 4th buffer and the 8-beat outstanding bound need a branch lookup (F-FE-017,
F-IMEM-008, F-IC-038, F-IC-043).

Timing and observability conventions (Critic pre-review S-2/S-4, gen_tb_architecture.md 8.2/8.3):
RVFI-anchored events are back-dated by one cycle (rvfi_valid is one flop after WB exit,
rtl/ibex_core.sv:1868); the commit-to-record offset is 2 for CSR writes and 1 for trap/mret/dret
records. An ebreak that enters debug mode has rvfi_trap = 0; the debug path is is_ebreak(rvfi_insn)
&& !rvfi_trap && next fetch == DmHaltAddr, the exception path rvfi_trap = 1. A redirect is derived
from RVFI (rvfi_pc_wdata != rvfi_pc_rdata + len, or a trap), never from an ibus request. Items that
assert "no re-fetch on the bus" of a word that could hit in the cache pin cpuctrlsts.icache_enable =
0 in their Preconditions (TP-IMEM-026, TP-FE-026) and exclude bit 0 from random cpuctrlsts writes.
Bins named `cp_<knob>.<value>` do not exist in this area: knob values appear only as cross operands
(fcov_mem_fetch_icache.md conventions; the knob bins are fcov_xcut.md CG-REG-*).

that lists its own distribution overrides the table for the named class only. Percentages are the
draw weights of the agent / program generator per transaction.

| W-IMEM-RVALID | gen_imem_agent rvalid latency per granted beat (cycles) | 1: 30%, 2-3: 25%, 4-15: 25%, 16-40: 15%, 41-100: 5% |
| W-DMEM-GNT | gen_dmem_agent grant latency per request (cycles) | 0: 30%, 1: 20%, 2-3: 20%, 4-15: 20%, 16-40: 8%, 41-200: 2% |
| W-DMEM-RVALID | gen_dmem_agent rvalid latency per granted beat (cycles) | 1: 30%, 2-3: 25%, 4-15: 25%, 16-60: 15%, 61-300: 5% |
| W-IMEM-ERR | injected I-side error class per injected beat | bus_err: 50%, intg_single: 25%, intg_double: 25%; victim position: aligned u32 30%, c16 30%, straddle first 15%, straddle second 15%, both halves 10% |
| W-DMEM-ERR | injected D-side error class per injected response | bus_err: 50%, intg_single: 25%, intg_double: 25%; beat: single 50%, first 20%, second 20%, both 10% |
| W-LS | load/store size x offset per generated access | size byte/half/word 30/30/40%; offset o0 40%, o1 20%, o2 20%, o3 20% (misaligned share 40% in ls_heavy) ; rd = x0 5% of loads |
| W-REDIRECT | redirect kind per generated control-flow event | taken branch 40%, not-taken branch 20%, jal 15%, jalr 10%, ecall/illegal 5%, fence.i 3%, mret/dret 5%, WFI 2% |
| W-IC-LINE | fetch-line class per generated code region | cold sequential 40%, warm loop 30%, line entered at word 1 (target[2]=1) 20%, line-crossing straddle 10% |
| W-KEY | gen_scr_key_agent valid-low duration after a pulse (cycles) | 0-1: 30%, 2-15: 30%, 16..IC_NUM_LINES-1: 25%, IC_NUM_LINES..2000: 15% |

### TP-IMEM-008: Outstanding depth ramps to the NUM_FB x IC_LINE_BEATS bound
- Features: F-IMEM-008
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: icache_enable = 1, cache cold (after reset sweep), sequential code over new lines
- Stimulus: gnt same-cycle, rvalid latency 40..80 cycles; sequential cold code until NUM_FB-1 lines
  ((NUM_FB-1)*IC_LINE_BEATS beats) are in flight (the throttle stops linear prefetch there,
  F-FE-017), then a taken branch into another cold region: the NUM_FB-1 buffers go stale with their
  beats still outstanding and the branch lookup allocates the NUM_FB-th buffer, whose IC_LINE_BEATS
  beats reach NUM_FB*IC_LINE_BEATS outstanding; repeat with knob:imem_outstanding_cap in
  {1, IC_LINE_BEATS, 2*IC_LINE_BEATS, NUM_FB*IC_LINE_BEATS}.
- Randomized: branch target, program, latency, number of lines in flight at the branch (1..NUM_FB-1)
- Knobs: knob:imem_gnt_delay (same_cycle), knob:imem_rvalid_delay (long), knob:imem_outstanding_cap
- Fire-check: per seed and per cap value c (agent record): (i) for c < NUM_FB*IC_LINE_BEATS (1, 2, 4)
  the outstanding count reaches c and, while it equals c, instr_req_o is observed high with
  instr_gnt_i withheld for >= 1 cycle (the DUT does not know the agent's cap: it holds the request,
  gen_sva_ibus checks address stability over the wait) and no (c+1)-th grant is ever recorded; (ii)
  for c == NUM_FB*IC_LINE_BEATS (the RTL bound) the count reaches NUM_FB*IC_LINE_BEATS at least once,
  always through the branch path ((NUM_FB-1)*IC_LINE_BEATS stale beats + IC_LINE_BEATS target
  beats), and instr_req_o is low in every cycle where the count equals NUM_FB*IC_LINE_BEATS; (iii)
  linear prefetch alone never exceeds (NUM_FB-1)*IC_LINE_BEATS outstanding.
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_ibus_proto (outstanding <= NUM_FB*IC_LINE_BEATS), gen_sva_ibus,
  gen_isa_compare; detects a request beyond the RTL bound or a deadlock at a withheld grant
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_imem_latency
- Bins: CG-IMEM-002.cp_outstanding_before.o8, CG-IMEM-002.cp_outstanding_before.o5,
  CG-IMEM-002.cp_max_outstanding.m8, CG-IMEM-002.cp_max_outstanding.m5_7,
  CG-IMEM-002.cp_req_held_at_depth.held, CG-IMEM-002.cp_req_held_at_depth.no_req,
  CG-IMEM-002.cr_held_x_depth.held_o1, CG-IMEM-002.cr_held_x_depth.held_o2,
  CG-IMEM-002.cr_held_x_depth.held_o4, CG-IMEM-002.cr_held_x_depth.no_req_o8

### TP-IMEM-011: Bus error on an executed instruction word raises an instruction access fault
- Features: F-IMEM-011
- Phase: 1
- Tier: smoke
- Preconditions: mtvec initialised (boot), handler reads mcause/mtval/mepc and returns past the
  faulting instruction (mepc += length from a side table)
- Stimulus: agent injects instr_err_i on the word of a randomly chosen aligned 32-bit or
  compressed instruction that the program will execute (address chosen from the program's
  straight-line path), at rate 1 per 200..2000 instructions (weights: W-IMEM-ERR, bus_err class).
- Randomized: victim instruction, latencies, cache enable, victim class (u32 aligned / c16), the
  errored word's payload as delivered by the agent (random: decodes as ALU, store, jump, ...)
- Knobs: knob:imem_err_rate (rare), knob:instr_mix
- Fire-check: agent record marks the injected beat consumed (its word delivered for the victim pc)
  and RVFI shows rvfi_trap on that pc with handler-read mcause == 1, mtval == pc, mepc == pc.
- Pass criteria: gen_isa_compare (trap, mepc/mtval/mcause, no rd write, no data_req_o for the
  victim), gen_chk_ibus_proto; detects a missing/extra fault or side effects of the errored word
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_imem_fetch_err
- Bins: CG-IMEM-003.cp_outcome.executed_trap, CG-IMEM-003.cp_half.aligned_u32,
  CG-IMEM-003.cp_half.c16, CG-IMEM-003.cp_mtval.eq_pc, CG-IMEM-003.cp_class.bus_err,

  CG-IMEM-003.cp_alert_major_bus.quiet, CG-FE-005.cp_source.bus, CG-FE-005.cp_errored_payload.rd_write,
  CG-FE-005.cp_errored_payload.other

- Features: F-IMEM-012

### TP-IMEM-016: Instruction-side integrity error: major bus alert, fetch fault when consumed, no NMI
- Features: F-IMEM-027

  coincident events

### TP-DMEM-024: Bus error on the first beat of a split access
- Features: F-DMEM-021
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: trap handler reads mcause/mtval/mepc, records them, returns past the instruction
- Stimulus: agent injects data_err_i on the first beat of split loads and stores (1 in 5..50 split
  accesses); second beat clean; second-beat gnt delay 0..8.
- Randomized: load/store, type, delays, address
- Knobs: knob:dmem_err_rate (rare), knob:dmem_gnt_delay (random)
- Fire-check: agent record: >= 20 first-beat errors (loads and stores) each followed by a granted
  and answered second request; RVFI trap mcause 5/7 with handler-read mtval == the unaligned
  effective address; for stores the second-word request carried data_we_o = 1 with the rotated data
  and complementary be, and the agent memory (which commits writes granted without an error)
  shows the second-half bytes written.

  issued, MEM-10); detects a cancelled second beat or mtval == second word
- Expected: pass

### TP-DMEM-034: WB load/store error outranks an exception of the instruction in ID
- Features: F-DMEM-038
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: handlers for all causes; the ID instruction is one of {illegal, ecall, ebreak,
  instruction with instr_err_i, wfi}
- Stimulus: load/store with data_err_i and rvalid latency 2..6 immediately followed by the chosen
  ID instruction (placed so it is in ID when the error response arrives).
- Randomized: cause pair, latency, size
- Knobs: knob:dmem_err_rate (rare), knob:imem_err_rate (rare)
- Fire-check: >= 5 pairs per ID class where the agent's error rvalid cycle falls inside the ID
  instruction's residency (RVFI: the ID instruction had not retired); the first trap record on RVFI
  is the load/store's (mcause 5/7, handler-read mepc == the load/store pc), no record of the ID
  instruction precedes it, and the ID instruction retires (or traps with its own record) only after
  the handler's mret. The two-record RVFI confirmation for the killed instruction is the
  informational item TP-DMEM-063, not part of this item's gate.
- Pass criteria: gen_isa_compare (trap order: the WB error outranks the ID exception; the ID
  instruction is killed and re-executes, producing its own record later; mepc/mtval/mcause of the
  WB trap), gen_chk_dbus_proto
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_dmem_err
- Bins: CG-DMEM-006.cr_cause_x_id.load_illegal, CG-DMEM-006.cr_cause_x_id.load_ecall,
  CG-DMEM-006.cr_cause_x_id.store_fetch_err, CG-DMEM-006.cr_cause_x_id.store_ebreak,
  CG-DMEM-006.cr_cause_x_id.load_wfi, CG-DMEM-006.cr_cause_x_id.store_illegal,
  CG-DMEM-006.cp_id_killed_reexecuted.yes,
  CG-DMEM-006.cp_id_insn.illegal, CG-DMEM-006.cp_id_insn.ecall, CG-DMEM-006.cp_id_insn.ebreak,
  CG-DMEM-006.cp_id_insn.fetch_err, CG-DMEM-006.cp_id_insn.wfi

### TP-DMEM-048: PMP-denied data access produces no bus request; permitted second half still issued
- Features: F-DMEM-033

- Features: F-DMEM-038

- Stimulus: as TP-DMEM-034: load/store with data_err_i and rvalid latency 2..6 immediately followed

  error rvalid cycle inside the ID instruction's residency); for each pair RVFI shows exactly two
  trap records in order: the load/store's (mcause 5/7) and then, after the handler's mret, the
  re-executed ID instruction's own record with rvfi_trap = 1. One record for the pair re-opens B14
  (gen_bug_log.md B14: downgraded to an RVFI convention note pending this confirmation).
- Pass criteria: none gating; gen_isa_compare records the number and order of trap records for the
  pair (informational mode for the RVFI record count only; the priority behaviour is gated by
  TP-DMEM-034)
- Expected: informational (B14 confirmation; excluded from the pass gate)

  re-enable), gen_isa_compare

  CG-IC-005.cp_off_window.long, CG-IC-005.cr_off_window_x_hit.long_hit, CG-IC-005.cr_off_window_x_hit.short_hit

## New checkers requested

- gen_test_fe_structure (cocotb, test-level): asserts at elaboration that ibex_prefetch_buffer,
  ibex_fetch_fifo and g_branch_predictor are absent under gen_dut_top and gen_icache is present;
  records the code-coverage exclusions for F-FE-001 / F-FE-019. Hosted by TP-FE-001.
- gen_test_ic_geometry (cocotb, test-level): asserts the ic_* port widths (TagSizeECC=28,
  LineSizeECC=78 = 2 x 39) and the index range derived from ibex_pkg, following the RTL against
  the icache.rst 72-bit layout (D9). Hosted by TP-IC-001.
- gen_chk_icache extensions (not new checkers, but capabilities the plan assumes): (a) a shadow
  tag view built from the tag writes the RAM model receives, giving hit/miss/way/validity per
  lookup (CG-IC-003, CG-FE-002.cp_halves_src); (b) write-side ECC decode with the address-derived
  tweak undone (MEM-B.3 correction); (c) an "informational" mode for TP-IC-038 (multi-way hit)
  and for the Q-DL-9 unsolicited-rvalid demonstration tests that are excluded from the pass gate.
- gen_chk_ibus_proto extensions: address-sequence tracker (line_base + ((entry+k) mod
  IC_LINE_BEATS)*4, no wrap when not caching), granted-not-consumed word accounting (discarded
  words per redirect, prefetch lead in lines), outstanding-depth history (max since last redirect).
- gen_chk_dbus_proto extensions: split-pair pairing by second address == first + 4 with the
  agent's memory-side-effect record (second-half write after a first-half error), and the
  "no data_req_o in an error-rvalid cycle" property (F-DMEM-032).
- gen_sva_ibus / gen_sva_dbus driver-rule properties (TB-error class, never a DUT failure): gnt only
  while req (F-IMEM-031, F-DMEM-048, including PMP-suppressed data requests) and no X on
  data_rdata_i with rvalid (F-DMEM-049); hosted by TP-IMEM-039, TP-DMEM-058, TP-DMEM-059.
- gen_chk_store_intg: decodes the whole 39-bit data_wdata_o on every store request (req & gnt &
  we), never over be-masked bytes, and never errors on a load; on loads it records the RTL's
  always-valid encoding as the coverage observation cp_load_wdata_intg_valid (F-DMEM-050 is an
  RTL-defined observation; gen_tb_architecture.md 8.3 item 2; TP-DMEM-045, TP-DMEM-060).
- gen_chk_dbus_proto / gen_chk_bus_intg_rsp / gen_chk_nmi informational mode for TP-DMEM-062 (the
  D-side Q-DL-9 demonstration), mirroring the I-side mode used by TP-IMEM-040.
- gen_chk_alerts: needs an expected-alert feed from gen_icache_ram_model (injection record) so
  alert_minor_o is checked as "exactly one pulse per injected error on a valid hit / real lookup,
  none otherwise", and a per-test suppression switch for TP-IC-038.

## Open questions

1. Reachable I-side outstanding depth (candidate owner question 4). Resolved by analysis (Critic
   C-05): linear prefetch reaches at most 6 outstanding beats; 7 and 8 are reachable only through
   the branch-lookup path (3 stale lines + the target line), which TP-IMEM-008 drives directly.
   CG-IMEM-002.cp_outstanding_before.o8 / cp_max_outstanding.m8 stay required bins.
2. Multi-way hit stimulation via self-modifying code without fence.i (candidate owner question 5;
   F-IC-021, F-IC-042). Blocks: whether TP-IC-038 is in the pass gate. Recommended default:
   informational only (as written), excluded from the gate, CG-IC-006.cp_multiway_mismatch kept
   as an informational bin.
3. Expected architectural state for a bus error inside a Zcmp push/pop sequence (candidate owner
   question 6; F-DMEM-047). Blocks: the pass criterion of TP-DMEM-053. Recommended default:
   compare against the ISS on the equivalent expanded sequence; divergences in mepc / partial
   progress are review items, not failures, until ruled.
4. B14 handling. Settled by gen_bug_log.md B14 / gen_tb_architecture.md 8.1 item 5 (Critic S-1):
   the priority behaviour (WB error outranks the ID exception; the ID instruction is killed and
   re-executes, producing its own record later) is the pass item TP-DMEM-034; the two-record RVFI
   confirmation is the informational item TP-DMEM-063 (fire-check = two trap records in order). One
   record in that simulation re-opens B14 as a bug candidate; nothing else is blocked.
5. PC-increment-check fault injection (F-FE-020). The only way to make alert_major_internal_o fire
   is a force on an internal net, which is outside the boundary-stimulus rule. Blocks: whether a
   force-based directed test is allowed as mutation evidence for gen_chk_alerts. Recommended
   default: no force test in the plan; TP-FE-021 stays an always-low check and the mutation-check
   skill supplies the checker evidence.
6. Unsolicited / grant-cycle rvalid demonstration tests (Q-DL-9). Both are now test-group entries,
   informational and outside the pass gate: TP-IMEM-040 (I side, F-IMEM-032, gen_imem_proto_basic)
   and TP-DMEM-062 (D side, F-DMEM-006/007, gen_dmem_proto_basic); their
   cp_unsolicited_rvalid_case bins (CG-IMEM-007, CG-DMEM-009) are informational and excluded from
   the closure measure. The SEC area's F-SEC-017/019 items cite TP-DMEM-062 rather than duplicating
   it. Blocks: nothing.
7. ic_scr_key_valid_i reset value distribution. Blocks: the ratio of seeds hitting
   CG-IC-002.cp_key_req_at_reset.issued vs skipped_valid_high. Recommended default: 50/50 per seed
   (ibex_top's behaviour is valid=1 at reset; the request path needs valid=0 to be exercised).
8. Whether the wrapper exposes dummy_instr_id_o (P1 probe) for CG-FE-004.cp_dummy_seen. Blocks:
   sampling of that bin and the strictness of the TP-FE-017 fire-check. Recommended default:
   accept the wrapper-internal net as a P1 probe (read-only, documented in the probe register);
   without it the bin is dropped and TP-FE-017 keeps only the timing-gap fire-check.


# 4.7 Areas DIT, SEC, RST, RVFI, CHERI: Dummy instructions and data-independent timing, alerts and countermeasures, reset and boot, RVFI trace, CHERIoT carve-out


Scope: 129 feature IDs (F-DIT-001..030, F-SEC-001..037, F-RST-001..027, F-RVFI-001..034,
F-CHERI-001; 108 ACTIVE, 7 ALIAS, 14 FOLDED per the Status field) from
dv/auto_dv/work/dv-lead/parts/gen_part_sec_rst_rvfi_cheri.md. Items may cite ALIAS / FOLDED IDs;
traceability resolves them to the canonical / parent ID. Build
`opentitan`; DUT gen_dut_top = ibex_core + ibex_register_file_ff with the Q-DL-1 wrapper defaults
(MemECC=1, DummyInstructions=1, ResetAll=1, RegFileECC=0, +define+RVFI, cheriot_enable_i tied
IbexMuBiOff, exclusion cheriot-out-of-scope). Bins referenced here live in
fcov_sec_rst_rvfi_cheri.md. Conventions:

- "gap" = clock cycles between consecutive rvfi_valid pulses, measured by the RVFI monitor.
- "P1" = the wrapper-internal nets dummy_instr_id_o / dummy_instr_wb_o (ibex_core ports wired
  inside gen_dut_top) and the if_stage fcov nets fcov_dummy_instr_type / fcov_insert_dummy_instr.
  Used for coverage only; every checker below works from the boundary or RVFI
  (tb-infra e, P1; rtl-arch s9 confirms they are wrapper nets, not RTL probes).
- Doc mismatches use the canonical D-numbers of the fix brief (D1..D19). Used here: D4 (tdata1
  reset 0x2800_1048, TP-RST-007), D11 (security.rst "early completion of multiplication by
  zero/one is removed" has no RTL counterpart, F-DIT-005, TP-DIT-006), D19 (security.rst
  dummy_instr_mask table lists 4 of the 8 legal values, F-DIT-011, TP-DIT-013).
- Injected integrity errors: the memory agents corrupt the 7 check bits of a 39-bit rdata beat on
  request (single-bit, double-bit or multi-bit flip). No existing knob names the rate; items use
  knob:imem_err_rate / knob:dmem_err_rate for the bus-error regime and ask for an integrity
  knob in Open questions.
- Every Phase 1 item runs with the regime knobs listed (pinned values in parentheses); unlisted
  knobs are randomized per seed by the regime schedule owned by the cross-cutting subagent.
  `Knobs: none` is used only for elaboration-only items that run no program (TP-SEC-037,
  TP-RST-020).
- Layer-1 weights: an item whose Stimulus enumerates classes without percentages draws from the
  weight tables of the next section, named in its `Weights:` field; Phase 2 items draw from every
  table.
- Probe-gated (P1) bins (all of CG-DIT-004, CG-DIT-005.cp_pattern_changed,
  CG-RST-004.cp_dummy_adjacent / cr_rd_bank_dummy, CG-RST-002.cp_inflight.dummy_in_id /
  cr_inflight_len.dummy_in_id_short) are listed in the Bins lines and the trace CSV for feature
  traceability but are NOT must-hit manifest bins until the probe register carries P1
  (gen_tb_architecture.md 8.3 item 5; Critic pre-review S-14). Every fire-check below is
  boundary- or RVFI-based; P1 is named only as coverage-only confirmation.
- Timing statements use the fcov file's Q-TIME qualifier: a "gap" is measured from the previous
  retirement and is this instruction's own ID residency only when no fetch stall, no dummy, no
  CSR-write flush and no redirect precede it (fcov_sec_rst_rvfi_cheri.md header, S-4). Every
  cpuctrlsts write flushes the pipe and re-fetches the following instruction (csr_pipe_flush,
  rtl/ibex_id_stage.sv:593-597).
- Bug-candidate status follows dv/auto_dv/docs/gen_bug_log.md: B7 (TP-DIT-019), B8 (TP-DIT-032)
  and B13 (TP-RVFI-013) are expected-fail; B12 is documented behaviour with a design-weakness note
  (TP-SEC-025 passes); B14 is an RVFI convention note pending its confirmation run (TP-RVFI-018 is
  the pass item for the priority behaviour, TP-RVFI-039 the informational confirmation).

## Layer-1 weight tables
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Per-transaction distributions (DV_prompt Section 6 layer 1). Percentages are per draw; ranges are
uniform unless stated. Items reference a table by name in `Weights:`; per-item percentages in a
Stimulus line override the table for that item.

| Table | Operand class | Distribution |
|---|---|---|
| W-CSROP | CSR op form | csrrw 25, csrrs 20, csrrc 20, csrrwi 15, csrrsi 10, csrrci 10; the read-only forms (csrrs/csrrc rs1 == x0, csrrsi/csrrci uimm == 0) are 20 percent of the csrrs/csrrc/csrrsi/csrrci draws |
| W-BR | Conditional branch | opcode uniform over beq/bne/blt/bge/bltu/bgeu; c.beqz/c.bnez 30 percent of draws; taken 50 / not-taken 50; target forward 40 / backward 60; distance log-uniform 2..512 bytes |
| W-MD | RV32M | mul 25, mulh-class 25 (uniform over mulh/mulhsu/mulhu), div-class 50 (uniform over div/divu/rem/remu); each operand: zero 20, one 10, minus one 10, 0x80000000 10, random 50 |
| W-LS | Load / store | load 50 / store 50; size byte 30 / half 30 / word 40; byte offset uniform 0..3 (misaligned accesses follow from size x offset); lb/lh 50 / lbu/lhu 50; data zero 10 / all ones 10 / sign-bit patterns 20 / random 60 |
| W-INTG | Integrity injection | flipped check/data bits single 50 / double 30 / multi 20; side ibus 40 / dbus load 35 / dbus store 20 / spurious 5 |
| W-IRQ | Interrupt lines | software 15, timer 15, external 20, fast 50 (uniform over the $bits(irq_fast_i) lines); NMI mix per knob:irq_line_mix; assertion cycle uniform over the item's window |
| W-CAUSE | Synchronous exception cause | illegal 25, ecall 15, ebreak (dcsr.ebreakm/u = 0) 10, load fault 20, store fault 15, fetch fault 15; each access fault PMP 60 / bus error 40 |
| W-RST | Reset and fetch_enable_i | reset length 1 cycle 20 / 2..9 cycles 50 / 10..50 cycles 30; fetch_enable_i excursion Off 50 / invalid 50 with the 2**IbexMuBiWidth - 2 invalid encodings uniform; hold 1 cycle 20 / 2..49 cycles 50 / 50 or more 30 |
| W-BOOT | Boot inputs | boot_addr_i[31:8] class zero 10 / low 30 / mid 30 / high 30 (bits 7:0 always 0); hart_id_i zero 10 / 0xFFFFFFFF 10 / random 80 |
| W-CHERI | CHERIoT encodings | funct3 uniform; funct7 0x00 25 / 0x01 25 / 0x7f 25 / random 25; SCR address named (CSR_MSHWM / CSR_MSHWMB / CSR_CDBG_CTRL) 60 / other 0xBC0..0xBCF 40; privilege M 50 / U 50 |

## DIT: dummy instruction insertion and data-independent timing
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### TP-DIT-001: cpuctrlsts.data_ind_timing write, read-back and effect hand-over
- Features: F-DIT-001
- Phase: 1
- Tier: smoke
- Preconditions: M-mode; cpuctrlsts read once to capture the reset value (bits 5:0 = 0).
- Stimulus: program writes cpuctrlsts bit 1 with csrrw/csrrs/csrrc/csrrwi/csrrsi/csrrci (uniform
  over the six forms), each followed by csrr cpuctrlsts; 20-60 write/read pairs per run with the
  other cfg bits (icache_enable, dummy_instr_en, mask) randomized in the same write.
- Randomized: CSR op form, write value of bits 5:0 (all 64 values reachable), distance between
  write and read (0-8 unrelated instructions), instruction mix around the pair.
- Knobs: knob:instr_mix, knob:imem_gnt_delay, knob:imem_rvalid_delay
- Fire-check: at least one RVFI record of a cpuctrlsts write with bit 1 = 1 and one with bit 1 = 0
  (from rvfi_insn + rs1/uimm value), each followed by a csrr whose rvfi_rd_wdata is observed.
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_csr_readback (predicted cpuctrlsts value incl. WARL: bits 31:9 read 0,
  bit 8 = delayed ic_scr_key_valid_i, bits 7:6 as modelled) ; gen_isa_compare (csrr rd value).
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_sec_cpuctrlsts
- Bins: CG-DIT-001.cp_access.m_write, CG-DIT-001.cp_dit.off, CG-DIT-001.cp_dit.on,
  CG-DIT-001.cp_dit_toggle.off2on, CG-DIT-001.cp_dit_toggle.on2off,
  CG-DIT-001.cp_dit_toggle.hold_on, CG-DIT-001.cp_dit_toggle.hold_off

### TP-DIT-002: Conditional branches take identical time taken vs not-taken under DIT
- Features: F-DIT-002
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: cpuctrlsts.data_ind_timing = 1 set by the program; dummy_instr_en = 0 (Q-TIME);
  icache_enable randomized; instruction memory regime held constant within the measured window.
- Stimulus: branch-heavy straight-line blocks: pairs of the same branch opcode (beq/bne/blt/bge/
  bltu/bgeu) with operands chosen so one is taken and one not-taken, 40% forward/60% backward
  targets, target distance 2..512 bytes, both 32-bit and 16-bit forms, both with DIT on and (in a
  second window of the same run) DIT off.
- Randomized: opcode, operand values (taken/not-taken 50/50), target distance and direction,
  compressed vs 32-bit (c.beqz/c.bnez 30%), surrounding ALU filler, privilege mode (M 70 / U 30).
- Knobs: knob:instr_mix (branch_heavy), knob:imem_gnt_delay (same_cycle), knob:imem_rvalid_delay
  (min1), knob:priv_regime
- Fire-check: RVFI shows >= 50 taken and >= 50 not-taken conditional branches with DIT on (cfg
  tracked from retired cpuctrlsts writes) and the same with DIT off; taken/not-taken derived from
  rvfi_pc_wdata vs rvfi_pc_rdata + length.
- Pass criteria: gen_test_dit_branch (cocotb): for timing-qualified branches (Q-TIME) the gap since
  the previous record is this branch's own ID residency: under DIT on every branch, taken or not,
  shows gap 2 (MULTI_CYCLE, rtl/ibex_id_stage.sv:925-928) and under DIT off every branch shows gap
  1 (BranchTargetALU = 1: FIRST_CYCLE); the taken and not-taken gap distributions are identical
  within each DIT state ; gen_isa_compare (architectural result of every branch) ; gen_chk_counters
  (NumBranches; NumBranchesTaken under DIT is the PMC area's B11 item, referenced not re-checked
  here).
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_dit_timing
- Bins: CG-DIT-002.cp_taken.taken, CG-DIT-002.cp_taken.not_taken,
  CG-DIT-002.cr_dit_taken_c.on_taken_i32, CG-DIT-002.cr_dit_taken_c.on_nt_i32,
  CG-DIT-002.cr_dit_taken_c.off_taken_i32, CG-DIT-002.cr_dit_taken_c.off_nt_i32,
  CG-DIT-002.cr_dit_gap.on_taken_g2, CG-DIT-002.cr_dit_gap.on_nt_g2,
  CG-DIT-002.cr_dit_gap.off_nt_g1, CG-DIT-002.cr_dit_gap.off_taken_g1,
  CG-DIT-002.cp_compressed.c16, CG-DIT-002.cp_compressed.i32, CG-DIT-002.cp_gap.g1,
  CG-DIT-002.cp_gap.g2

### TP-DIT-003: Not-taken branch under DIT redirects fetch to the fall-through address
- Features: F-DIT-002
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: cpuctrlsts.data_ind_timing = 1; icache_enable = 0 so every fetch is visible on
  instr_req_o/instr_addr_o.
- Stimulus: not-taken 32-bit conditional branches placed at word-aligned and half-word-aligned
  PCs, followed by 4-8 sequential instructions; the imem agent records the request stream.
- Randomized: branch opcode/operands (forced not-taken), PC alignment, fall-through code length,
  imem grant delay.
- Knobs: knob:imem_gnt_delay, knob:imem_rvalid_delay, knob:instr_mix (branch_heavy)
- Fire-check: for >= 30 not-taken branches with DIT on, the ibus monitor sees a new instr_req_o
  for the word containing PC+4 issued after the branch's own fetch (a re-request that does not
  occur for the same branch with DIT off in the control window), and rvfi_pc_wdata == PC+4.
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_ibus_proto (request sequence legal, no request while the prefetch buffer
  is being flushed is duplicated) ; gen_isa_compare (pc_wdata / next pc) ; gen_chk_alerts
  (alert_major_internal_o stays 0: branch_req disarms the PC check).
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_dit_timing

  CG-DIT-002.cr_dit_taken_c.on_nt_i32

### TP-DIT-007: DIT written by the instruction immediately before a branch or divide
- Features: F-DIT-006
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: M-mode.
- Stimulus: csrw/csrrs/csrrc cpuctrlsts toggling bit 1 immediately followed (zero intervening
  instructions) by a conditional branch, a div-class or a mul-class instruction; also the
  reverse order (div then csrw) to show the CSR write waits for the div.
- Randomized: toggle direction, following instruction class (branch 40 / div 40 / mul 20),
  branch taken/not-taken, div rs2 zero or not.
- Knobs: knob:imem_gnt_delay (same_cycle), knob:imem_rvalid_delay (min1)
- Fire-check: >= 10 RVFI pairs (cpuctrlsts write, next record a branch or div) with the toggle
  in each direction, gap between them measured.
- Pass criteria: gen_test_dit_handover (cocotb): every cpuctrlsts write flushes the pipe and
  re-fetches the follower (csr_pipe_flush, rtl/ibex_id_stage.sv:593-597), so the follower's gap =
  re-fetch latency + its own ID residency; the re-fetch latency is measured from control pairs (a
  cpuctrlsts write that does not change bit 1, same imem regime) and subtracted: the follower shows
  the residency of the NEW DIT value (div by zero after off->on: 37 cycles instead of 2; not-taken
  branch after on->off: 1 cycle instead of 2, rtl/ibex_id_stage.sv:925-928) ; gen_isa_compare.
  Note: "toggle DIT while a div is in flight" is unreachable (single issue, the div occupies ID);
  the reverse-order pairs document this: the csrw retires only after the div's full latency.
- Expected: pass

### TP-DIT-027: secureseed write of zero and of a seed-cancelling value (LFSR lockup recovery)
- Features: F-DIT-025
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: dummy_instr_en = 1, mask 000; the TB keeps a model of the running seed
  (seed_q ^= wdata per write, reset 0). If the VCS build defines SIMULATION (unverified, Open
  question 8) the run passes +prim_lfsr_use_default_seed=1 so the lockup reload value is the
  DefaultSeed parameter.
- Stimulus: (a) csrw secureseed, x0 (wdata 0) then 1000 instructions; (b) csrw secureseed with
  wdata == modelled seed_q (XOR result 0 -> all-zero LFSR seed -> lockup -> DefaultSeedLocal
  reload on the next lfsr_en, vendor/lowrisc_ip/ip/prim/rtl/prim_lfsr.sv:345-346;
  DefaultSeedLocal is the DefaultSeed parameter unless the build defines SIMULATION, where it is
  randomised in about 70% of runs without +prim_lfsr_use_default_seed=1, :250-276) then 1000
  instructions; (c) random nonzero write as control.
- Randomized: order of (a)/(b)/(c), filler, prior seed history length.
- Knobs: knob:imem_gnt_delay (same_cycle), knob:imem_rvalid_delay (min1)
- Fire-check: RVFI shows the three write records with the intended wdata (rs1 value) and >= 10
  extra gaps in each following window (dummies continue; no hang: the window completes within a
  cycle budget).
- Pass criteria: gen_test_dit_seed (cocotb): insertion continues after (a) and (b) (no hang) and
  end-of-test is reached; the post-(b) insertion pattern is compared with the DefaultSeed
  prediction only when the reload value is deterministic (plusarg present or SIMULATION not
  defined) ; gen_isa_compare ; gen_chk_csr_readback.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_dit_secureseed
- Bins: CG-DIT-005.cr_wdata_effect.zero_write, CG-DIT-005.cr_wdata_effect.cancels_seed_write,
  CG-DIT-005.cp_wdata.zero, CG-DIT-005.cp_wdata.cancels_seed, CG-DIT-005.cp_wdata.nonzero

### TP-DIT-034: Interrupt arriving while a dummy DIV occupies ID (37-cycle window)
- Features: F-DIT-030
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: dummy_instr_en = 1, mask 000, data_ind_timing = 1 (every DIV takes the full
  37-cycle divider latency); mie set for timer/external/fast lines; mstatus.MIE = 1; handler
  records mepc and returns; a control window with dummies disabled measures the plain
  interrupt-entry latency.
- Stimulus: straight-line single-cycle ALU code (no program div/mul) with dummies at the highest
  rate; irq lines pulsed at random cycles so that some assertions land inside a dummy DIV; a
  debug_req_i variant (sparse) for the debug-entry wait.
- Randomized: irq line, assertion cycle, hold policy, seed (drives which dummies are DIVs),
  debug_req_i timing.
- Knobs: knob:irq_regime (sparse), knob:irq_line_mix (multi), knob:irq_hold (until_taken),
  knob:debug_req_regime (sparse), knob:imem_gnt_delay (same_cycle), knob:imem_rvalid_delay (min1)
- Fire-check: >= 5 handler entries (rvfi_intr = 1) whose gap from the last pre-interrupt record
  exceeds the plain entry latency by >= 30 cycles (only a dummy DIV can add that much in
  straight-line ALU code); P1 confirms fcov_dummy_instr_type == DIV with dummy_instr_id_o = 1 in
  the irq assertion cycle (coverage-only); >= 2 debug entries with the same signature.
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_irq (entry latency <= plain latency + 37 cycles; mepc read in the handler
  == rvfi_pc_rdata of the first post-handler record) ; gen_chk_rvfi_proto (no record between the
  last pre-irq record and the handler; rvfi_intr on the handler's first record only) ;
  gen_chk_debug (dpc == next real PC for the debug variant) ; gen_isa_compare.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_dit_dummy_events
- Bins: CG-DIT-004.cr_type_irq.div_irq_pending, CG-DIT-004.cr_type_irq.mul_irq_pending,
  CG-DIT-004.cr_type_irq.add_irq_pending, CG-DIT-004.cr_type_irq.and_irq_pending,
  CG-DIT-004.cr_type_irq.div_debug_req_high, CG-DIT-004.cp_irq_delay_by_dummy.div,
  CG-DIT-004.cp_irq_delay_by_dummy.single, CG-DIT-004.cp_irq_delay_by_dummy.none,
  CG-DIT-004.cp_context.irq_pending, CG-DIT-004.cr_type_dit.div_on, CG-RVFI-001.cp_intr.yes

## SEC: security features and alerts at the ibex_core boundary
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### TP-SEC-001: alert_minor_o pulses exactly once per injected ICache ECC error
- Features: F-SEC-001
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: cpuctrlsts.icache_enable = 1; scramble key valid; a loop body that is re-executed
  so lines are hit from the cache.
- Stimulus: the tag/data RAM models flip 1 or 2 bits of a stored word (tag or data, random way)
  before a lookup that will hit it; 5-40 injections per run spaced >= 20 cycles.
- Randomized: tag vs data RAM, way, bit positions (single/double), injection timing relative to
  the lookup, loop size (fits in cache).
- Knobs: knob:icache_ecc_err_rate (rare), knob:imem_gnt_delay, knob:imem_rvalid_delay
- Fire-check: >= 5 injection events each followed within a bounded window by an alert_minor_o
  pulse (TB injection log correlated with the alert monitor).
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_alerts (exactly one 1-cycle alert_minor_o pulse per injected error; no
  pulse otherwise) ; gen_chk_icache (line invalidated and refilled from the bus after the alert) ;
  gen_isa_compare (program result unaffected).
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_sec_alert_inject_icache
- Bins: CG-SEC-001.cr_alert_inject.minor_icache_ecc, CG-SEC-001.cp_minor_count_per_inject.one,
  CG-SEC-001.cp_pulse_width.one_cycle, CG-SEC-001.cr_alert_phase.minor_running,
  CG-SEC-001.cp_event.alert_minor, CG-SEC-001.cp_alert.minor, CG-SEC-001.cp_phase.running,
  CG-SEC-001.cp_event.inject

### TP-SEC-002: alert_minor_o never pulses without an injected ICache ECC error
- Features: F-SEC-001, F-SEC-034
- Phase: 1
- Tier: smoke
- Preconditions: icache_enable toggled between windows; scramble key handshake exercised
  (fence.i).
- Stimulus: long random program (>= 50k instructions) with cache on and off, fence.i, bus errors
  on the instruction side (instr_err_i), integrity errors on both sides; no ECC injection.

  knob:scr_key_delay, knob:instr_mix
- Fire-check: >= 50k RVFI records, >= 1000 boundary-derived icache hits with icache_enable = 1 (the
  lookups that could raise a false minor alert; qualifier of CG-SEC-001.cp_minor_quiet_run) and >=
  10 instruction-side error responses observed; end-of-test reached.
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_alerts (alert_minor_o total == 0).
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_sec_alerts_neg
- Bins: CG-SEC-001.cp_minor_quiet_run.zero, CG-SEC-001.cp_event.eot

### TP-SEC-007: Instruction-side integrity error: alert_major_bus_o plus fetch fault, no NMI
- Features: F-SEC-003, F-SEC-018
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: icache_enable randomized (both), mtvec handler logs mcause/mtval and skips the
  faulting instruction.
- Stimulus: the imem agent corrupts the check bits of a returned instruction beat that WILL be
  executed (address of the next sequential instruction), 5-30 times per run.
- Randomized: single/double/multi-bit corruption, target instruction size and alignment, cache
  state (hit path excluded since the ECC-covered RAM path is a different feature), imem delays.
- Knobs: knob:imem_err_rate (rare), knob:imem_gnt_delay, knob:imem_rvalid_delay, knob:irq_regime
  (quiet)
- Fire-check: >= 5 corrupted beats whose PC is later retired as an rvfi_trap record with mcause =
  instruction access fault (1); alert_major_bus_o pulse in the beat's rvalid cycle.
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_bus_intg_rsp (one alert pulse per corrupted beat, aligned to
  instr_rvalid_i) ; gen_chk_nmi / gen_chk_irq (NO internal NMI: no record with rvfi_ext_nmi_int,
  mcause never the internal-NMI encoding {irq_ext 1, irq_int 1, lower_cause 0} = 0xFFFFFFE0 in the run) ; gen_isa_compare (fetch fault trap, mtval = 0 per Ibex,
  handler flow) ; gen_chk_alerts.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_sec_alert_inject_ibus
- Bins: CG-SEC-002.cr_side_op.ibus_na, CG-SEC-002.cr_ibus_consumed.ibus_executed_yes,
  CG-SEC-002.cr_errbits_side.single_ibus, CG-SEC-002.cr_errbits_side.double_ibus,

### TP-SEC-008: Data-side load integrity error: alert, internal NMI and RF write suppression
- Features: F-SEC-003, F-SEC-015
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: mtvec handler at base+0x7C logs mcause/mtval/mepc and mrets; mstatus.MIE random
  (NMI is unmaskable).
- Stimulus: the dmem agent corrupts the check bits of load responses (word/half/byte, aligned and
  misaligned first/second half), 5-30 per run; loads target registers holding known values so
  suppression is visible.
- Randomized: load size/offset/sign, rd, corruption class, dmem delays, MIE, privilege mode.
- Knobs: knob:dmem_err_rate (rare), knob:dmem_gnt_delay, knob:dmem_rvalid_delay,
  knob:priv_regime
- Fire-check: >= 5 corrupted load responses each followed by (a) alert_major_bus_o pulse in the
  rvalid cycle, (b) the load's RVFI record with rvfi_ext_rf_wr_suppress = 1, (c) a handler entry
  record with rvfi_intr = 1 and rvfi_ext_nmi_int = 1 within one instruction.
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_bus_intg_rsp (alert, suppression, NMI mcause = the internal-NMI encoding 0xFFFFFFE0 {irq_ext 1, irq_int 1}, mtval = faulting
  address, vector base+0x7C, taken at most one instruction later) ; gen_chk_nmi (mstack save/
  restore across the handler's mret) ; gen_isa_compare with the rd value legalised to "unchanged"
  (rvfi_rd_addr = 0 on the suppressed load, rd keeps its old value) ; gen_chk_alerts.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_sec_alert_inject_dbus
- Bins: CG-SEC-002.cr_side_op.dbus_load, CG-SEC-002.cr_load_half.load_aligned_yes,
  CG-SEC-002.cr_load_half.load_first_yes, CG-SEC-002.cr_load_half.load_second_yes,
  CG-SEC-002.cp_nmi_taken.yes, CG-SEC-002.cp_nmi_latency.same_insn, CG-SEC-002.cp_nmi_latency.next_insn,
  CG-SEC-002.cp_load_size.byte, CG-SEC-002.cp_load_size.half, CG-SEC-002.cp_load_size.word,
  CG-SEC-002.cr_errbits_side.single_dbus, CG-SEC-002.cr_errbits_side.double_dbus,
  CG-SEC-002.cr_errbits_side.multi_dbus, CG-SEC-001.cr_alert_inject.major_bus_dbus_load_intg,
  CG-RVFI-003.cp_rf_wr_suppress.yes, CG-RVFI-003.cr_irq_kind.yes_no_yes,
  CG-SEC-002.cp_side.dbus, CG-SEC-002.cp_dbus_op.load, CG-SEC-002.cp_half.aligned,
  CG-SEC-002.cp_half.first, CG-SEC-002.cp_half.second, CG-SEC-002.cp_ibus_consumed.na

### TP-SEC-012: Integrity error on a speculatively fetched, never-executed word

### TP-SEC-013: Register-file ECC alert is unreachable with RegFileECC=0 (negative)
- Features: F-SEC-004, F-SEC-005, F-SEC-006
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: wrapper parameter RegFileECC = 0 confirmed by the config banner.
- Stimulus: register-intensive program that reads every register through both ports, including
  same-cycle WB forwarding cases (rs == rd of the previous instruction) and encodings whose rs2
  field is an immediate (I-type) so "addressed but not read" registers occur; dummies enabled in
  half the run.

- Knobs: knob:instr_mix (mixed), knob:imem_gnt_delay, knob:imem_rvalid_delay
- Fire-check: >= 31 distinct rs1 addresses and >= 31 distinct rs2 addresses read (RVFI), >= 50
  forwarding cases (rs addr == previous rd addr, consecutive records) and >= 1000 records retired
  with dummies enabled.

  decoder) ; gen_isa_compare. The former fault injection (force one bit of a wrapper-internal RF
  flop and observe the data mismatch) is mutation evidence for gen_isa_compare, not a pass-gate
  step (Critic pre-review S-13): named mutation "rf_bit_flip" in the mutation build, recorded next
  to TP-SEC-004's evidence, never in a regression run.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_sec_alerts_neg
- Bins: CG-SEC-001.cp_internal_total.zero, CG-RST-004.cr_fwd_bank.yes_x1_15,
  CG-RST-004.cr_fwd_bank.yes_x16, CG-RST-004.cr_fwd_bank.yes_x17_31

### TP-SEC-021: Double fault: second synchronous exception before mret pulses double_fault_seen_o
- Features: F-SEC-022
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: mtvec handler that, on selected entries, deliberately raises a second exception
  (illegal instruction, ecall, misaligned-PMP load, store to a PMP-denied region, ebreak with
  ebreakm = 0, fetch from a PMP-denied page) before its mret; recovery path via a nested handler
  that clears cpuctrlsts bits 6/7 and returns.

  the second fault.

  double_fault_seen_o pulse in the cycle of the second trap's FLUSH and a csrr cpuctrlsts record
  showing bit 7 = 1 and bit 6 = 1.
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_double_fault (pulse exactly one cycle, once per pair; sticky bit 7 until
  software clears it; bit 6 set after the first trap) ; gen_isa_compare ; gen_chk_csr_readback.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_sec_double_fault
- Bins: CG-SEC-003.cr_event_seen.sync_exc_clear_no, CG-SEC-003.cr_event_seen.sync_exc_set_no,

### TP-SEC-024: Interrupt or NMI entry between two synchronous exceptions neither sets nor clears the flag
- Features: F-SEC-024
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: exception handler that enables interrupts (mstatus.MIE = 1) before its mret so an
  interrupt or NMI pre-empts it; the interrupt handler raises a second synchronous exception
  (illegal) in 50% of entries and otherwise mrets.
- Stimulus: sync exception, then irq / irq_nm_i asserted while in the exception handler.
- Randomized: irq vs NMI, timing, second exception cause, which handler raises it.
- Knobs: knob:irq_regime (sparse), knob:irq_line_mix (with_nmi), knob:irq_hold (until_taken)
- Fire-check: >= 5 sequences trap -> handler entry (rvfi_intr = 1, irq) -> trap with no mret
  between the first trap and the second, and >= 5 with NMI (rvfi_ext_nmi = 1) instead of irq.
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_double_fault (irq/NMI entry leaves bit 6 set: the second exception inside
  the interrupt handler pulses double_fault_seen_o) ; gen_chk_irq ; gen_chk_nmi.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_sec_double_fault
- Bins: CG-SEC-003.cr_event_seen.irq_entry_set_no, CG-SEC-003.cr_event_seen.nmi_entry_set_no,
  CG-SEC-003.cp_event.irq_entry, CG-SEC-003.cp_event.nmi_entry

### TP-SEC-025: mret from an interrupt or NMI handler clears sync_exc_seen (B12 documented behaviour; design-weakness note)
- Features: F-SEC-024
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: as TP-SEC-024 but the interrupt/NMI handler mrets back into the still-active
  exception handler, which then raises a second synchronous exception before its own mret.
- Stimulus: trap -> exception handler enables MIE -> irq/NMI -> interrupt handler mret -> second
  synchronous exception in the exception handler.
- Randomized: irq vs NMI, causes, timing.
- Knobs: knob:irq_regime (sparse), knob:irq_line_mix (with_nmi)
- Fire-check: >= 5 sequences trap -> irq entry -> mret (from the irq handler, rvfi_insn mret with
  the model in irq context) -> trap, with no exception-handler mret in between; for >= 2 of them
  the pre-empting entry is an NMI.
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_double_fault following the documented behaviour
  (exception_interrupts.rst:191 and cs_registers.rst:556: sync_exc_seen is cleared by ANY retired
  mret, including the interrupt handler's, rtl/ibex_cs_registers.sv:964-965): after the irq/NMI
  handler's mret the model clears bit 6, so the second synchronous exception in the still-active
  exception handler does NOT pulse double_fault_seen_o, and csrr cpuctrlsts in the exception
  handler after the return shows bit 6 = 0 ; gen_chk_csr_readback ; gen_chk_irq / gen_chk_nmi.
  Design-weakness note for the security owner (bug log B12, Critic pre-review S-1): an interrupt
  taken inside a synchronous-exception handler disarms double-fault detection for the rest of that
  handler; no RISC-V specification covers the detector, so this is documented behaviour, not a bug
  candidate; the item records the sequence as evidence for the owner ruling (Q-DL-3).
- Expected: pass (B12 documented behaviour; design-weakness note)
- Test group: gen_sec_double_fault
- Bins: CG-SEC-003.cr_mret_ctx.mret_irq_handler, CG-SEC-003.cr_mret_ctx.mret_nmi_handler,
  CG-SEC-003.cp_mret_context.irq_handler, CG-SEC-003.cp_mret_context.nmi_handler

### TP-SEC-026: Software-written sync_exc_seen and double_fault_seen
- Features: F-SEC-025
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: M-mode; a handler that clears bit 7 on request.
- Stimulus: (a) csrs cpuctrlsts bit 6 then a single synchronous exception (expect a pulse); (b)
  csrc bit 7 after a real double fault (expect read-back 0); (c) csrs bit 7 with no exception
  (expect read-back 1 and no pulse); (d) csrc bit 6 inside an exception handler followed by a

- Fire-check: RVFI records of the four write kinds (from rvfi_insn and operand value) each
  followed by the related trap or csrr record.
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_double_fault (pulse only in (a) and never in (c)/(d); bit 7 read-back
  per the model) ; gen_chk_csr_readback.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_sec_double_fault
- Bins: CG-SEC-003.cr_event_seen.sw_set_b6_clear_no, CG-SEC-003.cr_event_seen.sw_clr_b7_set_no,

  CG-SEC-003.cp_event.sw_set_b6, CG-SEC-003.cp_event.sw_clr_b7

### TP-SEC-027: cpuctrlsts write coinciding with a load/store exception in WB
- Features: F-SEC-026
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: a load or store that will fault (PMP-denied or data_err_i) immediately followed
  by csrw cpuctrlsts (bits 6/7 random) so the CSR write is in ID when the WB fault is signalled.
- Stimulus: 200 such pairs with the fault arriving after 1..6 cycles of dmem latency.

  write that was NOT retired before the trap (it appears after the handler), plus a csrr
  cpuctrlsts in the handler.
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_double_fault (bit 6 set by the exception regardless of the pending CSR
  write; bit 7 unaffected) ; gen_chk_csr_readback ; gen_isa_compare. If no run shows the CSR write
  committed in the same cycle as the WB exception (expected: wb_exception_o blocks ID), the item
  documents unreachability and its bin is ignored with reason (see Open questions).
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_sec_double_fault
- Bins: CG-SEC-003.cp_sync_exc_cause.load_fault, CG-SEC-003.cp_sync_exc_cause.store_fault,

### TP-SEC-033: cpuctrlsts layout: WARL fields, reserved bits, read-only bit 8, software-writable bits 6/7
- Features: F-SEC-031, F-SEC-032

  set in >= 50%), each followed by csrr; read-modify-write sequences (csrrs / csrrc / csrrw
  touching bits 6/7) after a real exception set bit 6, including csrrc clearing bit 6 and csrrs
  setting bit 7.

  write; bits 5:0 as written; bits 7:6 per the double-fault model with software writes APPLIED as written: both bits are RW,
  rtl/ibex_cs_registers.sv:874-876,1967-1968, cs_registers.rst:551-557, so a csrrs/csrrc does NOT
  preserve them; Critic C-05 correction of the v1 expectation) ; gen_isa_compare.
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_sec_cpuctrlsts

- Features: F-RST-002
- Phase: 1
- Tier: smoke

### TP-RST-007: Other CSR reset values relevant to boot
- Features: F-RST-007
- Phase: 1
- Tier: smoke
- Preconditions: none.
- Stimulus: read mcause, mepc, mie, mtval, mscratch, dcsr (from debug mode via debug_req at reset,
  TP-RST-024), dpc, dscratch0/1, cpuctrlsts, mcountinhibit, mcounteren, mseccfg, pmpcfg0..3,
  pmpaddr0..15, tselect, tdata1 before any write.
- Randomized: read order, op form, ic_scr_key_valid_i state (cpuctrlsts bit 8).
- Knobs: knob:scr_key_delay
- Fire-check: RVFI records for every listed CSR read with rd values before any write to it.
- Pass criteria: gen_isa_compare with the shim's reset values (mcause 0, mepc 0, mie 0, mtval 0,
  mscratch 0, dscratch0/1 0, cpuctrlsts bit 8 only, mcountinhibit 0, mcounteren 0, PMP per ibex_pkg
  PMPRstCfg/PMPRstAddr/PMPRstMsecCfg, tselect 0, tdata1 0x28001048 (D4)) ; gen_chk_csr_readback.
  dcsr and dpc are read inside the debug ROM after the reset-time debug_req entry (TP-RST-024), and
  the entry itself writes them (rtl/ibex_cs_registers.sv:910-917: dcsr.prv = the interrupted
  privilege, dcsr.cause = the debug cause, depc = the interrupted PC), so the expected dcsr is
  {xdebugver XDEBUGVER_STD (4), cause DBG_CAUSE_HALTREQ (3), prv PRIV_LVL_M, every other field 0:
  ebreakm/ebreaku 0, step 0, stopcount/stoptime 0, mprven 0} with bit 13 (ebreaks) predicted 0 (B15
  rule, owner items TP-CSR-076 / TP-DBG-018) and bit 3 (nmip) excluded from the compare (B5, owner
  item TP-DBG-021), and the expected dpc is the boot vector {boot_addr_i[31:8], 8'h80}; the true
  reset values of dcsr.cause/prv and dpc are not observable because every path into debug mode
  overwrites them.
- Expected: pass (doc mismatch D4)
- Test group: gen_rst_boot
- Bins: CG-SEC-005.cp_bit8_readback.zero, CG-SEC-005.cp_bit8_readback.one,
  CG-SEC-005.cp_bits67_readback.b6_0_b7_0

### TP-RST-009: fetch_enable_i Off mid-run: in-flight instructions complete, then no retirements or requests
- Features: F-RST-010

### TP-RST-015: core_busy_o Off exactly when asleep after WFI with nothing pending
- Features: F-RST-016
- Phase: 1

- Features: F-RST-018, F-RST-001
- Phase: 1

  outstanding (monitors), >= 2 with a late response returned after release.
- Pass criteria: cocotb gen_test_rst_values (all outputs at reset values within the assert cycle
  and until the boot request) ; gen_chk_alerts (bad-integrity late response -> alert_major_bus_o
  only; valid late response -> nothing) ; gen_isa_compare restarted at the boot vector (no RF
  write, no trap from the late response) ; gen_chk_rvfi_proto (rvfi_order restarts at 1).
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_rst_midrun_reset

### TP-RST-018: Reset during a multi-cycle instruction or a split misaligned access
- Features: F-RST-019
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: as TP-RST-017.
- Stimulus: rst_ni asserted (a) during a 37-cycle division, (b) between the two halves of a
  misaligned store/load (first half granted, second not yet requested or not yet responded), (c)
  in the middle of a Zcmp expansion, (d) while a dummy instruction is in ID (P1).
- Randomized: which case, exact cycle, reset length.
- Knobs: knob:dmem_gnt_delay (long), knob:dmem_rvalid_delay (long), knob:instr_mix
- Fire-check: >= 3 resets in each of (a)-(c) identified from RVFI/dbus state (division record not
  retired; misaligned first half seen on the bus without the second; expanded_insn_valid without
  last).
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_dbus_proto (no second-half request after release) ; gen_chk_rvfi_proto
  (no record for the abandoned instruction; order restarts) ; gen_isa_compare (memory model shows
  the first-half write only, as an accepted RTL detail).
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_rst_midrun_reset
- Bins: CG-RST-002.cr_inflight_len.div_in_flight_one_cycle, CG-RST-002.cr_inflight_len.zcmp_mid_short,
  CG-RST-002.cr_inflight_resp.misaligned_first_done_none, CG-RST-002.cr_inflight_len.dummy_in_id_short,

- Features: F-RST-018, F-RST-001

### TP-RVFI-002: rvfi_valid is a one-cycle pulse per instruction, one cycle after WB completion
- Features: F-RVFI-002

### TP-RVFI-006: rvfi_intr marks only the first instruction of interrupt/NMI handlers (RTL-defined)
- Features: F-RVFI-006
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: interrupts enabled; exception handlers and debug ROM in place.
- Stimulus: interrupts (all line classes), external NMI, internal NMI (integrity error),
  synchronous exceptions, debug entries, mret/dret/fence.i redirects.
- Randomized: per knobs.
- Weights: W-IRQ, W-CAUSE
- Knobs: knob:irq_regime (sparse), knob:irq_line_mix (with_nmi), knob:debug_req_regime (sparse),
  knob:dmem_err_rate (rare), knob:pmp_regime
- Fire-check: >= 20 records with rvfi_intr = 1 following irq entries, >= 3 following NMIs, and >=
  20 exception-handler first records, >= 5 debug-entry first records, each with rvfi_intr = 0.
- Pass criteria: gen_chk_rvfi_proto in the RTL-defined direction: rvfi_intr = 1 iff the record is
  the first after an interrupt/NMI entry (rvfi_ext_irq_valid seen since the previous record);

### TP-RVFI-017: Fault on the second half of a misaligned access: one record, first-half address
- Features: F-RVFI-014
- Phase: 1

### TP-RVFI-018: ID-stage exception coinciding with a WB load/store fault: the WB error wins, the ID instruction is killed and re-executed
- Features: F-RVFI-015
- Phase: 1
- Tier: targeted
- Preconditions: a load/store that will fault in WB (data_err_i with 1..4 cycles of latency, or a
  PMP fault on the second half of a misaligned access) immediately followed by an instruction that
  raises an ID exception (illegal instruction, ecall, ebreak with dcsr.ebreakm/u = 0, U-mode CSR
  violation); the handler logs mcause/mepc and returns to mepc, so the killed instruction
  re-executes and traps again.
- Stimulus: 200+ such pairs with latencies swept so the ID exception request coincides with the WB
  exception (the TB timing model of the two instructions decides which pairs coincide).
- Randomized: ID cause, latency, load vs store, privilege.
- Weights: W-CAUSE, W-LS
- Knobs: knob:dmem_rvalid_delay (short), knob:dmem_err_rate (frequent), knob:pmp_regime (sparse)
- Fire-check: >= 5 coincident pairs (TB model) where the WB fault's trap record (mcause
  ExcCauseLoadAccessFault / ExcCauseStoreAccessFault, mepc read in the handler = the load/store PC)
  is followed directly by the handler's first record, and after the handler's mret the ID
  instruction re-executes and produces its own record (rvfi_pc_rdata = the ID instruction's PC,
  rvfi_trap = 1, mcause = its own cause).
- Pass criteria: gen_isa_compare (priority: the WB fault is taken first, mepc = the load/store PC,
  the ID instruction has no architectural effect before the handler and executes after mret; order
  continuity) ; gen_chk_rvfi_proto (no record for the killed ID instruction between the WB trap
  record and the handler's first record). The RVFI-record confirmation (two trap records in order,
  B14 convention note) is TP-RVFI-039 (informational).
- Expected: pass
- Test group: gen_rvfi_trap
- Bins: CG-RVFI-004.cr_wb_coincident.wb_yes_no, CG-RVFI-004.cr_wb_coincident.wb_no_no,
  CG-RVFI-004.cr_wb_coincident.id_no_no, CG-RVFI-004.cp_coincident_wb_err.yes,
  CG-RVFI-004.cp_coincident_wb_err.no, CG-RVFI-004.cp_missing_record.no

- Features: F-RVFI-015

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## New checkers requested
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

- gen_chk_rvfi_proto (NEW, requested): RVFI self-consistency checker, independent of the ISA
  model. Rules: rvfi_order increments by exactly 1 (64-bit) and restarts at 1 after reset;
  rvfi_valid is a one-cycle pulse per order value; pc_rdata[n+1] == pc_wdata[n] unless rvfi_intr
  on n+1, a trap record at n, a debug entry between them, or a FLUSH-redirect record (mret, dret,
  fence.i, trap) at n (Q-DL default 6: pc_wdata of those records is logged, not compared);
  rd_wdata == 0 when rd_addr == 0; rd_addr == 0 on trap records; rs*_rdata == 0 when rs*_addr ==
  0; rs3_addr == 0 on single-cycle instructions; exactly one of rmask/wmask nonzero on a non-trap
  load/store record and both 0 on trap records; mask values only {0001, 0011, 1111} at bit 0;
  insn[31:16] == 0 when insn[1:0] != 11; rvfi_halt == 0; rvfi_ixl == 1; rvfi_mode in {0, 3};
  rvfi_intr == 1 iff the record is the first after an interrupt/NMI entry (RTL-defined meaning);
  no record carries the dummy encoding class at a PC outside the program image (dummies never on
  RVFI); expanded_insn_last exactly once per Zcmp sequence with the same pc_rdata on every
  micro-op; exactly one rd write per record, from the source implied by the instruction class
  (ALU / CSR / mul-div -> WB flop, load -> LSU return, stores / branches / traps none;
  F-RVFI-034); no instruction in program order is missing from the trace (B14 detector, needs the
  program image and the model's order). Disable knob +gen_chk_rvfi_proto_en=0. Mutation classes:
  RVFI pipeline plumbing, order/valid gating, dummy gating, mask derivation.
- gen_test_dit_* (cocotb test-level fire-checks): gen_test_dit_branch, gen_test_dit_div,
  gen_test_dit_mul, gen_test_dit_handover, gen_test_dit_lsu, gen_test_dit_dummy,
  gen_test_dit_dummy_div, gen_test_dit_seed - gap-histogram assertions named in the items; these
  are test-level Python assertions, not new SV checkers.
- gen_test_rst_values / gen_test_rst_boot (cocotb): reset-value and boot-timing assertions.
- gen_chk_alerts extension: per-injection accounting (exactly one alert_minor_o pulse per
  injected ICache ECC error; alert_major_bus_o pulse count == corrupted rvalid beat count) and
  the in-reset rule (bus alert may follow corrupted beats during reset; the other two never).
- gen_chk_debug extension: "RTL-documenting" mode for the step-consumes-a-dummy case (accept a
  step re-entry with unchanged dpc only when P1 shows a dummy) and for trap/debug entry while
  fetch is disabled (Q-DL-8).
- gen_chk_crash_dump: the RVFI-derived model must include the WritebackStage offset (current_pc
  is the ID PC, one instruction ahead of the retiring record) and the misaligned rule for
  last_data_addr (word-aligned second-half address).
